seg.4643e12d303d.back: Stirring, pour the rava in a thin stream so lumps do not form.

seg.3c98bb62770b.src: Roasting the rava first keeps each grain separate; skip it and the upma turns sticky.
seg.3c98bb62770b.t: ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ ᱨᱟᱣᱟ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱱᱟ; ᱵᱟᱝ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ ᱞᱟᱴᱟᱣᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.3c98bb62770b.back: If the rava is fried first, every grain stays separate; if not fried, the upma becomes sticky.

seg.fc5bc0e0bf4e.src: Fry the cashews on medium-low heat and lift them out as soon as they turn golden; they keep darkening in the hot ghee.
seg.fc5bc0e0bf4e.t: ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ-ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱢᱮ; ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮᱭᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.fc5bc0e0bf4e.back: Fry the cashews on medium-low fire and take out as soon as they become gold colour; in the hot ghee they become even darker.

seg.975560a8a158.src: Upma firms up as it stands, so take it off the heat when it is a little softer than you want.
seg.975560a8a158.t: ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡᱚᱜᱼᱟ, ᱚᱱᱟᱛᱮ ᱟᱢ ᱠᱩᱥᱤᱭᱟᱜ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱜᱮ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱟᱲᱟᱜ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.975560a8a158.back: If kept, upma thickens, so take it off the fire while it is still a little softer than you like.

seg.508f0ab3992d.src: Vegetable upma: add ½ cup chopped carrot, beans and green peas with the onion and cook them for 3–4 minutes before the water goes in.
seg.508f0ab3992d.t: ᱩᱛᱩ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ: ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ ᱥᱟᱶ ½ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱜᱟᱡᱚᱨ, ᱵᱤᱱᱥ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱚᱴᱚᱨ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ 3–4 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.508f0ab3992d.back: Vegetable upma: with the onion add ½ cup cut carrot, beans and green peas and cook 3–4 minutes before adding water.

seg.1742d7bd0e23.src: Tomato upma: add 1 chopped tomato after the onion and cook till soft before adding the water.
seg.1742d7bd0e23.t: ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ: ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ 1 ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.1742d7bd0e23.back: Tomato upma: after the onion add 1 cut tomato and cook until soft before adding water.

seg.1981c7f3fc60.src: Godhuma rava upma: use the same amount of wheat rava with 3 cups water and cook it covered for 5–6 minutes.
seg.1981c7f3fc60.t: ᱜᱳᱫᱷᱩᱢᱟ ᱨᱟᱣᱟ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ: ᱚᱛᱠᱮ ᱜᱮ ᱜᱳᱦᱚᱢ ᱨᱟᱣᱟ 3 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱦᱟᱛᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ 5–6 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.1981c7f3fc60.back: Godhuma rava upma: take the same amount of wheat rava with 3 cups of water and cook covered 5–6 minutes.

seg.01300d94ad36.src: Serve hot as a breakfast tiffin with coconut chutney, allam pachadi or a spoon of sugar, or next to pesarattu for pesarattu upma.
seg.01300d94ad36.t: ᱥᱟᱹᱠᱟᱹᱞ ᱴᱤᱯᱷᱤᱱ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱱᱟᱨᱤᱭᱟᱞ ᱪᱟᱴᱱᱤ, ᱟᱞᱞᱟᱢ ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ ᱥᱮ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱪᱤᱱᱤ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱮ ᱯᱮᱥᱟᱨᱟᱴᱴᱩ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱯᱮᱥᱟᱨᱟᱴᱴᱩ ᱥᱟᱶ᱾
seg.01300d94ad36.back: As a morning tiffin serve hot with coconut chutney, allam pachadi or a spoon of sugar, or for pesarattu upma with pesarattu.

seg.3316a3d82f44.src: Upma is best eaten hot, soon after it is made. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 1 day and sprinkle with water before reheating.
seg.3316a3d82f44.t: ᱩᱯᱢᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱞᱚᱜᱚᱱ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱡᱟᱹᱥᱛᱤ ᱵᱮᱥ᱾ ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ 1 ᱢᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱩᱦᱲᱟᱹ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱪᱤᱴᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.3316a3d82f44.back: Upma is best eaten hot quickly after making. Keep the leftover covered in the fridge up to 1 day and before reheating sprinkle water.

seg.b53646711bf0.src: How do I make upma without lumps?
seg.b53646711bf0.t: ᱫᱤᱞᱟ ᱵᱤᱱ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ ᱪᱮᱫ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ?
seg.b53646711bf0.back: How can upma be made without lumps?

seg.429b54b4ab3a.src: Keep the water at a boil, turn the heat to low and pour in the rava in a thin stream with one hand while you stir with the other.
seg.429b54b4ab3a.t: ᱫᱟᱜ ᱚᱥᱚᱝ ᱜᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱛᱤ ᱛᱮ ᱨᱟᱣᱟ ᱯᱚᱛᱞᱟ ᱫᱷᱟᱨ ᱛᱮ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱮᱴᱟᱜ ᱛᱤ ᱛᱮ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.429b54b4ab3a.back: Keep the water just boiling, lower the fire and pour the rava in a thin stream with one hand and stir with the other hand.

seg.0c2874233201.src: What is the right rava to water ratio for upma?
seg.0c2874233201.t: ᱩᱯᱢᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱨᱟᱣᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱴᱷᱤᱠ ᱦᱤᱥᱟᱹᱵ ᱪᱮᱫ?
seg.0c2874233201.back: What is the right measure of rava and water for upma?

seg.91a8fe1a38a5.src: For a soft Andhra-style upma, use 2½ cups water to 1 cup bombay rava. Use 2 cups for a firmer, more separate upma.
seg.91a8fe1a38a5.t: ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 1 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱵᱚᱢᱵᱮ ᱨᱟᱣᱟ ᱨᱮ 2½ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ, ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 2 ᱠᱟᱯ᱾
seg.91a8fe1a38a5.back: For a soft Andhra-style upma add 2½ cups of water to 1 cup Bombay rava. For a thick, more separate-grain upma 2 cups.

seg.bd11a83d27d8.src: The rava was not roasted, or too much water went in. Roast the rava till it smells toasty, and stay close to 2½ cups water per cup.
seg.bd11a83d27d8.t: ᱨᱟᱣᱟ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱠᱟᱱᱟ, ᱥᱮ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱵᱟᱹᱲᱛᱤ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱠᱟᱱᱟ᱾ ᱨᱟᱣᱟ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱥᱩᱜᱚᱫ ᱦᱤᱡᱩᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱟᱨ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 2½ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.bd11a83d27d8.back: The rava may not have been fried, or very much water may have been added. Fry the rava until smell comes, and for every cup keep about 2½ cups of water.

seg.247181e411d9.src: When should I add cashews to upma?
seg.247181e411d9.t: ᱩᱯᱢᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱛᱤᱥ ᱮᱢ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ?
seg.247181e411d9.back: When must cashews be added in upma?

seg.83f262d9c56e.src: Fry them in the ghee first and lift them out, then stir them in at the end. Added early, they turn soft in the upma.
seg.83f262d9c56e.t: ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱢᱩᱪᱟᱹᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱞᱚᱜᱚᱱ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.83f262d9c56e.back: First fry in ghee and take out, then mix at the end. If added quickly they become soft in the upma.

seg.6cb14eaca16a.t: ᱡᱤᱰᱤᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ · ᱡᱤᱰᱤᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ | 1acrefarms

seg.8b57b24af158.src: జీడిపప్పు ఉప్మా. Andhra rava upma with Jeedipappu cashews fried golden in ghee, a soft and quick morning tiffin. Step-by-step method, tips and FAQs. Serves 3.
seg.8b57b24af158.t: ᱡᱤᱰᱤᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ᱾ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱡᱤᱰᱤᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱨᱟᱣᱟ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ, ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱚᱜᱚᱱ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱥᱟᱹᱠᱟᱹᱞ ᱴᱤᱯᱷᱤᱱ᱾ ᱫᱷᱟᱯ ᱫᱷᱟᱯ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ, ᱠᱟᱹᱢᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱛᱷᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱩᱠᱞᱤ᱾ 3 ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ᱾
seg.8b57b24af158.back: Jidipappu Upma. Andhra rava upma with Jidipappu cashews fried gold in ghee, a soft and quickly-made morning tiffin. Step-by-step recipe, tips and questions. For 3 people.

seg.661f01591624.src: Jeedipappu Upma: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.661f01591624.t: ᱡᱤᱰᱤᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ: 1acrefarms ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱠᱟᱨᱰ, ᱡᱤᱱᱤᱥ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ
seg.661f01591624.back: Jidipappu Upma: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and steps

seg.c944ba9a331c.t: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · ᱠᱳᱰᱤ ᱣᱮᱯᱩᱰᱩ · ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ
seg.c944ba9a331c.back: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · Kodi Vepudu · Andhra chicken meat fry

seg.992a8475993f.src: Kodi vepudu is the dry Andhra chicken fry: small pieces of chicken cooked in their own juices, then fried hard in oil with curry leaves, green chillies and a just-roasted masala until dark and sticky with spice. It is the starter at Andhra weddings and the side that sits next to rasam rice or pappu at home.
seg.992a8475993f.t: ᱠᱳᱰᱤ ᱣᱮᱯᱩᱰᱩ ᱫᱚ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ: ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱟᱡᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ, ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱟᱨ ᱛᱷᱚᱲᱟ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱛᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤᱭᱚᱜᱼᱟ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱛᱮ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣᱜ᱾ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱵᱟᱯᱞᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱦᱚᱵ ᱡᱚᱢᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱚᱲᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱨᱟᱥᱚᱢ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱥᱮ ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱛᱮ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱱᱟ᱾
seg.992a8475993f.back: Kodi vepudu is Andhra's dry chicken fry: small pieces of chicken are cooked in their own juices, then fried well in oil with curry leaves, green chillies and briefly roasted masala until dark and coated in masala. It is eaten at Andhra weddings and at home with rasam rice or pappu.

seg.db90598234ea.src: Our Teja chilli powder gives it the deep red colour and the heat Andhra fries are known for, our turmeric powder goes into the marinade, and our whole cashew kernels, fried golden, go in at the end. Serves 4 as a side.
seg.db90598234ea.t: ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱟᱲᱦᱟ ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱚᱱᱟ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱠᱚ ᱧᱩᱛᱩᱢ, ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱢᱟᱠᱷᱟᱣ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ, ᱟᱨ ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱵᱩᱛ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ, ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ, ᱢᱩᱪᱟᱹᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱡᱚᱢᱟᱜ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ 4 ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ᱾
seg.db90598234ea.back: Our Teja chilli powder gives this deep red colour and that heat for which Andhra fries are famous, our turmeric powder goes in the marinade, and our whole cashew nuts, fried gold colour, go in at the end. As a side dish for 4 people.

seg.22b3994cc48a.src: Marinate chicken in Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder, ginger-garlic paste and lemon, cook it in its own juices, then fry it dry with curry leaves, green chillies, a roasted masala and cashews.
seg.22b3994cc48a.t: ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ, ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ, ᱟᱫᱟ-ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱯᱮᱥᱴ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱟᱠᱷᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱟᱡᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ, ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ, ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.22b3994cc48a.back: Marinate the chicken meat in Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder, ginger-garlic paste and lemon, cook in its own juice, then fry dry with curry leaves, green chilli, fried masala and cashews.

seg.4cb33a348eb8.src: 500 g boneless chicken ⟦1⟧cut into 1-inch pieces; or 600 g small bone-in pieces⟦/1⟧
seg.4cb33a348eb8.t: 500 g ᱡᱟᱝ ᱵᱤᱱ ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ⟦1⟧1 ᱤᱧᱪ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱛᱮ ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ; ᱥᱮ 600 g ᱡᱟᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ⟦/1⟧
seg.4cb33a348eb8.back: 500 g boneless chicken meat ⟦1⟧cut into 1 inch pieces; or 600 g small pieces with bone⟦/1⟧

seg.57789012bc80.src: 15 cashews ⟦1⟧whole cashew kernels; halve any large ones⟦/1⟧
seg.57789012bc80.t: 15 ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ⟦1⟧ᱥᱟᱵᱩᱛ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ; ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱵᱟᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱴᱤᱧ ᱢᱮ⟦/1⟧
seg.57789012bc80.back: 15 cashews ⟦1⟧whole cashew nuts; if big split in two⟦/1⟧

seg.444a0a15a466.t: 1 ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱢᱟᱯ ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ (ᱢᱚᱱ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ) ⟦1⟧ᱯᱚᱛᱞᱟ ᱯᱚᱛᱞᱟ ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ⟦/1⟧
seg.444a0a15a466.back: 1 medium-size onion (as you wish) ⟦1⟧cut thin thin⟦/1⟧

seg.e43b68ea429f.t: 2 ᱫᱟᱨᱮ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ⟦1⟧ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱦᱟᱛᱟᱣ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ, ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 30⟦/1⟧

seg.8df3bc4567e3.src: Pat the chicken dry with a cloth so the marinade sticks.
seg.8df3bc4567e3.t: ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱠᱟᱯᱲᱟ ᱛᱮ ᱪᱟᱯᱟᱹᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱢᱟᱠᱷᱟᱣ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣᱜ᱾
seg.8df3bc4567e3.back: Dry the chicken meat by pressing with a cloth so the marinade sticks.

seg.075327f4deca.src: Marinate the chicken in Teja chilli powder, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice and salt, 30 minutes. Mix well with your hands so every piece is coated.
seg.075327f4deca.t: ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ, ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ, ᱟᱫᱟ-ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱯᱮᱥᱴ, ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱨᱮ 30 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱢᱟᱠᱷᱟᱣ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱛᱤ ᱛᱮ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱛᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣᱜ᱾
seg.075327f4deca.back: Keep the chicken meat marinated in Teja chilli powder, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice and salt for 30 minutes. Mix well by hand so the masala sticks on every piece.

seg.63af904bba96.src: Meanwhile, dry-roast the coriander seeds, cumin seeds, fennel seeds, cloves and cinnamon in a small pan on low heat until fragrant and a shade darker, about 2 minutes. Cool and grind to a coarse powder. This is the fry masala.
seg.63af904bba96.t: ᱚᱱᱟ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ, ᱫᱷᱚᱱᱤᱭᱟ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ, ᱡᱤᱨᱟ, ᱢᱚᱵᱽᱨᱤ, ᱞᱟᱣᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱞᱪᱤᱱᱤ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱜᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱥᱩᱜᱚᱫ ᱦᱤᱡᱩᱜ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱫᱷᱟᱯ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜ, ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 2 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ᱾ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱜᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ᱾
seg.63af904bba96.back: At that time, dry-fry coriander seeds, cumin, fennel, cloves and cinnamon in a small pan on low fire until smell comes and they become one step dark, about 2 minutes. After cooling grind to a coarse powder. This is the fried masala.

seg.4406ac2e72fe.src: Put the chicken in a heavy kadai with no water, cover and set it on medium heat.
seg.4406ac2e72fe.t: ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱵᱤᱱ ᱦᱟᱭᱟᱹᱠ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱦᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.4406ac2e72fe.back: Put the chicken meat without water in a heavy kadai, cover and keep on medium fire.

seg.93ccca0c5178.src: Cook it covered in its own juices till no pink remains, about 12 minutes. Stir once or twice; the chicken releases water as it cooks.
seg.93ccca0c5178.t: ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱟᱡᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱱ ᱜᱩᱞᱟᱹᱵᱤ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱭᱟ, ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 12 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ᱾ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱵᱟᱨ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ; ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱚᱰᱚᱠᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.93ccca0c5178.back: Covered, cook in its own juice until no pink colour remains, about 12 minutes. Stir once or twice; while cooking water comes out of the chicken meat.

seg.32f3a3f56679.src: Uncover and cook on high, stirring, until the liquid has almost dried up, 3–4 minutes. Tip the chicken out onto a plate and wipe the kadai.
seg.32f3a3f56679.t: ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱯᱟᱥᱤ ᱥᱩᱠᱟᱹᱣᱜ, 3–4 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ᱾ ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱛᱷᱟᱨᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱹᱛᱩᱨ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱦᱤ ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.32f3a3f56679.back: Uncovered, cook on high fire stirring until all the water dries, 3–4 minutes. Take the chicken meat out into a plate and clean the kadai.

seg.f3e846aa4edd.src: Heat the oil in the kadai on medium heat.
seg.f3e846aa4edd.t: ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱦᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.f3e846aa4edd.back: Heat oil in the kadai on medium fire.

seg.e210c9534a07.src: Fry the cashews in oil till golden; lift out. They take under a minute, so stir them all the time and lift them out with a slotted spoon.
seg.e210c9534a07.t: ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ; ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱦᱚᱸ ᱠᱚᱢ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫᱼᱟ, ᱚᱱᱟᱛᱮ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱷᱚᱠᱟ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱛᱮ ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.e210c9534a07.back: Fry the cashews in oil until gold colour; take out. This takes even less than one minute, so stir all the time and take out with a slotted spoon.

seg.09e282d2e36f.src: Add the onion, if using, and fry until golden. Fry the green chillies and curry leaves. Stand back; the leaves crackle and spit.
seg.09e282d2e36f.t: ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ, ᱡᱩᱫᱤ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱱᱟᱢ, ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱦᱤ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱥᱟᱝᱜᱤᱧ ᱛᱮ ᱛᱤᱝᱜᱩ ᱢᱮ; ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱠᱚ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱥᱟᱰᱮᱜᱼᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱪᱤᱴᱟᱹᱣᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.09e282d2e36f.back: Onion, if you are adding it, add and fry until golden. Fry the green chillies and curry leaves. Stand back from the kadai; the leaves splutter and the oil spatters.

seg.1fae224eb27a.src: Add the chicken and fry masala. Fry on high till dry and dark, then toss in the cashews. Keep tossing for 6–8 minutes, until the masala clings to the pieces and the edges turn dark and crisp.
seg.1fae224eb27a.t: ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ 6–8 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱩᱪᱷᱟᱞ ᱛᱮ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱢᱮ, ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣᱜ ᱟᱨ ᱜᱟᱫᱮᱨ ᱠᱚ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱢ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜ᱾
seg.1fae224eb27a.back: Add the chicken meat and the fried masala. Fry on high fire until dry and dark, then mix in the cashews. Keep tossing 6–8 minutes, until the masala sticks to the pieces and the edges become dark and crisp.

seg.0b62f402945c.src: Taste, add salt if needed, scatter the coriander leaves and serve hot.
seg.0b62f402945c.t: ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱧᱮᱞ ᱢᱮ, ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱫᱷᱚᱱᱤᱭᱟ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱪᱤᱴᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.0b62f402945c.back: Taste, if needed add salt, sprinkle coriander leaves and serve hot.

seg.349c72ce839a.src: Fry it on high heat at the end so the masala clings to every piece.
seg.349c72ce839a.t: ᱢᱩᱪᱟᱹᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣᱜ᱾
seg.349c72ce839a.back: At the end fry on high fire so the masala sticks on every piece.

seg.d287ba2c2c11.src: Teja chilli powder is very hot. For medium heat use 1 tsp, or swap in Sannam chilli powder for the red colour with less fire.
seg.d287ba2c2c11.t: ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱜᱮᱭᱟ᱾ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱮ ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱚᱢ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱚᱱᱟ ᱵᱚᱫᱚᱞ ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.d287ba2c2c11.back: Teja chilli powder is very hot. For medium heat add 1 small spoon, or for red colour and less heat add Sannam chilli powder instead of it.

seg.a0ef9b138cd4.src: Cut the pieces small and even so they cook through at the same time and crisp up well in the fry.
seg.a0ef9b138cd4.t: ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱢᱟᱯ ᱜᱮᱫ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱚᱜ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱛᱮ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱢᱚᱜ᱾
seg.a0ef9b138cd4.back: Cut the pieces small and of one size so they cook at one time and become well crisp in the frying.

seg.d72b3c1c529a.src: Grind the fry masala just before you cook; the roasted spice smell is the soul of a good vepudu.
seg.d72b3c1c529a.t: ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱜᱮ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ; ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱥᱩᱜᱚᱫ ᱜᱮ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱣᱮᱯᱩᱰᱩ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱡᱤᱣᱤ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ᱾
seg.d72b3c1c529a.back: Grind the fried masala only just before cooking; the smell of fried masala is the life of a good vepudu.

seg.62d6684e446e.src: Bone-in: use 600 g small bone-in pieces and cook them in their juices for 18–20 minutes, until no pink remains near the bone.
seg.62d6684e446e.t: ᱡᱟᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ: 600 g ᱡᱟᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱛᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱟᱡᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱨᱮ 18–20 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ, ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱡᱟᱝ ᱥᱩᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱱ ᱜᱩᱞᱟᱹᱵᱤ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱭᱟ᱾
seg.62d6684e446e.back: With bone: take 600 g small pieces with bone and cook 18–20 minutes in their own juice, until no pink colour remains near the bone.

seg.6960fe7f3ff8.src: Kobbari vepudu: add 3 tbsp grated dry coconut to the fry with the masala and toss until it browns.
seg.6960fe7f3ff8.t: ᱠᱳᱵᱵᱟᱨᱤ ᱣᱮᱯᱩᱰᱩ: ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ 3 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱱᱟᱨᱤᱭᱟᱞ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱷᱩᱨᱟ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱩᱪᱷᱟᱞ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.6960fe7f3ff8.back: Kobbari vepudu: with the masala add 3 big spoons grated dry coconut and toss until brown.

seg.afd92118eb80.src: Mutton vepudu: pressure-cook 500 g boneless mutton with the marinade and ½ cup water for 5–6 whistles, then fry it the same way.
seg.afd92118eb80.t: ᱢᱚᱴᱚᱱ ᱣᱮᱯᱩᱰᱩ: 500 g ᱡᱟᱝ ᱵᱤᱱ ᱢᱮᱨᱚᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱢᱟᱠᱷᱟᱣ ᱟᱨ ½ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱶ 5–6 ᱥᱤᱴᱤ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱯᱨᱮᱥᱟᱨ ᱠᱩᱠᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱚᱱᱟ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.afd92118eb80.back: Mutton vepudu: marinate 500 g boneless goat meat and with ½ cup of water cook in a pressure cooker up to 5–6 whistles, then fry in that same way.

seg.2c4ab1a1a5de.src: Serve hot as a side with rasam rice, pappu and rice or sambar rice, or on its own as a starter with sliced onion and lemon wedges.
seg.2c4ab1a1a5de.t: ᱨᱟᱥᱚᱢ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ, ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱥᱮ ᱥᱟᱢᱵᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱡᱚᱢᱟᱜ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱮ ᱮᱦᱚᱵ ᱡᱚᱢᱟᱜ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱥᱟᱶ᱾
seg.2c4ab1a1a5de.back: Serve hot as a side dish with rasam rice, pappu and rice or sambar rice, or as a starting food with cut onion and lemon pieces.

seg.b7598301bd86.src: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat in a hot pan with a few drops of oil until steaming hot all the way through; it crisps up again.
seg.b7598301bd86.t: ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ 2 ᱢᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱴᱚᱯᱟ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱫᱩᱦᱲᱟᱹ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ, ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱯᱩᱨᱟᱹ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱥᱤᱡᱩ ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ; ᱫᱩᱦᱲᱟᱹ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.b7598301bd86.back: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Add a few drops of oil to a hot pan and reheat, until it is fully hot inside and steam comes out; it becomes crisp again.

seg.551573b4b443.src: What is the difference between chicken fry and chicken curry in Andhra?
seg.551573b4b443.t: ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱩᱛᱩ ᱨᱮ ᱪᱮᱫ ᱯᱷᱟᱨᱟᱠ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ?
seg.551573b4b443.back: What difference is there between chicken meat fry and chicken meat curry in Andhra?

seg.dbeff7335e31.src: Vepudu is dry: the chicken is cooked in its own juices, then fried until the masala coats it with no gravy. Kodi kura is a curry with an onion-tomato gravy for rice.
seg.dbeff7335e31.t: ᱣᱮᱯᱩᱰᱩ ᱫᱚ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱜᱮᱭᱟ: ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱟᱡᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱡᱩᱞ ᱵᱤᱱ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤᱭᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱠᱳᱰᱤ ᱠᱩᱨᱟ ᱫᱚ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ-ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱡᱩᱞ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜ ᱩᱛᱩ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ᱾
seg.dbeff7335e31.back: Vepudu is dry: the chicken meat after cooking in its own juice is then fried until the masala sticks without gravy. Kodi kura is a curry with onion-tomato gravy for rice.

seg.439aacfe8e34.src: Should I use boneless or bone-in chicken for vepudu?
seg.439aacfe8e34.t: ᱣᱮᱯᱩᱰᱩ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱡᱟᱝ ᱵᱤᱱ ᱥᱮ ᱡᱟᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱦᱟᱛᱟᱣ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ?
seg.439aacfe8e34.back: For vepudu must boneless or with-bone chicken meat be taken?

seg.982f470b118d.src: Both work. Boneless cooks faster and crisps more; small bone-in pieces have more flavour but need about 8 minutes longer in their juices.
seg.982f470b118d.t: ᱵᱟᱨᱭᱟ ᱜᱮ ᱪᱟᱞᱟᱣᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱡᱟᱝ ᱵᱤᱱ ᱞᱚᱜᱚᱱ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱚᱜᱼᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ; ᱡᱟᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ ᱢᱮᱱᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱟᱡᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 8 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ᱾
seg.982f470b118d.back: Both work. Boneless cooks quickly and becomes more crisp; small pieces with bone have more taste but need about 8 more minutes in their own juice.

seg.ade697e78f9b.src: Cut open the thickest piece. The chicken is cooked when no pink remains in the middle (or near the bone) and the juices run clear.
seg.ade697e78f9b.t: ᱡᱟᱹᱥᱛᱤ ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱜᱮᱫ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱧᱮᱞ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱨᱮ (ᱥᱮ ᱡᱟᱝ ᱥᱩᱨ ᱨᱮ) ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱱ ᱜᱩᱞᱟᱹᱵᱤ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱟᱨ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱚᱜ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ᱾
seg.ade697e78f9b.back: Cut the thickest piece and look. If no pink colour remains in the middle (or near the bone) and the juice comes out clear, the chicken meat is cooked.

seg.eddd3046275b.src: How do I make kodi vepudu less spicy?
seg.eddd3046275b.t: ᱠᱳᱰᱤ ᱣᱮᱯᱩᱰᱩ ᱪᱮᱫ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱠᱚᱢ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ?
seg.eddd3046275b.back: How can kodi vepudu be made less hot?

seg.9b5459aec9d6.src: Use 1 tsp Teja chilli powder, or swap in Sannam chilli powder, and slit only 2 green chillies. The cashews and curry leaves keep the flavour full.
seg.9b5459aec9d6.t: 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱮ ᱚᱱᱟ ᱵᱚᱫᱚᱞ ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ, ᱟᱨ ᱥᱩᱢᱩᱝ 2 ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱪᱤᱨᱟᱹ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱯᱮᱨᱮᱡ ᱫᱚᱦᱚᱭᱟ᱾
seg.9b5459aec9d6.back: Add 1 small spoon of Teja chilli powder, or instead of it Sannam chilli powder, and slit only 2 green chillies. The cashews and curry leaves keep the taste full.

seg.a00af5cf9954.src: కోడి వేపుడు · Kodi Vepudu (Andhra Chicken Fry) | 1acrefarms
seg.a00af5cf9954.t: ᱠᱳᱰᱤ ᱣᱮᱯᱩᱰᱩ · ᱠᱳᱰᱤ ᱣᱮᱯᱩᱰᱩ (ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ) | 1acrefarms
seg.a00af5cf9954.back: Kodi Vepudu · Kodi Vepudu (Andhra chicken meat fry) | 1acrefarms

seg.1af4fbb646e3.src: కోడి వేపుడు. Andhra chicken fry: chicken in Teja chilli powder and turmeric powder, fried dry with curry leaves, green chillies, a roasted masala and our cashews.
seg.1af4fbb646e3.t: ᱠᱳᱰᱤ ᱣᱮᱯᱩᱰᱩ᱾ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ: ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱟᱠᱷᱟᱣ ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ, ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ, ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ, ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ᱾
seg.1af4fbb646e3.back: Kodi Vepudu. Andhra chicken meat fry: chicken meat marinated in Teja chilli powder and turmeric powder, fried dry with curry leaves, green chilli, fried masala and our cashews.

seg.917dba1166ab.src: Kodi Vepudu: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.917dba1166ab.t: ᱠᱳᱰᱤ ᱣᱮᱯᱩᱰᱩ: 1acrefarms ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱠᱟᱨᱰ, ᱡᱤᱱᱤᱥ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ
seg.917dba1166ab.back: Kodi Vepudu: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and steps

seg.f9771e2222df.src: Nimmakaya pulihora is the bright yellow lemon rice of Andhra homes: cooked rice tossed with a crackling tempering of peanuts, chana dal, urad dal, mustard seeds, green chillies and curry leaves, then soured with lemon juice. It is the rice packed for train journeys, school tiffin boxes and temple days, and it is made in big batches for festivals and pujas.
seg.f9771e2222df.t: ᱱᱤᱢᱢᱟᱠᱟᱭᱟ ᱯᱩᱞᱤᱦᱳᱨᱟ ᱫᱚ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱚᱲᱟᱜ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱡᱚᱞᱚᱜ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ: ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱪᱤᱱᱟ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ, ᱵᱩᱴ ᱫᱟᱞ, ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ, ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ, ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣᱚᱜᱼᱟ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱛᱮ ᱡᱚᱰᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱨᱮᱞ ᱥᱟᱦᱮᱫ, ᱤᱥᱠᱩᱞ ᱴᱤᱯᱷᱤᱱ ᱵᱟᱠᱥᱚ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱚᱱᱫᱤᱨ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱵᱟᱸᱫᱷᱟᱣᱚᱜᱼᱟ, ᱟᱨ ᱯᱚᱨᱚᱵ ᱟᱨ ᱯᱩᱡᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱟᱭᱢᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.f9771e2222df.back: Nimmakaya pulihora is the yellow lemon rice eaten in Andhra homes: cooked rice is mixed with a crackling tempering of groundnuts, chana dal, urad dal, mustard seeds, green chillies and curry leaves, then joined with lemon juice. It is packed for train journeys, school tiffin boxes and temple days, and made in large amounts for festivals and puja.

seg.ac569e0882d5.src: Our turmeric powder goes into the hot oil for a few seconds, which turns every grain an even golden yellow and takes away its raw edge. This recipe serves 4.
seg.ac569e0882d5.t: ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱥᱮᱠᱮᱱᱰ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ, ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱮᱫᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱚᱱᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱸᱪᱟ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱪᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱮᱫᱟ᱾ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ 4 ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ᱾
seg.ac569e0882d5.back: Our turmeric powder goes in the hot oil for a few seconds, which gives every grain an even gold-yellow colour and takes away its raw taste. This recipe is for 4 people.

seg.d194bee0cc5e.src: Total includes cooking the rice and a 15-minute rest so the flavours settle.
seg.d194bee0cc5e.t: ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱟᱨ 15 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱥᱮᱞᱮᱫ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱛᱷᱤᱨᱚᱜ᱾
seg.d194bee0cc5e.back: In the total time the cooking of the rice and 15 minutes of keeping are included so the taste settles.

seg.1cfa4342f462.src: Fry peanuts, dals, mustard seeds, chillies and curry leaves in oil, add turmeric powder and hing, then toss with cooled rice, salt and lemon juice.
seg.1cfa4342f462.t: ᱪᱤᱱᱟ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ, ᱫᱟᱞ, ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ, ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱤᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ, ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.1cfa4342f462.back: Fry peanuts, dal, mustard seeds, chilli [or: pepper? 'marich', colour not stated] and curry leaves in oil, add turmeric powder and hing [asafoetida], then mix with the cooled [or: prepared? 'lalag akan' unclear] rice, salt and lemon juice.

seg.2561142fed2c.src: 1 cup rice ⟦1⟧sona masoori, about 200 g; gives about 3 cups cooked⟦/1⟧
seg.2561142fed2c.t: 1 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱪᱟᱩᱞᱤ ⟦1⟧ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱢᱟᱥᱩᱨᱤ, ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 200 g; ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 3 ᱠᱟᱯ⟦/1⟧
seg.2561142fed2c.back: 1 cup rice ⟦1⟧Sona Masoori, about 200 g; after cooking about 3 cups⟦/1⟧

seg.06ba75699134.src: 3 cups cooked rice ⟦1⟧cooked a little firm, grains separate⟦/1⟧
seg.06ba75699134.t: 3 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ⟦1⟧ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ, ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱟᱞᱟᱜ⟦/1⟧
seg.06ba75699134.back: 3 cups cooked rice ⟦1⟧cooked a little firm, grains separate⟦/1⟧

seg.fbba93c11bc9.src: 3 tbsp lemon juice ⟦1⟧from about 2 lemons; add more to taste⟦/1⟧
seg.fbba93c11bc9.t: 3 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ ⟦1⟧ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 2 ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ; ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ⟦/1⟧
seg.fbba93c11bc9.back: 3 big spoons lemon juice ⟦1⟧from about 2 lemons; according to taste more⟦/1⟧

seg.e254f20f8f14.src: 3 tbsp oil ⟦1⟧groundnut oil is the usual choice⟦/1⟧
seg.e254f20f8f14.t: 3 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ⟦1⟧ᱥᱟᱫᱷᱟᱨᱚᱱ ᱛᱮ ᱪᱤᱱᱟ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ⟦/1⟧

seg.ad3af06df4e4.t: ¼ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱪᱤᱱᱟ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ ⟦1⟧ᱠᱟᱸᱪᱟ, ᱪᱷᱚᱞᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ⟦/1⟧

seg.3165601826cb.t: 2 ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ⟦1⟧ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱛᱮ ᱵᱟᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱴᱤᱧ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ⟦/1⟧
seg.3165601826cb.back: 2 dry red chillies ⟦1⟧broken in two by hand⟦/1⟧

seg.985dfde69f06.t: 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱟᱫᱟ ⟦1⟧ᱢᱚᱱ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ⟦/1⟧
seg.985dfde69f06.back: 1 small spoon grated ginger ⟦1⟧as you wish⟦/1⟧

seg.bc63d9715c03.src: Wash the rice and cook it with 2 cups of water until just done, so the grains stay separate. You need about 3 cups of cooked rice.
seg.bc63d9715c03.t: ᱪᱟᱩᱞᱤ ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ 2 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱥᱩᱢᱩᱝ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ, ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱭ᱾ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 3 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ᱾
seg.bc63d9715c03.back: Wash the rice and cook with 2 cups of water just until cooked, so the grains stay separate. About 3 cups of cooked rice are needed.

seg.adb2b75edafc.src: Spread the cooked rice on a plate to cool; add the salt. Fluff it with a fork and let it sit about 10 minutes until warm, not hot, so the grains do not break when mixed.
seg.adb2b75edafc.t: ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱛᱷᱟᱨᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱯᱟᱥᱱᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ; ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱠᱟᱸᱴᱟ ᱛᱮ ᱯᱷᱩᱞᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 10 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱭ, ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱫᱚ ᱵᱟᱝ, ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱨᱟᱹᱯᱩᱫᱚᱜ᱾
seg.adb2b75edafc.back: Spread the cooked rice in a plate to cool; add salt. Fluff with a fork and keep about 10 minutes until it is a little warm, not very hot, so the grains don't break while mixing.

seg.e05322a3ed24.src: Heat the oil; fry the peanuts, dals, mustard seeds, chillies and curry leaves. Start with the peanuts on medium heat and fry them about 2 minutes until they crackle and the skins darken.
seg.e05322a3ed24.t: ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ; ᱪᱤᱱᱟ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ, ᱫᱟᱞ, ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ, ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ ᱪᱤᱱᱟ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 2 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱥᱟᱰᱮᱜ ᱟᱨ ᱪᱷᱚᱞᱟ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮᱭᱚᱜ᱾
seg.e05322a3ed24.back: Heat the oil; fry the groundnuts, dal, mustard seeds, chillies and curry leaves. On medium heat first fry the groundnuts for about 2 minutes until they crackle and the skins darken.

seg.542a4fea7b18.src: Add the chana dal and urad dal and fry until light golden, about 1 minute.
seg.542a4fea7b18.t: ᱵᱩᱴ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱟᱨ ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱟᱞᱠᱟᱹ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 1 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ᱾
seg.542a4fea7b18.back: Add chana dal and urad dal and fry until light gold colour, about 1 minute.

seg.502483d7a042.src: Add the mustard seeds and let them splutter, then add the dry red chillies, green chillies, ginger and curry leaves and fry a few seconds until the leaves turn crisp.
seg.502483d7a042.t: ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱥᱟᱰᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ, ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ, ᱟᱫᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱥᱮᱠᱮᱱᱰ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱢᱚᱜ᱾
seg.502483d7a042.back: Add mustard seeds and let crackle, then adding dry red chilli, green chilli, ginger and curry leaves fry a few seconds until the leaves become crisp.

seg.6e856356980b.src: Stir in the turmeric powder and hing; switch off. Stir for 5–10 seconds only so the turmeric cooks in the hot oil without burning.
seg.6e856356980b.t: ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱤᱝ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ; ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱥᱩᱢᱩᱝ 5–10 ᱥᱮᱠᱮᱱᱰ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱚᱜ ᱢᱮᱱᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱡᱟᱹᱞᱤᱭᱚᱜ᱾
seg.6e856356980b.back: Mix in the turmeric powder and hing; turn off the fire. Stir just 5–10 seconds so the turmeric cooks in the hot oil but does not burn.

seg.dd6ccaf923d8.src: Pour over the rice, add the lemon juice and mix gently. Use your fingers or a flat spatula and lift the rice from below so every grain turns yellow without turning mushy.
seg.dd6ccaf923d8.t: ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱪᱮᱛᱟᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱟᱦᱟᱭ ᱛᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱛᱤ ᱛᱟᱨᱟᱵ ᱥᱮ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱵᱮᱵᱷᱟᱨ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱟᱛᱟᱨ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱨᱟᱠᱟᱵ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜ ᱢᱮᱱᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱜᱷᱟᱸᱴᱩᱣᱟᱹᱜ᱾
seg.dd6ccaf923d8.back: Pour over the rice, add lemon juice and mix slowly. Use fingertips or a flat spoon and lift the rice from the bottom so every grain becomes yellow colour but is not mashed.

seg.1bfc2c04d40e.src: Taste and add more salt or lemon juice if needed. The rice should taste clearly sour and salty, as the flavour softens on standing.
seg.1bfc2c04d40e.t: ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱧᱮᱞ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱥᱮ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱯᱩᱨᱟᱹ ᱡᱚᱰ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ, ᱪᱮᱫᱟᱜ ᱥᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.1bfc2c04d40e.back: Taste and if needed add more salt or lemon juice. The rice needs to be fully sour and salty, because if kept the taste softens.

seg.8cea6688d0fb.src: Cover and rest the pulihora for 15 minutes before serving so the rice takes in the lemon and tempering.
seg.8cea6688d0fb.t: ᱮᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱯᱩᱞᱤᱦᱳᱨᱟ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ 15 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱟᱨ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱥᱚᱵᱚᱫᱚᱜ᱾
seg.8cea6688d0fb.back: Before serving keep the pulihora covered 15 minutes so the rice soaks up the lemon and tempering.

seg.c1a7043ce357.src: Add the lemon juice off the heat so it stays sharp. Cooked lemon juice turns bitter.
seg.c1a7043ce357.t: ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱟᱲᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱡᱚᱰ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱭ᱾ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱦᱚᱨᱚᱜᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.c1a7043ce357.back: Add the lemon juice after taking off the fire so it stays sour. Cooked lemon juice becomes bitter.

seg.b634a4257b6c.src: Cook the rice slightly firm and let it cool before mixing; hot, soft rice turns pasty.
seg.b634a4257b6c.t: ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ; ᱞᱚᱞᱚ, ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱯᱮᱥᱴ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.b634a4257b6c.back: Cook the rice a little firm and cool before mixing; hot, soft rice becomes like a paste.

seg.a1d93274ea3f.src: Keep the turmeric powder in the oil for just a few seconds; burnt turmeric gives a dark colour and a bitter taste.
seg.a1d93274ea3f.t: ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱩᱢᱩᱝ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱥᱮᱠᱮᱱᱰ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ; ᱡᱟᱹᱞᱤ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱚᱨᱚᱜ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.a1d93274ea3f.back: Keep turmeric powder in the oil only a few seconds; burnt turmeric gives dark colour and bitter taste.

seg.747474140bbf.src: Leftover rice from the morning works well, as the grains are already firm and separate.
seg.747474140bbf.t: ᱥᱟᱹᱠᱟᱹᱞ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱪᱟᱞᱟᱣᱜᱼᱟ, ᱪᱮᱫᱟᱜ ᱥᱮ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱜᱮ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱟᱨ ᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱱᱟ᱾
seg.747474140bbf.back: Leftover rice from the morning works well, because the grains are already firm and separate.

seg.7a379d805448.src: Cashews: fry 10 cashew halves with the peanuts for a festive pulihora.
seg.7a379d805448.t: ᱠᱟᱡᱩ: ᱯᱚᱨᱚᱵ ᱯᱩᱞᱤᱦᱳᱨᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱪᱤᱱᱟ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ ᱥᱟᱶ 10 ᱵᱟᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱴᱤᱧ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.7a379d805448.back: Cashew: for festive pulihora fry 10 cashew halves along with the groundnuts.

seg.be93899ec308.src: Mamidikaya pulihora: in place of lemon juice, mix in 1 cup grated raw mango with the tempering.
seg.be93899ec308.t: ᱢᱟᱢᱤᱰᱤᱠᱟᱭᱟ ᱯᱩᱞᱤᱦᱳᱨᱟ: ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱵᱚᱫᱚᱞ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱥᱟᱶ 1 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱠᱟᱸᱪᱟ ᱩᱞ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.be93899ec308.back: Mamidikaya pulihora: instead of lemon juice mix 1 cup grated raw mango with the tempering.

seg.867dba923c04.src: Grated coconut: add 2 tbsp grated coconut along with the lemon juice for a milder rice.
seg.867dba923c04.t: ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱱᱟᱨᱤᱭᱟᱞ: ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱥᱟᱶ 2 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱱᱟᱨᱤᱭᱟᱞ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.867dba923c04.back: Grated coconut: for soft rice add 2 big spoons grated coconut with the lemon juice.

seg.88b87529b506.src: Serve at room temperature with curd, a pickle or appadams. It is a classic tiffin-box and travel rice.
seg.88b87529b506.t: ᱠᱚᱴᱷᱨᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱤ, ᱟᱪᱟᱨ ᱥᱮ ᱟᱯᱯᱟᱰᱚᱢ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱫᱚ ᱴᱤᱯᱷᱤᱱ ᱵᱟᱠᱥᱚ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱦᱮᱫ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱧᱩᱛᱩᱢ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ᱾
seg.88b87529b506.back: Serve at room temperature with curd, pickle or appadam. This is the famous rice of tiffin box and journey.

seg.9791f1c7a8e4.src: It keeps well at room temperature for about 6 hours, which is why it travels. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within a day.
seg.9791f1c7a8e4.t: ᱠᱚᱴᱷᱨᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 6 ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱱᱟ, ᱚᱱᱟᱛᱮ ᱥᱟᱦᱮᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱫᱤᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱢᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.9791f1c7a8e4.back: At room temperature it stays good about 6 hours, so it is taken on journeys. Keep the leftover covered in the fridge and eat within one day.

seg.c12ab7274709.src: Why does my lemon rice taste bitter?
seg.c12ab7274709.t: ᱤᱧᱟᱜ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱪᱮᱫᱟᱜ ᱦᱚᱨᱚᱜ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ?
seg.c12ab7274709.back: Why does my lemon rice taste bitter?

seg.44b56d19b9fb.src: Either the lemon juice was cooked or the turmeric burnt in the oil. Switch off the stove before the turmeric goes in, and add the lemon juice only to the rice, off the heat.
seg.44b56d19b9fb.t: ᱥᱮ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱮᱱᱟ ᱥᱮ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱟᱹᱞᱤ ᱮᱱᱟ᱾ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱪᱩᱞᱦᱟᱹ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱢᱮ, ᱟᱨ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱥᱩᱢᱩᱝ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱨᱮ, ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱟᱲᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.44b56d19b9fb.back: Either the lemon juice was cooked or the turmeric burnt in the oil. Before adding turmeric turn off the stove, and add lemon juice only to the rice, after taking off the fire.

seg.69e4bfb93ba8.src: What is the difference between pulihora and lemon rice?
seg.69e4bfb93ba8.t: ᱯᱩᱞᱤᱦᱳᱨᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱪᱮᱫ ᱯᱷᱟᱨᱟᱠ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ?
seg.69e4bfb93ba8.back: What difference is there between pulihora and lemon rice?

seg.f2f993f1b94b.src: Pulihora is the Telugu name for soured rice. Chintapandu pulihora is soured with tamarind paste; nimmakaya pulihora is the lemon version, quicker to make and lighter in colour.
seg.f2f993f1b94b.t: ᱯᱩᱞᱤᱦᱳᱨᱟ ᱫᱚ ᱡᱚᱰ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱛᱮᱞᱩᱜᱩ ᱧᱩᱛᱩᱢ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ᱾ ᱪᱤᱱᱛᱟᱯᱟᱱᱰᱩ ᱯᱩᱞᱤᱦᱳᱨᱟ ᱡᱚᱡᱚ ᱯᱮᱥᱴ ᱛᱮ ᱡᱚᱰᱚᱜᱼᱟ; ᱱᱤᱢᱢᱟᱠᱟᱭᱟ ᱯᱩᱞᱤᱦᱳᱨᱟ ᱫᱚ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ, ᱞᱚᱜᱚᱱ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣᱚᱜᱼᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱞᱠᱟᱹ᱾
seg.f2f993f1b94b.back: Pulihora is the Telugu name of sour rice. Chintapandu pulihora is soured with tamarind paste; nimmakaya pulihora is lemon-like, made quickly and light in colour.

seg.1ab5dcf1d80a.src: How do I stop lemon rice from getting mushy?
seg.1ab5dcf1d80a.t: ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱜᱷᱟᱸᱴᱩᱣᱟᱹ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱪᱮᱫ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ?
seg.1ab5dcf1d80a.back: How can lemon rice be saved from becoming mashed?

seg.8a0fad2d4bfd.src: Cook the rice a little firm with less water, cool it on a plate, and mix gently by lifting from below instead of pressing.
seg.8a0fad2d4bfd.t: ᱠᱚᱢ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱛᱮ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱷᱟᱨᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱢᱮ, ᱟᱨ ᱪᱟᱯᱟᱹᱣ ᱵᱚᱫᱚᱞ ᱞᱟᱛᱟᱨ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱨᱟᱠᱟᱵ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱞᱟᱦᱟᱭ ᱛᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.8a0fad2d4bfd.back: Cook the rice a little firm with less water, cool in a plate, and instead of pressing lift from the bottom and mix slowly.

seg.dd00224f5f94.src: How much lemon juice for 3 cups of rice?
seg.dd00224f5f94.t: 3 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱛᱤᱱᱟᱹᱜ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ?
seg.dd00224f5f94.back: How much lemon juice for 3 cups of rice?

seg.50f8efabb87e.src: About 3 tbsp, the juice of 2 medium lemons. Add it slowly and taste, because lemons vary in sourness.
seg.50f8efabb87e.t: ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 3 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ, 2 ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱢᱟᱯ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱥ᱾ ᱞᱟᱦᱟᱭ ᱛᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱧᱮᱞ ᱢᱮ, ᱪᱮᱫᱟᱜ ᱥᱮ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱡᱚᱰ ᱮᱴᱟᱜ ᱮᱴᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱱᱟ᱾
seg.50f8efabb87e.back: About 3 big spoons, the juice of 2 medium-size lemons. Add slowly and taste, because the sourness of lemons is different in each.

seg.0251508f9c8b.t: ᱱᱤᱢᱢᱟᱠᱟᱭᱟ ᱯᱩᱞᱤᱦᱳᱨᱟ · ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ | 1acrefarms

seg.2d3c4d5f7608.src: నిమ్మకాయ పులిహోర. Andhra lemon rice: cooled rice tossed with a peanut and dal tempering, our turmeric powder and lemon juice. Step-by-step method, tips and FAQs.
seg.2d3c4d5f7608.t: ᱱᱤᱢᱢᱟᱠᱟᱭᱟ ᱯᱩᱞᱤᱦᱳᱨᱟ᱾ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ: ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱪᱤᱱᱟ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ, ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ᱾ ᱫᱷᱟᱯ ᱫᱷᱟᱯ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ, ᱠᱟᱹᱢᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱛᱷᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱩᱠᱞᱤ ᱛᱮᱞᱟ᱾
seg.2d3c4d5f7608.back: Nimmakaya Pulihora. Andhra lemon rice: in cooled [or: prepared/cooked? 'lalag akan' unclear] rice, a tempering [chhowk] of peanuts [lit. 'china badam'] and dal, our turmeric powder and lemon juice mixed in. Step-by-step making method [lit. way], work-related notes [or: tips/things to know about the work?] and questions-answers [i.e. FAQ].

seg.5f0282fcd0a8.src: Nimmakaya Pulihora: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.5f0282fcd0a8.t: ᱱᱤᱢᱢᱟᱠᱟᱭᱟ ᱯᱩᱞᱤᱦᱳᱨᱟ: 1acrefarms ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱠᱟᱨᱰ, ᱡᱤᱱᱤᱥ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ
seg.5f0282fcd0a8.back: Nimmakaya Pulihora: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and steps

seg.8922ef1e3767.src: Pasupu annam is plain rice turned bright yellow with turmeric and tossed in a crackling tempering of mustard seeds, chana dal, curry leaves and green chillies, with fried cashews on top. Andhra homes make it for lunch boxes, for quick weekday meals and as a prasadam on puja days, often with the morning's leftover rice.
seg.8922ef1e3767.t: ᱯᱟᱥᱩᱯᱩ ᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱫᱚ ᱥᱟᱫᱷᱟᱨᱚᱱ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱛᱮ ᱡᱚᱞᱚᱜ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ, ᱵᱩᱴ ᱫᱟᱞ, ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣᱚᱜᱼᱟ, ᱪᱮᱛᱟᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱥᱟᱶ᱾ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱚᱲᱟᱜ ᱠᱚ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱞᱟᱧᱪ ᱵᱟᱠᱥᱚ, ᱦᱟᱯᱛᱟ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱞᱚᱜᱚᱱ ᱡᱚᱢᱟᱜ ᱟᱨ ᱯᱩᱡᱟ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱯᱨᱚᱥᱟᱫ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣᱟ, ᱟᱭᱢᱟ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱥᱟᱹᱠᱟᱹᱞ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱛᱮ᱾
seg.8922ef1e3767.back: Pasupu annam is ordinary rice which, made shining yellow colour with turmeric, is mixed in a crackling tempering of mustard seeds, chana dal, curry leaves and green chilli, with fried cashews on top. Andhra houses make this for lunch boxes, quick meals of the week and as prasad on puja days, many times from leftover morning rice.

seg.510252086556.src: Our hill turmeric powder (Konda Pasupu) gives the rice its deep yellow colour and an earthy turmeric smell, so half a teaspoon is enough for 4. Whole cashews (Jeedipappu) fried in the same oil add the crunch.
seg.510252086556.t: ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱩᱨᱩ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ (ᱠᱚᱱᱰᱟ ᱯᱟᱥᱩᱯᱩ) ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱟᱲᱦᱟ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱟᱥᱟ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱥᱩᱜᱚᱫ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ, ᱚᱱᱟᱛᱮ 4 ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱟᱫᱷᱟ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱜᱮ ᱡᱚᱛᱚᱱ᱾ ᱚᱱᱟ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱥᱟᱵᱩᱛ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ (ᱡᱤᱰᱤᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ) ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱢ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.510252086556.back: Our hill turmeric powder (konda pasupu) gives the rice a deep yellow colour and soil-like turmeric smell, so for 4 people only half a small spoon is enough. Whole cashews (Jidipappu) fried in that oil give a crunchy taste.

seg.38badedc8d11.src: Total includes about 15 minutes for the cooked rice to cool.
seg.38badedc8d11.t: ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 15 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱥᱮᱞᱮᱫ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.38badedc8d11.back: In the total time about 15 minutes for the cooked rice to cool is included.

seg.8ad70ebff643.src: Cook rice and let it cool. Fry cashews, mustard seeds, chana dal, chillies and curry leaves in oil, add hill turmeric powder and toss in the rice.
seg.8ad70ebff643.t: ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ, ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ, ᱵᱩᱴ ᱫᱟᱞ, ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱵᱩᱨᱩ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.8ad70ebff643.back: Cook the rice and cool it. Fry cashew, mustard seeds, chana dal, chilli and curry leaves in oil, add hill turmeric powder and mix the rice.

seg.bc286f12f1ba.src: 1 cup rice ⟦1⟧sona masoori, about 200 g; makes about 3 cups cooked⟦/1⟧
seg.bc286f12f1ba.t: 1 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱪᱟᱩᱞᱤ ⟦1⟧ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱢᱟᱥᱩᱨᱤ, ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 200 g; ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 3 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ⟦/1⟧
seg.bc286f12f1ba.back: 1 cup rice ⟦1⟧Sona Masoori, about 200 g; after cooking about 3 cups are made⟦/1⟧

seg.06cd9d581aec.src: ½ tsp hill turmeric powder ⟦1⟧Konda Pasupu⟦/1⟧
seg.06cd9d581aec.t: ½ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱵᱩᱨᱩ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ⟦1⟧ᱠᱚᱱᱰᱟ ᱯᱟᱥᱩᱯᱩ⟦/1⟧
seg.06cd9d581aec.back: ½ small spoon hill turmeric powder ⟦1⟧konda pasupu⟦/1⟧

seg.399f19de4e13.src: 1 tbsp ghee (optional) ⟦1⟧stirred in at the end⟦/1⟧
seg.399f19de4e13.t: 1 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ (ᱢᱚᱱ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ) ⟦1⟧ᱢᱩᱪᱟᱹᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ⟦/1⟧
seg.399f19de4e13.back: 1 big spoon ghee (as you wish) ⟦1⟧mixed in at the end⟦/1⟧

seg.afe3b0737680.back: It is also good with ⟦1⟧turmeric powder⟦/1⟧.

seg.53fcfe53b909.src: Wash the rice in 2–3 changes of water and drain it.
seg.53fcfe53b909.t: ᱪᱟᱩᱞᱤ 2–3 ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱵᱚᱫᱚᱞ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱧᱩᱨ ᱦᱤᱡᱩᱜ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.53fcfe53b909.back: Wash the rice changing water 2–3 times and drain the water.

seg.cdcf37be99e8.src: Cook the rice so the grains stay separate, then spread it on a plate to cool. Use 2 cups water to 1 cup rice in a pot or pressure cooker (2 whistles), and fluff it with a fork before spreading it out.
seg.cdcf37be99e8.t: ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱭ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱛᱷᱟᱨᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱯᱟᱥᱱᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱦᱟᱸᱰᱤ ᱥᱮ ᱯᱨᱮᱥᱟᱨ ᱠᱩᱠᱟᱨ (2 ᱥᱤᱴᱤ) ᱨᱮ 1 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱪᱟᱩᱞᱤ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 2 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱟᱨ ᱯᱟᱥᱱᱟᱣ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱠᱟᱸᱴᱟ ᱛᱮ ᱯᱷᱩᱞᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.cdcf37be99e8.back: Cook the rice so the grains stay separate, then spread in a plate to cool. In a pot or pressure cooker (2 whistles) add 2 cups of water for 1 cup rice, and before spreading fluff with a fork.

seg.296995189451.src: Let the rice cool for about 15 minutes until it is just warm. Sprinkle the salt over it.
seg.296995189451.t: ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 15 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱥᱩᱢᱩᱝ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱭ᱾ ᱪᱮᱛᱟᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱪᱤᱴᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.296995189451.back: Keep the rice to cool about 15 minutes until it is just a little warm. Sprinkle salt on top.

seg.48839bd22983.src: Heat the oil in a wide kadai on medium heat.
seg.48839bd22983.t: ᱢᱤᱫᱴᱟᱝ ᱚᱥᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱦᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.48839bd22983.back: Heat oil in a dry kadai on medium fire.

seg.bdc1a0df8ffc.src: Fry the cashews in the oil till golden; lift out. Add mustard seeds and chana dal. Keep the cashews on a plate; they turn golden in about 1 minute.
seg.bdc1a0df8ffc.t: ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ; ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱴ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱛᱷᱟᱨᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ; ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 1 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.bdc1a0df8ffc.back: Fry the cashews in oil until gold colour; take out. Add mustard seeds and chana dal. Keep the cashews in a plate; in about 1 minute they become gold colour.

seg.0729c6efc94a.src: Once the mustard seeds splutter, add the urad dal and the dried red chillies and stir.
seg.0729c6efc94a.t: ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱥᱟᱰᱮ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ, ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱟᱨ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.0729c6efc94a.back: When the mustard seeds crackle, add urad dal and dry red chilli and stir.

seg.2688182af66a.src: When the dal turns golden, add the chillies and curry leaves, then the turmeric on low heat. Add the ginger and asafoetida with the curry leaves, and stir the turmeric for only 5–10 seconds.
seg.2688182af66a.t: ᱫᱟᱞ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ᱾ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱟᱫᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱤᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱥᱩᱢᱩᱝ 5–10 ᱥᱮᱠᱮᱱᱰ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.2688182af66a.back: As soon as the dal becomes gold colour add chilli and curry leaves, then turmeric on low fire. With the curry leaves add ginger and hing, and stir the turmeric just 5–10 seconds.

seg.59fd9b87153d.src: Switch off the heat straight away so the turmeric does not burn.
seg.59fd9b87153d.t: ᱛᱩᱨᱩᱛ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱡᱟᱹᱞᱤᱭᱚᱜ᱾
seg.59fd9b87153d.back: Turn off the fire at once so the turmeric doesn't burn.

seg.15dc85e42ca1.src: Tip in the rice, cashews and salt and toss gently till evenly yellow. Use a flat spatula and lift and fold rather than pressing down, so the grains stay whole.
seg.15dc85e42ca1.t: ᱫᱟᱠᱟ, ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ ᱛᱮ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱞᱟᱦᱟᱭ ᱛᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱵᱮᱵᱷᱟᱨ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱪᱟᱯᱟᱹᱣ ᱵᱚᱫᱚᱞ ᱨᱟᱠᱟᱵ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱩᱞᱴᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱥᱟᱵᱩᱛ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱭ᱾
seg.15dc85e42ca1.back: Add the rice, cashews and salt and mix slowly until evenly yellow colour. Use a flat spoon and instead of pressing lift and turn, so the grains stay whole.

seg.b005e5771235.src: Taste for salt, stir in the ghee if using, cover and leave for 5 minutes before serving so the rice takes on the tempering.
seg.b005e5771235.t: ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱧᱮᱞ ᱢᱮ, ᱡᱩᱫᱤ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱱᱟᱢ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱮᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ 5 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱥᱚᱵᱚᱫᱚᱜ᱾
seg.b005e5771235.back: Taste the salt, if you are adding it mix in ghee, cover and before serving keep 5 minutes so the rice soaks up the tempering.

seg.9bce1ed4dbee.src: Spread the rice to cool first so the grains do not break.
seg.9bce1ed4dbee.t: ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱯᱟᱥᱱᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱨᱟᱹᱯᱩᱫᱚᱜ᱾
seg.9bce1ed4dbee.back: First spread the rice to cool so the grains don't break.

seg.1f9a348f8750.src: Add the turmeric on low heat and stir for only a few seconds; burnt turmeric turns the rice bitter.
seg.1f9a348f8750.t: ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱩᱢᱩᱝ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱥᱮᱠᱮᱱᱰ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ; ᱡᱟᱹᱞᱤ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱦᱚᱨᱚᱜ ᱮᱫᱟ᱾
seg.1f9a348f8750.back: Add turmeric on low fire and stir just a few seconds; burnt turmeric makes the rice bitter.

seg.394d01a50207.src: Hill turmeric powder colours strongly; start with ½ tsp for 1 cup of rice and add a pinch more only if you want a deeper yellow.
seg.394d01a50207.t: ᱵᱩᱨᱩ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱮᱢᱟ; 1 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱪᱟᱩᱞᱤ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ½ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱛᱮ ᱮᱦᱚᱵ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱜᱟᱲᱦᱟ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱠᱩᱥᱤᱭᱟᱜ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱜᱮ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱤᱢᱴᱤ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.394d01a50207.back: Hill turmeric powder gives a lot of colour; start with ½ small spoon for 1 cup rice and only if you like a deep yellow colour add one more pinch.

seg.505872469eb9.src: Leftover rice from the morning works well, as long as the grains are separate.
seg.505872469eb9.t: ᱥᱟᱹᱠᱟᱹᱞ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱪᱟᱞᱟᱣᱜᱼᱟ, ᱡᱩᱫᱤ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ᱾
seg.505872469eb9.back: Leftover rice from the morning works well, if the grains are separate.

seg.ab1b24f9cf3d.src: Turmeric powder: our everyday Pasupu turmeric powder works the same way; use the same ½ tsp.
seg.ab1b24f9cf3d.t: ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ: ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱯᱟᱥᱩᱯᱩ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱦᱚᱸ ᱚᱱᱟ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱪᱟᱞᱟᱣᱜᱼᱟ; ᱚᱛᱠᱮ ᱜᱮ ½ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.ab1b24f9cf3d.back: Turmeric powder: our everyday pasupu turmeric powder also works in that same way; add the same ½ small spoon.

seg.302f50dc74c9.src: Peanuts: fry 2 tbsp raw peanuts in the oil before the cashews for extra crunch.
seg.302f50dc74c9.t: ᱪᱤᱱᱟ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ: ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱢ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ 2 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱠᱟᱸᱪᱟ ᱪᱤᱱᱟ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.302f50dc74c9.back: Groundnuts: for more crunch fry 2 tablespoons raw groundnuts in oil before the cashews.

seg.551f49339b3d.src: Lemon: squeeze in the juice of half a lemon with the rice for a tangy, pulihora-style rice.
seg.551f49339b3d.t: ᱞᱮᱵᱩ: ᱡᱚᱰ, ᱯᱩᱞᱤᱦᱳᱨᱟ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱟᱫᱷᱟ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱪᱤᱯᱩᱫ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.551f49339b3d.back: Lemon: for a sour, pulihora-like rice squeeze the juice of half a lemon in with the rice.

seg.6b9e9c07efba.src: Coconut: toss in 2 tbsp grated coconut along with the rice.
seg.6b9e9c07efba.t: ᱱᱟᱨᱤᱭᱟᱞ: ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ 2 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱱᱟᱨᱤᱭᱟᱞ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.6b9e9c07efba.back: Coconut: mix 2 big spoons grated coconut with the rice.

seg.d541a1d237fc.src: Serve warm or at room temperature with curd, appadalu or a dry potato fry. It also packs well for lunch boxes and travel.
seg.d541a1d237fc.t: ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱥᱮ ᱠᱚᱴᱷᱨᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱤ, ᱟᱯᱯᱟᱰᱟᱞᱩ ᱥᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱟᱞᱩ ᱵᱷᱟᱡᱤ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱞᱟᱧᱪ ᱵᱟᱠᱥᱚ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱦᱮᱫ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱦᱚᱸ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱵᱟᱸᱫᱷᱟᱣᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.d541a1d237fc.back: Serve a little warm or at room temperature with curd, appadalu or dry potato fry. It also packs well for lunch box and journey.

seg.db97e1ae49fa.src: Best eaten the same day. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 1 day and warm them with a sprinkle of water.
seg.db97e1ae49fa.t: ᱚᱱᱟ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱜᱮ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱡᱟᱹᱥᱛᱤ ᱵᱮᱥ᱾ ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ 1 ᱢᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱪᱤᱴᱟᱹᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.db97e1ae49fa.back: Eating that same day is best. Keep the leftover covered in the fridge up to 1 day and heat sprinkling a little water.

seg.54acb7b11b4c.src: How do you make pasupu annam?

seg.d99d12f26e71.src: Cook rice so the grains stay separate and let it cool. Fry cashews, mustard seeds, chana dal, chillies and curry leaves in oil, add turmeric on low heat for a few seconds, then toss in the rice with salt.
seg.d99d12f26e71.t: ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱭ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ, ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ, ᱵᱩᱴ ᱫᱟᱞ, ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱥᱮᱠᱮᱱᱰ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.d99d12f26e71.back: Cook the rice so the grains stay separate and cool. Fry cashew, mustard seeds, chana dal, chilli and curry leaves in oil, add turmeric on low fire for a few seconds, then mix the rice with salt.

seg.a4a87b4f7d63.src: How much turmeric powder goes into turmeric rice?
seg.a4a87b4f7d63.t: ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱛᱤᱱᱟᱹᱜ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ?
seg.a4a87b4f7d63.back: How much turmeric powder goes in turmeric rice?

seg.aa37527cdcfb.src: About ½ tsp for 1 cup of raw rice (about 3 cups cooked). Hill turmeric powder colours strongly, so start with less and add a pinch more if needed.
seg.aa37527cdcfb.t: 1 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱪᱟᱩᱞᱤ (ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 3 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ) ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ ½ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ᱾ ᱵᱩᱨᱩ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱮᱢᱟ, ᱚᱱᱟᱛᱮ ᱠᱚᱢ ᱛᱮ ᱮᱦᱚᱵ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱤᱢᱴᱤ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.aa37527cdcfb.back: For 1 cup rice (about 3 cups cooked rice) about ½ small spoon. Hill turmeric powder gives a lot of colour, so start with less and if needed add one more pinch.

seg.3d200fb0e6fc.src: Why is my turmeric rice bitter?
seg.3d200fb0e6fc.t: ᱤᱧᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱪᱮᱫᱟᱜ ᱦᱚᱨᱚᱜ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ?
seg.3d200fb0e6fc.back: Why is my turmeric rice bitter?

seg.2c9da3559a42.src: The turmeric burnt in the hot oil, or too much went in. Add it on low heat, stir for only a few seconds and switch off before tipping in the rice.
seg.2c9da3559a42.t: ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱟᱹᱞᱤ ᱮᱱᱟ, ᱥᱮ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱵᱟᱹᱲᱛᱤ ᱮᱢᱮᱱᱟ᱾ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱩᱢᱩᱝ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱥᱮᱠᱮᱱᱰ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.2c9da3559a42.back: The turmeric burnt in the hot oil, or very much was added. Add on low fire, stir just a few seconds and before adding the rice turn off the fire.

seg.36ca370ac0d9.src: Can I make pasupu annam with leftover rice?
seg.36ca370ac0d9.t: ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱛᱮ ᱯᱟᱥᱩᱯᱩ ᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ ᱥᱮ?
seg.36ca370ac0d9.back: Can pasupu annam be made with leftover rice?

seg.71df75edcd26.src: Yes. Leftover rice with separate grains works well. Break up any lumps with your fingers before tossing it in the tempering.
seg.71df75edcd26.t: ᱮᱦᱚᱸ᱾ ᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜ ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱪᱟᱞᱟᱣᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱫᱤᱞᱟ ᱠᱚ ᱛᱤ ᱛᱟᱨᱟᱵ ᱛᱮ ᱨᱟᱹᱯᱩᱫ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.71df75edcd26.back: Yes. Leftover rice with separate grains works well. Before mixing into the tempering break the lumps with the fingertips.

seg.42238d687a8f.t: ᱯᱟᱥᱩᱯᱩ ᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ · ᱯᱟᱥᱩᱯᱩ ᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ | 1acrefarms

seg.720281a9dc26.src: పసుపు అన్నం. Pasupu annam, Andhra turmeric rice: cooked rice tossed in a mustard, chana dal and curry leaf tempering with hill turmeric powder and fried cashews. Serves 4.
seg.720281a9dc26.t: ᱯᱟᱥᱩᱯᱩ ᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ᱾ ᱯᱟᱥᱩᱯᱩ ᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ, ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ: ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ, ᱵᱩᱴ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱩᱨᱩ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ᱾ 4 ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ᱾
seg.720281a9dc26.back: Pasupu Annam. Pasupu annam, Andhra turmeric rice: cooked rice mixed in a tempering of mustard, chana dal and curry leaves with hill turmeric powder and fried cashews. For 4 people.

seg.a5bf108c0e27.src: Pasupu Annam: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.a5bf108c0e27.t: ᱯᱟᱥᱩᱯᱩ ᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ: 1acrefarms ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱠᱟᱨᱰ, ᱡᱤᱱᱤᱥ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ
seg.a5bf108c0e27.back: Pasupu Annam: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and steps

seg.ed1a4a430aee.t: ½ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱵᱩᱨᱩ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ
seg.ed1a4a430aee.back: ½ small spoon hill turmeric powder

seg.cc1333072822.src: Ragi java is a pourable porridge of ragi flour cooked in water, a daily drink in many Andhra and Rayalaseema homes. The salted version is made with buttermilk; this sweet one is loosened with milk and sweetened with jaggery, and it is drunk warm from a steel tumbler at breakfast or in the evening.
seg.cc1333072822.t: ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ ᱫᱚ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱟᱴᱟ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱧᱩ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱯᱚᱛᱞᱟ ᱡᱟᱣ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ, ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱟᱨ ᱨᱟᱭᱚᱞᱟᱥᱤᱢᱟ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱟᱭᱢᱟ ᱚᱲᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱧᱩᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱫᱚ ᱢᱚᱴᱷᱟ ᱛᱮ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣᱚᱜᱼᱟ; ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱫᱚ ᱛᱚᱣᱟ ᱛᱮ ᱯᱚᱛᱞᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱛᱮ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣᱚᱜᱼᱟ, ᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱹᱠᱟᱹᱞ ᱥᱮ ᱟᱭᱩᱵ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱴᱤᱞ ᱴᱟᱢᱵᱞᱟᱨ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱧᱩᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.cc1333072822.back: Ragi java is a thin porridge like a drink of ragi flour cooked in water, drunk every day in many houses of Andhra and Rayalaseema. The salty kind is made with buttermilk; this sweet kind is made thin with milk and sweet with jaggery, and is drunk warm from a steel tumbler in the morning or evening.

seg.b29ec96bcd5c.src: Our Thati Bellam palm jaggery suits the earthy taste of ragi and gives the java a toffee-brown colour. It takes about 15 minutes from start to finish. This recipe serves 2.
seg.b29ec96bcd5c.t: ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱴᱤ ᱵᱮᱞᱞᱟᱢ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱦᱟᱥᱟ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱢᱤᱞᱟᱹᱣᱜᱼᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱴᱚᱯᱷᱤ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱵᱷᱩᱨᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱮᱦᱚᱵ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱢᱩᱪᱟᱹᱫ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 15 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫᱼᱟ᱾ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ 2 ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ᱾
seg.b29ec96bcd5c.back: Our tati bellam palm jaggery blends well with the soil-like taste of ragi and gives the java a toffee-like brown colour. From start to end it takes about 15 minutes. This recipe is for 2 people.

seg.f65620e4f5c4.src: Total includes the 2-minute rest before the jaggery goes in.
seg.f65620e4f5c4.t: ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱮᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ 2 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱥᱮᱞᱮᱫ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.f65620e4f5c4.back: In the total time 2 minutes of keeping before adding jaggery is included.

seg.f0a8282433d4.src: Whisk ragi flour into water, cook it in boiling water till thick and glossy, then add milk. Off the heat, stir in palm jaggery and cardamom.
seg.f0a8282433d4.t: ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱟᱴᱟ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱚᱥᱚᱝ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱚᱞᱚᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱛᱚᱣᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱟᱲᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱟᱨ ᱮᱞᱟᱭᱪᱤ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.f0a8282433d4.back: Mix ragi flour in water stirring, cook in boiling water until thick and shining, then add milk. After taking off the fire mix in palm jaggery and cardamom.

seg.41bd564147d7.src: ¼ cup ragi flour ⟦1⟧finger millet flour, about 35 g⟦/1⟧
seg.41bd564147d7.t: ¼ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱟᱴᱟ ⟦1⟧ᱢᱟᱲᱩᱣᱟ ᱟᱴᱟ, ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 35 g⟦/1⟧
seg.41bd564147d7.back: ¼ cup ragi flour ⟦1⟧madua flour, about 35 g⟦/1⟧

seg.d9504b3b8592.src: 2 cups water ⟦1⟧1 cup to mix the flour, 1 cup to boil⟦/1⟧
seg.d9504b3b8592.t: 2 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ⟦1⟧1 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱟᱴᱟ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ, 1 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱚᱥᱚᱝ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ⟦/1⟧
seg.d9504b3b8592.back: 2 cups water ⟦1⟧1 cup for mixing the flour, 1 cup for boiling⟦/1⟧

seg.0570314748ee.src: 3 tbsp grated palm jaggery ⟦1⟧about 30 g; add a spoon more if you like it sweeter⟦/1⟧
seg.0570314748ee.t: 3 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ⟦1⟧ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 30 g; ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱠᱩᱥᱤᱭᱟᱜ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ⟦/1⟧
seg.0570314748ee.back: 3 big spoons grated palm jaggery ⟦1⟧about 30 g; if you like more sweet one more spoon⟦/1⟧

seg.2b7de8d37fd0.src: Put the ragi flour in a bowl.
seg.2b7de8d37fd0.t: ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱟᱴᱟ ᱢᱤᱫᱴᱟᱝ ᱵᱟᱴᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.2b7de8d37fd0.back: Put the ragi flour in a bowl.

seg.fce6db4082ef.src: Whisk the ragi flour into 1 cup water till smooth, with no lumps. Use a whisk or a fork and break up any lumps against the side of the bowl.
seg.fce6db4082ef.t: ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱟᱴᱟ 1 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ, ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱱ ᱫᱤᱞᱟ ᱵᱟᱝ᱾ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱥᱮ ᱠᱟᱸᱴᱟ ᱵᱮᱵᱷᱟᱨ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱤᱞᱟ ᱠᱚ ᱵᱟᱴᱤ ᱜᱟᱫᱮᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱨᱟᱹᱯᱩᱫ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.fce6db4082ef.back: Stir the ragi flour in 1 cup of water until smooth, no lumps at all. Use a whisk or fork and break the lumps on the side of the bowl.

seg.ac6b0e0e7003.src: Pour the remaining 1 cup of water into a heavy-bottomed pan and set it on medium heat.
seg.ac6b0e0e7003.t: ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ 1 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱦᱟᱭᱟᱹᱠ ᱞᱟᱛᱟᱨ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.ac6b0e0e7003.back: Pour the remaining 1 cup of water into a heavy-bottomed pan and keep on medium fire.

seg.ec55acf2b96a.src: Boil the other cup of water, pour in the ragi and stir on low heat till thick and glossy, 6–8 minutes. Stir the mix once more before pouring, as the flour settles at the bottom of the bowl.
seg.ec55acf2b96a.t: ᱮᱴᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱚᱥᱚᱝ ᱢᱮ, ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱚᱞᱚᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ, 6–8 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ᱾ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ, ᱪᱮᱫᱟᱜ ᱥᱮ ᱟᱴᱟ ᱵᱟᱴᱤ ᱞᱟᱛᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱩᱵᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.ec55acf2b96a.back: Boil the other cup of water, pour in the ragi and stir on low fire until thick and shining, 6–8 minutes. Before pouring stir the mixture once more, because the flour sinks to the bottom of the bowl.

seg.d0f8efa78d43.src: Keep stirring all the time. The java is cooked when it turns from dull pinkish-brown to a darker, glossy brown and coats the back of the spoon.
seg.d0f8efa78d43.t: ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱛᱮ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱢᱚᱞᱤᱱ ᱜᱩᱞᱟᱹᱵᱤ-ᱵᱷᱩᱨᱟ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ, ᱡᱚᱞᱚᱜ ᱵᱷᱩᱨᱟ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱥᱮᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱚᱜ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ᱾
seg.d0f8efa78d43.back: Keep stirring all the time. When from dull pinkish-brown it becomes darker, shining brown, and coats the back of the spoon, the java is cooked.

seg.e7ef07a808c5.src: Add the milk and simmer 2 minutes. Switch off and rest 2 minutes. Stir once or twice while it simmers so it does not catch.
seg.e7ef07a808c5.t: ᱛᱚᱣᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ 2 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ 2 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱵᱟᱨ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱞᱟᱛᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣᱜ᱾
seg.e7ef07a808c5.back: Add the milk and cook 2 minutes on low fire. After turning off the fire keep 2 minutes. While cooking stir once or twice so it does not stick at the bottom.

seg.8f86db3a6d08.src: Grate the palm jaggery finely while the java rests, so it melts quickly.
seg.8f86db3a6d08.t: ᱡᱟᱣᱟ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱵᱟᱨᱤᱠ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱞᱚᱜᱚᱱ ᱞᱤᱞᱤᱭᱚᱜ᱾
seg.8f86db3a6d08.back: While the java rests grate the palm jaggery fine so it melts quickly.

seg.9cad3a0176bc.src: Stir in the palm jaggery and cardamom. Serve warm. Stir till the jaggery has fully melted, then taste and add a little more if needed.
seg.9cad3a0176bc.t: ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱟᱨ ᱮᱞᱟᱭᱪᱤ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱯᱩᱨᱟᱹ ᱞᱤᱞᱤ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱧᱮᱞ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.9cad3a0176bc.back: Mix in the palm jaggery and cardamom. Serve warm. Stir until the jaggery fully melts, then taste and if needed add a little more.

seg.a8de8fe6382d.src: Pour into tumblers or bowls. If it is too thick to drink, stir in a few spoons of warm milk.
seg.a8de8fe6382d.t: ᱴᱟᱢᱵᱞᱟᱨ ᱥᱮ ᱵᱟᱴᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱧᱩ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱛᱚᱣᱟ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.a8de8fe6382d.back: Pour into a tumbler or bowl. If very thick for drinking mix in a few spoons of warm milk.

seg.c3916a972329.src: Always mix the ragi flour in water first; flour added straight to boiling water forms lumps that do not break up.
seg.c3916a972329.t: ᱡᱟᱣᱜᱮ ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱟᱴᱟ ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ; ᱥᱤᱫᱷᱟ ᱚᱥᱚᱝ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱟᱴᱟ ᱫᱚ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱨᱟᱹᱯᱩᱫᱚᱜ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱫᱤᱞᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣᱟ᱾
seg.c3916a972329.back: Always mix the ragi flour first in water; flour put directly into boiling water makes lumps that do not break.

seg.966098732312.src: Do not rush the cooking; undercooked ragi tastes raw and floury.
seg.966098732312.t: ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱲᱵᱚᱲᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ; ᱟᱫᱷᱟ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱠᱟᱸᱪᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱟᱴᱟ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.966098732312.back: Don't hurry the cooking; half-cooked ragi tastes raw and floury.

seg.7c0f350f3691.src: For a thinner java to drink from a tumbler, use 2 tbsp ragi flour; for a spoonable porridge, use ⅓ cup.
seg.7c0f350f3691.t: ᱴᱟᱢᱵᱞᱟᱨ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱧᱩ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱯᱚᱛᱞᱟ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 2 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱟᱴᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ; ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱛᱮ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱡᱟᱣ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ⅓ ᱠᱟᱯ᱾
seg.7c0f350f3691.back: From the tumbler, for a thin java for drinking add 2 big spoons ragi flour; for a porridge to eat with a spoon ⅓ cup.

seg.146636ba6c2e.src: With dry fruit: stir in a few chopped cashews or almonds and a spoon of raisins at the end.
seg.146636ba6c2e.t: ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱡᱚ ᱥᱟᱶ: ᱢᱩᱪᱟᱹᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱥᱮ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱠᱤᱥᱢᱤᱥ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.146636ba6c2e.back: With dry fruits: at the end mix in a few cut cashews or nuts (badam) and a spoon of raisins.

seg.6fc3ada569ad.src: Without milk: cook the ragi in 2½ cups water and stir in the jaggery once it has stopped bubbling, for a thinner, darker java.
seg.6fc3ada569ad.t: ᱛᱚᱣᱟ ᱵᱤᱱ: ᱨᱟᱜᱤ 2½ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱰᱵᱩᱰ ᱛᱷᱟᱢᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱯᱚᱛᱞᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ᱾
seg.6fc3ada569ad.back: Without milk: cook the ragi in 2½ cups of water and after the bubbling stops mix in the jaggery, for a thin and darker java.

seg.639ea388ead3.src: Serve warm in a steel tumbler or bowl for breakfast, or as an evening drink with a few biscuits or murukulu. Some like it chilled in summer.
seg.639ea388ead3.t: ᱥᱟᱹᱠᱟᱹᱞ ᱡᱚᱢᱟᱜ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱥᱴᱤᱞ ᱴᱟᱢᱵᱞᱟᱨ ᱥᱮ ᱵᱟᱴᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱮ ᱟᱭᱩᱵ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱵᱤᱥᱠᱩᱴ ᱥᱮ ᱢᱩᱨᱩᱠᱩᱞᱩ ᱥᱟᱶ᱾ ᱛᱤᱱᱟᱹᱜ ᱦᱚᱲ ᱥᱤᱛᱩᱝ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱠᱩᱥᱤᱭᱟᱠᱟ᱾
seg.639ea388ead3.back: For a morning meal serve warm in a steel tumbler or bowl, or in the evening with a few biscuits or murukulu. Many people like it cooled in summer.

seg.e770a9eec01e.src: Best drunk the day it is made. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 1 day and stir in a little warm milk, off the heat, when reheating.
seg.e770a9eec01e.t: ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱜᱮ ᱧᱩ ᱡᱟᱹᱥᱛᱤ ᱵᱮᱥ᱾ ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ 1 ᱢᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱩᱦᱲᱟᱹ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱟᱲᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱛᱚᱣᱟ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.e770a9eec01e.back: Drinking on the day of making is best. Keep the leftover covered in the fridge up to 1 day and when reheating take off the fire and mix in a little warm milk little by little.

seg.a10b6147a5ac.src: How do I make ragi java without lumps?
seg.a10b6147a5ac.t: ᱫᱤᱞᱟ ᱵᱤᱱ ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ ᱪᱮᱫ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ?
seg.a10b6147a5ac.back: How can ragi java be made without lumps?

seg.ca8628b7e082.src: Whisk the ragi flour into room-temperature water first until smooth, then pour this into boiling water while stirring all the time.
seg.ca8628b7e082.t: ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱟᱴᱟ ᱠᱚᱴᱷᱨᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱚᱥᱚᱝ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.ca8628b7e082.back: First stir the ragi flour in room-temperature water until smooth, then pour it into boiling water stirring all the time.

seg.8bd78affc52d.src: How do I know ragi java is cooked?
seg.8bd78affc52d.t: ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱮᱱᱟ ᱪᱮᱫ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱵᱟᱰᱟᱭ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ?
seg.8bd78affc52d.back: How can one know ragi java is cooked?

seg.9b05db7490cb.src: It turns darker and glossy, thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon, and no longer tastes floury. This takes about 6–8 minutes on low heat.
seg.9b05db7490cb.t: ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱚᱞᱚᱜ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ, ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱥᱮᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡᱚᱜᱼᱟ, ᱟᱨ ᱟᱴᱟ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱭᱟ᱾ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 6–8 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫᱼᱟ᱾
seg.9b05db7490cb.back: It becomes darker and shining, thickens to coat the back of the spoon, and does not taste floury. On low fire it takes about 6–8 minutes.

seg.6d748d67adfb.src: Can I use palm jaggery in ragi java?
seg.6d748d67adfb.t: ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱵᱮᱵᱷᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ ᱥᱮ?
seg.6d748d67adfb.back: Can palm jaggery be used in ragi java?

seg.06e768643767.src: Yes. Grate the palm jaggery (thati bellam) finely and stir it in after switching off the stove, so the milk does not split. It gives a deeper colour and a slightly smoky sweetness.
seg.06e768643767.t: ᱮᱦᱚᱸ᱾ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ (ᱛᱟᱴᱤ ᱵᱮᱞᱞᱟᱢ) ᱵᱟᱨᱤᱠ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱪᱩᱞᱦᱟᱹ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱛᱚᱣᱟ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱯᱷᱟᱴᱟᱜ᱾ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱜᱟᱲᱦᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱫᱷᱩᱸᱣᱟᱹ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.06e768643767.back: Yes. Grate the palm jaggery (tati bellam) fine and mix after turning off the stove, so the milk does not split. It gives deep colour and a slightly smoky-like sweetness.

seg.9a71713417de.src: What is the difference between ragi java and ragi malt?
seg.9a71713417de.t: ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱢᱟᱞᱴ ᱨᱮ ᱪᱮᱫ ᱯᱷᱟᱨᱟᱠ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ?
seg.9a71713417de.back: What difference is there between ragi java and ragi malt?

seg.c2632b6d0b4f.src: They are the same drink with different names. Ragi java is the Telugu name; ragi malt is what it is often called in shops and on menus.
seg.c2632b6d0b4f.t: ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱫᱚ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱜᱮ ᱧᱩ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ, ᱧᱩᱛᱩᱢ ᱜᱮ ᱮᱴᱟᱜ᱾ ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ ᱫᱚ ᱛᱮᱞᱩᱜᱩ ᱧᱩᱛᱩᱢ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ; ᱫᱩᱠᱟᱹᱱ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱮᱱᱩ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱭᱢᱟ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱢᱟᱞᱴ ᱢᱮᱱᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.c2632b6d0b4f.back: This is one same drink, only the name is different. Ragi java is the Telugu name; in shops and menus it is many times called ragi malt.

seg.6134777fbfa8.src: రాగి జావ · Sweet Ragi Java Recipe | 1acrefarms
seg.6134777fbfa8.t: ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ · ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ | 1acrefarms
seg.6134777fbfa8.back: Ragi Java · Sweet ragi java recipe | 1acrefarms

seg.708e3c523d72.src: రాగి జావ. Sweet ragi java, the Andhra way: ragi flour cooked in water till glossy, loosened with milk and sweetened with Thati Bellam palm jaggery. Method and tips.
seg.708e3c523d72.t: ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ᱾ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ: ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱟᱴᱟ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱚᱞᱚᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ, ᱛᱚᱣᱟ ᱛᱮ ᱯᱚᱛᱞᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱛᱟᱴᱤ ᱵᱮᱞᱞᱟᱢ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱛᱮ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ᱾ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱹᱢᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱛᱷᱟ᱾
seg.708e3c523d72.back: Ragi Java. Andhra-style sweet ragi java: ragi flour cooked in water until shining, made thin with milk and sweetened with tati bellam palm jaggery. Recipe and tips.

seg.2889ed2cf93b.src: Ragi Java: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.2889ed2cf93b.t: ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ: 1acrefarms ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱠᱟᱨᱰ, ᱡᱤᱱᱤᱥ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ
seg.2889ed2cf93b.back: Ragi Java: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and steps

seg.8ee2205b2e8b.t: 3 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ

seg.7dee83c87fea.t: ᱥᱟᱢᱩᱫᱽᱨᱚ ᱫᱷᱟᱨᱮ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱩᱛᱩ · 4 ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ
seg.7dee83c87fea.back: Curry of the seaside · for 4 people

seg.671d48882eed.src: Iguru is the Andhra way of cooking meat or prawns down in a thick onion masala until almost dry, so the spices cling to every piece. Royyala iguru comes from the coastal districts, from Nellore to Godavari to Srikakulam, where prawns from the backwaters and the sea are a Sunday lunch with rice.
seg.671d48882eed.t: ᱤᱜᱩᱨᱩ ᱫᱚ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱚᱱᱟ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱥᱮ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱯᱟᱥᱤ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱚᱜᱼᱟ, ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣᱜ᱾ ᱨᱳᱭᱭᱟᱞᱟ ᱤᱜᱩᱨᱩ ᱫᱚ ᱥᱟᱢᱩᱫᱽᱨᱚ ᱫᱷᱟᱨᱮ ᱡᱤᱞᱟ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱦᱤᱡᱩᱜ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ, ᱱᱮᱞᱚᱨ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱜᱳᱫᱟᱵᱟᱨᱤ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱨᱤᱠᱟᱠᱩᱞᱟᱢ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ, ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱮᱠᱣᱟᱴᱟᱨ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱢᱩᱫᱽᱨᱚ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱥᱤᱸᱜᱮ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱛᱤᱥ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱡᱚᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.671d48882eed.back: Iguru is that Andhra way in which meat or prawns are cooked in thick onion masala until all dry, so the masala sticks on every piece. Royyala iguru comes from the seaside districts, from Nellore up to Godavari and Srikakulam, where backwater and sea prawns are eaten with rice on Sunday afternoons.

seg.ff39877dbdbd.src: Our hill turmeric powder (Konda Pasupu) goes on the prawns first and into the masala. Teja chilli powder brings the deep red colour and strong heat coastal homes like, so scale it to your table.
seg.ff39877dbdbd.t: ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱩᱨᱩ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ (ᱠᱚᱱᱰᱟ ᱯᱟᱥᱩᱯᱩ) ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱚᱱᱟ ᱜᱟᱲᱦᱟ ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱥᱟᱢᱩᱫᱽᱨᱚ ᱫᱷᱟᱨᱮ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱚᱲᱟᱜ ᱠᱚ ᱠᱩᱥᱤᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ, ᱚᱱᱟᱛᱮ ᱟᱢᱟᱜ ᱡᱚᱢᱟᱜ ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱠᱚᱢ ᱵᱟᱹᱲᱛᱤ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.ff39877dbdbd.back: Our hill turmeric powder (konda pasupu) goes first on the prawns and then in the masala. Teja chilli powder gives it deep red colour and strong heat which seaside houses like, so reduce or increase according to the people eating with you.

seg.885826f68de3.src: Prep includes cleaning the prawns and the 10-minute rest with turmeric.
seg.885826f68de3.t: ᱛᱮᱭᱟᱨ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ 10 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱥᱮᱞᱮᱫ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.885826f68de3.back: In the preparation time 10 minutes of keeping the prawns after cleaning with turmeric is included.

seg.cff5bbd725a6.src: Rub prawns with turmeric and salt. Fry onions and ginger-garlic paste, add Teja chilli powder and coriander powder, then cook the prawns in the masala till it coats them.
seg.cff5bbd725a6.t: ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱢᱟᱠᱷᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ ᱟᱨ ᱟᱫᱟ-ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱯᱮᱥᱴ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱷᱚᱱᱤᱭᱟ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣᱜ᱾
seg.cff5bbd725a6.back: Marinate the prawns with turmeric and salt. Fry onion and ginger-garlic paste, add Teja chilli powder and coriander powder, then cook the prawns in the masala until the masala sticks.

seg.cf489166a3fd.src: 500 g prawns ⟦1⟧medium size, shelled and deveined, weighed after cleaning⟦/1⟧
seg.cf489166a3fd.t: 500 g ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ⟦1⟧ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱢᱟᱯ, ᱪᱷᱚᱞᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ ᱥᱤᱨᱟ ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ, ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱡᱚᱠᱷᱟ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ⟦/1⟧
seg.cf489166a3fd.back: 500 g prawns ⟦1⟧medium size, shell and black vein removed, weighed after cleaning⟦/1⟧

seg.141eb60cb009.src: ¾ tsp salt ⟦1⟧divided, or to taste⟦/1⟧
seg.141eb60cb009.t: ¾ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ⟦1⟧ᱵᱟᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱴᱤᱧ ᱨᱮ, ᱥᱮ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ⟦/1⟧
seg.141eb60cb009.back: ¾ small spoon salt ⟦1⟧in two parts, or according to taste⟦/1⟧

seg.8c4c1b789de7.t: 3 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ⟦1⟧ᱥᱟᱫᱷᱟᱨᱚᱱ ᱛᱮ ᱪᱤᱱᱟ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ⟦/1⟧

seg.38eba91a0c15.t: 2 ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ ⟦1⟧ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱢᱟᱯ, ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ⟦/1⟧

seg.d4841433219c.t: 1 ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ (ᱢᱚᱱ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ) ⟦1⟧ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ, ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ⟦/1⟧
seg.d4841433219c.back: 1 tomato (as you wish) ⟦1⟧small, cut small small⟦/1⟧

seg.716dc45cf0b3.src: ½ tsp hill turmeric powder ⟦1⟧Konda Pasupu; ¼ tsp for the prawns, ¼ tsp for the masala⟦/1⟧
seg.716dc45cf0b3.t: ½ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱵᱩᱨᱩ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ⟦1⟧ᱠᱚᱱᱰᱟ ᱯᱟᱥᱩᱯᱩ; ¼ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ, ¼ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ⟦/1⟧
seg.716dc45cf0b3.back: ½ small spoon hill turmeric powder ⟦1⟧konda pasupu; ¼ small spoon for the prawns, ¼ small spoon for the masala⟦/1⟧

seg.f7ec1e72abc0.src: 1½ tsp Teja chilli powder ⟦1⟧very hot; use 1 tsp for medium heat, ½ tsp for mild⟦/1⟧
seg.f7ec1e72abc0.t: 1½ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ⟦1⟧ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ; ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ, ᱦᱟᱞᱠᱟᱹ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ½ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ⟦/1⟧
seg.f7ec1e72abc0.back: 1½ small spoons Teja chilli powder ⟦1⟧very hot; for medium heat 1 small spoon, for light ½ small spoon⟦/1⟧

seg.fce641038ff4.src: Shell and devein the prawns, rinse them well and drain in a colander.
seg.fce641038ff4.t: ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱪᱷᱚᱞᱟ ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ ᱥᱤᱨᱟ ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱢᱮ, ᱵᱮᱥ ᱛᱮ ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱪᱷᱟᱹᱱᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱧᱩᱨ ᱦᱤᱡᱩᱜ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.fce641038ff4.back: Remove the shell of the prawns and remove the black vein, clean well and drain the water in a strainer.

seg.152d1d89f6a5.src: Rub the prawns with half the turmeric and a little salt; set aside 10 minutes. Use ¼ tsp turmeric and ¼ tsp of the salt.
seg.152d1d89f6a5.t: ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱫᱷᱟ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱢᱟᱠᱷᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ; 10 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱫᱷᱟᱨᱮ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾ ¼ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱟᱨ ¼ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱦᱟᱛᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.152d1d89f6a5.back: Marinate the prawns with half the turmeric and a little salt; keep aside 10 minutes. Take ¼ small spoon turmeric and ¼ small spoon salt.

seg.9e027c56020d.src: Heat the oil in a heavy kadai on medium heat and add the mustard seeds. When they splutter, add the green chillies and curry leaves.
seg.9e027c56020d.t: ᱦᱟᱭᱟᱹᱠ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱦᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱥᱟᱰᱮ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.9e027c56020d.back: Heat oil in a heavy kadai on medium fire and add mustard seeds. When they crackle add green chilli and curry leaves.

seg.5d608fabeb97.src: Fry the onions in the oil till golden, then the ginger-garlic paste till it smells cooked. The onions take about 8–10 minutes; the paste about 1 minute, until the raw smell goes.
seg.5d608fabeb97.t: ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱟᱫᱟ-ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱯᱮᱥᱴ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱥᱩᱜᱚᱫ ᱦᱤᱡᱩᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ᱾ ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 8–10 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫᱼᱟ; ᱯᱮᱥᱴ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 1 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ, ᱠᱟᱸᱪᱟ ᱥᱩᱜᱚᱫ ᱪᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ᱾
seg.5d608fabeb97.back: Fry the onion in oil until gold colour, then the ginger-garlic paste until a cooked smell comes. The onion takes about 8–10 minutes; the paste about 1 minute, until the raw smell goes.

seg.7677bdc79559.src: If using the tomato, add it now and cook until soft and pulpy, about 4 minutes.
seg.7677bdc79559.t: ᱡᱩᱫᱤ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱱᱟᱢ, ᱱᱤᱛᱚᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱤᱞᱤ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ, ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 4 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ᱾
seg.7677bdc79559.back: If you are adding tomato, add now and cook until soft and melted, about 4 minutes.

seg.5aff56b73c8a.src: Turn the heat to low. Add the rest of the turmeric, Teja chilli powder and coriander powder; fry 1 minute. Add the remaining salt and stir so the spices do not catch.
seg.5aff56b73c8a.t: ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ, ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱷᱚᱱᱤᱭᱟ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ; 1 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱞᱟᱛᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣᱜ᱾
seg.5aff56b73c8a.back: Lower the fire. Add the remaining turmeric, Teja chilli powder and coriander powder; fry 1 minute. Stir after adding the remaining salt so the masala does not stick at the bottom.

seg.ba25fbb9cf98.src: Pour in the water and cook the masala on medium heat until the oil starts to separate at the edges, about 3–4 minutes.
seg.ba25fbb9cf98.t: ᱫᱟᱜ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱜᱟᱫᱮᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱮᱦᱚᱵᱚᱜ, ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 3–4 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ᱾
seg.ba25fbb9cf98.back: Pour water and cook the masala on medium fire until oil separates at the edges, about 3–4 minutes.

seg.e60a6389cdf2.src: Add the prawns and cook till they curl and turn pink, 5–6 minutes. Finish with garam masala. Stir often on medium-high heat so the masala dries and coats the prawns.
seg.e60a6389cdf2.t: ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱜᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱟᱨ ᱜᱩᱞᱟᱹᱵᱤ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ, 5–6 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ᱾ ᱢᱩᱪᱟᱹᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱟᱨᱚᱢ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ-ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱭᱢᱟ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲᱚᱜ ᱟᱨ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣᱜ᱾
seg.e60a6389cdf2.back: Add the prawns and cook until they curl and become pink colour, 5–6 minutes. At the end add garam masala. On medium-high fire stir many times so the masala dries and sticks on the prawns.

seg.af87e48d1429.src: Check doneness: prawns are cooked when they are pink and opaque all the way through and curled into a loose C. Cut one open if unsure; there should be no grey, see-through centre.
seg.af87e48d1429.t: ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱧᱮᱞ ᱢᱮ: ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱜᱩᱞᱟᱹᱵᱤ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱟᱨᱯᱟᱨ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱧᱮᱞᱚᱜ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ, ᱟᱨ ᱞᱟᱦᱟᱭ C ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱜᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱮᱫᱚᱜ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱚᱜ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ᱾ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱵᱟᱰᱟᱭ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱢᱤᱫᱴᱟᱝ ᱜᱮᱫ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱧᱮᱞ ᱢᱮ; ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱱ ᱜᱽᱨᱮ ᱨᱚᱝ, ᱠᱟᱸᱪ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱟᱨᱯᱟᱨ ᱧᱮᱞᱚᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱴᱤᱧ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ᱾
seg.af87e48d1429.back: Check doneness: prawns are cooked when they turn pink all the way inside and are not see-through, and curl gently like a C. If unsure, cut one and look; in the centre there should be no grey, glass-like see-through part.

seg.32e58c09609e.src: Taste for salt, scatter the coriander leaves and switch off. Do not keep cooking once the prawns are done, or they turn rubbery.
seg.32e58c09609e.t: ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱧᱮᱞ ᱢᱮ, ᱫᱷᱚᱱᱤᱭᱟ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱪᱤᱴᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱟᱨ ᱟᱞᱚᱢ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱟ, ᱵᱟᱝᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱨᱟᱵᱟᱲ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.32e58c09609e.back: Taste the salt, sprinkle coriander leaves and turn off the fire. After the prawns are cooked do not cook any more, otherwise they become hard like rubber.

seg.89a9cb293875.src: Teja is very hot: 1½ tsp makes a fiery iguru the way coastal homes like it; use 1 tsp for medium heat, or ½ tsp for mild.
seg.89a9cb293875.t: ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱜᱮᱭᱟ: 1½ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱛᱮ ᱥᱟᱢᱩᱫᱽᱨᱚ ᱫᱷᱟᱨᱮ ᱚᱲᱟᱜ ᱠᱚᱣᱟᱜ ᱠᱩᱥᱤ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱤᱜᱩᱨᱩ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ; ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ, ᱥᱮ ᱦᱟᱞᱠᱟᱹ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ½ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.89a9cb293875.back: Teja is very hot: with 1½ small spoons the iguru becomes hot as the seaside houses like; for medium heat add 1 small spoon, or for light ½ small spoon.

seg.095c6105ce36.src: Fry the onions until properly golden; the colour and body of an iguru come from well-browned onions.
seg.095c6105ce36.t: ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ ᱯᱩᱨᱟᱹ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ; ᱤᱜᱩᱨᱩ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱫᱚ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱵᱷᱩᱨᱟ ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱦᱤᱡᱩᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.095c6105ce36.back: Fry the onion fully until gold colour; the colour and thickness of the iguru come from well-browned onion.

seg.04fb6307d058.src: Prawns cook fast. A loose C shape means done; a tight O means overcooked and chewy.
seg.04fb6307d058.t: ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱞᱚᱜᱚᱱ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱞᱟᱦᱟᱭ C ᱨᱩᱯ ᱢᱮᱱ ᱛᱮ ᱛᱮᱭᱟᱨ; ᱯᱩᱨᱟᱹ ᱜᱩᱴᱩᱢ O ᱨᱩᱯ ᱢᱮᱱ ᱛᱮ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱵᱟᱹᱲᱛᱤ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱮᱱᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱨᱟᱵᱟᱲ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱦᱩᱭᱮᱱᱟ᱾
seg.04fb6307d058.back: Prawns cook quickly. Gentle C shape means ready; fully curled O shape means very overcooked and they become hard like rubber.

seg.a5e6a832090a.src: Pat the prawns dry after rinsing so they fry in the masala instead of stewing in water.
seg.a5e6a832090a.t: ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱪᱟᱯᱟᱹᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱤᱡᱩ ᱵᱚᱫᱚᱞ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤᱭᱚᱜ᱾
seg.a5e6a832090a.back: After cleaning press the prawns dry so they fry in the masala instead of boiling in water.

seg.4145e1ca56b5.src: Gongura royyalu: stir in ½ cup gongura leaves, wilted in a little oil and mashed, with the prawns.
seg.4145e1ca56b5.t: ᱜᱳᱝᱜᱩᱨᱟ ᱨᱳᱭᱭᱟᱞᱩ: ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱥᱟᱶ ½ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱜᱳᱝᱜᱩᱨᱟ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ, ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱤᱞᱤ ᱟᱨ ᱜᱷᱟᱸᱴᱩᱣᱟᱹ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ, ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.4145e1ca56b5.back: Gongura royyalu: with the prawns mix ½ cup gongura leaves, melted and mashed in a little oil.

seg.e52b316e5c51.src: Coconut: add 2 tbsp grated coconut or 3 tbsp thick coconut milk in the last 2 minutes for a softer, richer masala.
seg.e52b316e5c51.t: ᱱᱟᱨᱤᱭᱟᱞ: ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱟᱨ ᱜᱟᱲᱦᱟ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱢᱩᱪᱟᱹᱫ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ 2 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱨᱮ 2 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱱᱟᱨᱤᱭᱟᱞ ᱥᱮ 3 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱱᱟᱨᱤᱭᱟᱞ ᱛᱚᱣᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.e52b316e5c51.back: Coconut: for a softer and deeper-flavoured masala, in the last 2 minutes add 2 tablespoons grated coconut or 3 tablespoons thick coconut milk.

seg.fc55c7b1a788.src: Gravy style: add ¾ cup water after the prawns for a thinner royyala kura to pour over rice.
seg.fc55c7b1a788.t: ᱡᱩᱞ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ: ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱪᱮᱛᱟᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱯᱚᱛᱞᱟ ᱨᱳᱭᱭᱟᱞᱟ ᱠᱩᱨᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ¾ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.fc55c7b1a788.back: Gravy-like: for a thin royyala kura for pouring over rice add ¾ cup of water after the prawns.

seg.8ccb6d545dd0.src: Serve hot with steamed rice and a spoon of ghee, or with rasam or sambar rice. It also goes well with chapati.
seg.8ccb6d545dd0.t: ᱥᱤᱡᱩ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱮ ᱨᱟᱥᱚᱢ ᱥᱮ ᱥᱟᱢᱵᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ᱾ ᱪᱟᱯᱟᱛᱤ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱦᱚᱸ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫᱼᱟ᱾
seg.8ccb6d545dd0.back: Serve hot with boiled rice and a spoon of ghee, or with rasam or sambar rice. It is also good with chapati.

seg.d51021b311d0.src: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 1 day. Warm gently in a pan; long reheating makes the prawns tough.
seg.d51021b311d0.t: ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ 1 ᱢᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ; ᱡᱤᱞᱤᱧ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱫᱩᱦᱲᱟᱹ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.d51021b311d0.back: Keep the leftover covered in the fridge and eat within 1 day. Heat in a pan on low fire; if reheated a long time the prawns become hard.

seg.8381d6ac4e4f.src: How do I know when prawns are cooked?
seg.8381d6ac4e4f.t: ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱮᱱᱟ ᱪᱮᱫ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱵᱟᱰᱟᱭ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ?
seg.8381d6ac4e4f.back: How can one know the prawns are cooked?

seg.45cd36ecb77b.src: They turn pink and opaque all the way through and curl into a loose C shape, usually in 5–6 minutes in the hot masala. A grey, see-through centre means they need a little longer.
seg.45cd36ecb77b.t: ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱜᱩᱞᱟᱹᱵᱤ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱟᱨᱯᱟᱨ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱧᱮᱞᱚᱜᱼᱟ, ᱟᱨ ᱞᱟᱦᱟᱭ C ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱜᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱮᱫᱚᱜᱼᱟ, ᱥᱟᱫᱷᱟᱨᱚᱱ ᱛᱮ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱨᱮ 5–6 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱨᱮ᱾ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱽᱨᱮ ᱨᱚᱝ, ᱠᱟᱸᱪ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱟᱨᱯᱟᱨ ᱧᱮᱞᱚᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱴᱤᱧ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ᱾
seg.45cd36ecb77b.back: They turn pink all the way inside and are not see-through, and curl gently like a C, usually in 5–6 minutes in the hot masala. If there is a grey, glass-like see-through part in the centre, they need to cook a little more.

seg.2e4c4a4632d7.src: What is the difference between iguru and vepudu?
seg.2e4c4a4632d7.t: ᱤᱜᱩᱨᱩ ᱟᱨ ᱣᱮᱯᱩᱰᱩ ᱨᱮ ᱪᱮᱫ ᱯᱷᱟᱨᱟᱠ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ?
seg.2e4c4a4632d7.back: What difference is there between iguru and vepudu?
