seg.1ee73f38a967.src: Iguru is cooked down in an onion masala until thick and almost dry, with the masala clinging to the prawns. Vepudu is a fry, with less or no onion gravy, cooked until the prawns are crisp at the edges.
seg.1ee73f38a967.t: ᱤᱜᱩᱨᱩ ᱫᱚ ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱟᱨ ᱯᱟᱥᱤ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱚᱜᱼᱟ, ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ᱾ ᱣᱮᱯᱩᱰᱩ ᱫᱚ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ, ᱠᱚᱢ ᱥᱮ ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ ᱡᱩᱞ ᱵᱤᱱ, ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱜᱟᱫᱮᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱢᱚᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.1ee73f38a967.back: Iguru is cooked in onion masala until thick and all dry, with the masala sticking on the prawns. Vepudu is a fry, with little or no onion gravy, cooked until the prawn edges become crisp.

seg.d248a2970455.src: How can I make royyala iguru less spicy?
seg.d248a2970455.t: ᱨᱳᱭᱭᱟᱞᱟ ᱤᱜᱩᱨᱩ ᱪᱮᱫ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱠᱚᱢ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ?
seg.d248a2970455.back: How can royyala iguru be made less hot?

seg.8c9c12b68361.src: Use 1 tsp Teja chilli powder for medium heat or ½ tsp for mild, and skip the green chillies. A tablespoon of curd or coconut milk at the end also softens the heat.
seg.8c9c12b68361.t: ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱥᱮ ᱦᱟᱞᱠᱟᱹ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ½ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱟᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱟᱞᱚᱢ ᱮᱢᱟ᱾ ᱢᱩᱪᱟᱹᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱫᱚᱦᱤ ᱥᱮ ᱱᱟᱨᱤᱭᱟᱞ ᱛᱚᱣᱟ ᱦᱚᱸ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱮᱫᱟ᱾
seg.8c9c12b68361.back: For medium heat add 1 small spoon of Teja chilli powder or for light ½ small spoon, and don't add green chilli. At the end a big spoon of curd or coconut milk also softens the heat.

seg.d024c66a11b8.t: ᱵᱚᱨᱚᱯᱷ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱵᱮᱵᱷᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ ᱥᱮ?

seg.9cd9740c2604.src: Yes. Thaw them in the fridge, drain them well and pat them dry before rubbing with turmeric and salt. Frozen prawns release more water, so cook the masala a little longer.
seg.9cd9740c2604.t: ᱮᱦᱚᱸ᱾ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱤᱞᱤ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱵᱮᱥ ᱛᱮ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱧᱩᱨ ᱦᱤᱡᱩᱜ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱢᱟᱠᱷᱟᱣ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱪᱟᱯᱟᱹᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱵᱚᱨᱚᱯᱷ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱵᱟᱹᱲᱛᱤ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱚᱰᱚᱠᱟ, ᱚᱱᱟᱛᱮ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.9cd9740c2604.back: Yes. Thaw in the fridge, drain the water well and before marinating with turmeric and salt press dry. Frozen prawns give out more water, so cook the masala a little more.

seg.3120e29b987a.t: ᱨᱳᱭᱭᱟᱞᱟ ᱤᱜᱩᱨᱩ · ᱨᱳᱭᱭᱟᱞᱟ ᱤᱜᱩᱨᱩ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ | 1acrefarms

seg.0484ea984ed7.src: రొయ్యల ఇగురు. Royyala iguru, the coastal Andhra prawn roast: prawns cooked down in onion masala with hill turmeric powder and fiery Teja chilli powder. Serves 4.
seg.0484ea984ed7.t: ᱨᱳᱭᱭᱟᱞᱟ ᱤᱜᱩᱨᱩ᱾ ᱨᱳᱭᱭᱟᱞᱟ ᱤᱜᱩᱨᱩ, ᱥᱟᱢᱩᱫᱽᱨᱚ ᱫᱷᱟᱨᱮ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱨᱳᱥᱴ: ᱵᱩᱨᱩ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ᱾ 4 ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ᱾
seg.0484ea984ed7.back: Royyala Iguru. Royyala iguru, the prawn roast of seaside Andhra: prawns cooked in onion masala with hill turmeric powder and hot Teja chilli powder. For 4 people.

seg.1b1d6a89c215.src: Royyala Iguru: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.1b1d6a89c215.t: ᱨᱳᱭᱭᱟᱞᱟ ᱤᱜᱩᱨᱩ: 1acrefarms ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱠᱟᱨᱰ, ᱡᱤᱱᱤᱥ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ
seg.1b1d6a89c215.back: Royyala Iguru: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and steps

seg.965a1e93fb08.src: Sunnundalu are the urad dal laddus of Andhra: split urad dal roasted till nutty, ground fine with jaggery and pressed together with hot ghee. There is no cooking of syrup, so they come together in about half an hour. Andhra homes make a tin for Sankranti and Diwali, pack them for relatives travelling abroad, and keep them for an evening sweet with tea.
seg.965a1e93fb08.t: ᱥᱩᱱᱱᱩᱱᱰᱟᱞᱩ ᱫᱚ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱞᱟᱰᱰᱩ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ: ᱦᱟᱹᱴᱤᱧ ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱥᱩᱜᱚᱫ ᱦᱤᱡᱩᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ, ᱜᱩᱲ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱵᱟᱨᱤᱠ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱛᱮ ᱪᱟᱯᱟᱹᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱡᱚᱲᱟᱣᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱪᱟᱥᱱᱤ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤ ᱵᱟᱹᱱᱩᱜᱼᱟ, ᱚᱱᱟᱛᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ ᱟᱫᱷᱟ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱚᱲᱟᱜ ᱠᱚ ᱥᱟᱝᱠᱨᱟᱱᱛᱤ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱤᱣᱟᱞᱤ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱢᱤᱫᱴᱟᱝ ᱰᱟᱵᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣᱟ, ᱵᱤᱫᱮᱥ ᱥᱮᱱᱚᱜ ᱜᱷᱟᱨᱚᱧᱡᱽ ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱵᱟᱸᱫᱷᱟᱣᱟ, ᱟᱨ ᱟᱭᱩᱵ ᱪᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱡᱚᱢᱟᱜ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱫᱚᱦᱚᱭᱟ᱾
seg.965a1e93fb08.back: Sunnundalu is Andhra's urad dal laddu: split urad dal is fried until a nut-like smell comes, ground fine with jaggery and bound by pressing with hot ghee. No need to cook a syrup, so it is made in about half an hour. Andhra houses make a box for Sankranti and Diwali, pack it for family members going abroad, and keep it as a sweet food with evening tea.

seg.e564344550cd.src: Our Thati Bellam palm jaggery gives sunnundalu a deep brown colour and a rich, slightly smoky sweetness that suits the roasted dal. This recipe makes about 15 laddus.
seg.e564344550cd.t: ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱴᱤ ᱵᱮᱞᱞᱟᱢ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱥᱩᱱᱱᱩᱱᱰᱟᱞᱩ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱟᱲᱦᱟ ᱵᱷᱩᱨᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱯᱮᱨᱮᱡ, ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱫᱷᱩᱸᱣᱟᱹ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱢᱤᱞᱟᱹᱣᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱛᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 15 ᱞᱟᱰᱰᱩ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.e564344550cd.back: Our tati bellam palm jaggery gives sunnundalu a deep brown colour and a full, slightly smoky-like sweetness which blends well with the fried dal. With this recipe about 15 laddus are made.

seg.b1400f429b2f.src: Total includes cooling the roasted dal before grinding.
seg.b1400f429b2f.t: ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱥᱮᱞᱮᱫ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.b1400f429b2f.back: In the total time cooling the fried dal before grinding is included.

seg.6c6369238635.src: Roast urad dal till golden, cool and grind fine, then grind in palm jaggery and cardamom. Mix with hot ghee and shape into laddus.
seg.6c6369238635.t: ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱵᱟᱨᱤᱠ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱟᱨ ᱮᱞᱟᱭᱪᱤ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱞᱟᱰᱰᱩ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.6c6369238635.back: Fry urad dal until gold colour, cool and grind fine, then grind in palm jaggery and cardamom and mix. Mixing with hot ghee make laddus.

seg.890ddaaca185.src: 1 cup white urad dal ⟦1⟧split, skinless (minapappu), about 200 g⟦/1⟧
seg.890ddaaca185.t: 1 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱯᱩᱸᱰ ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ⟦1⟧ᱦᱟᱹᱴᱤᱧ, ᱪᱷᱚᱞᱟ ᱵᱤᱱ (ᱢᱤᱱᱟᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ), ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 200 g⟦/1⟧
seg.890ddaaca185.back: 1 cup white urad dal ⟦1⟧split, without skin (minapappu), about 200 g⟦/1⟧

seg.06c2723f717d.src: 1 cup grated palm jaggery ⟦1⟧about 180 g, lightly packed; pound or grate the pieces first⟦/1⟧
seg.06c2723f717d.t: 1 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ⟦1⟧ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 180 g, ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱯᱟᱹᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱢᱟᱯ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ; ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱠᱚ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱢᱮ ᱥᱮ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱢᱮ⟦/1⟧
seg.06c2723f717d.back: 1 cup grated palm jaggery ⟦1⟧about 180 g, measured pressing a little; first pound the pieces or grate them⟦/1⟧

seg.25c886ef1375.src: ½ cup ghee ⟦1⟧melted and hot; keep 1–2 tbsp extra on hand⟦/1⟧
seg.25c886ef1375.t: ½ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ⟦1⟧ᱞᱤᱞᱤ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ; ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ 1–2 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱛᱮᱭᱟᱨ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ⟦/1⟧
seg.25c886ef1375.back: ½ cup ghee ⟦1⟧melted and warm; keep 1–2 tablespoons more ghee ready⟦/1⟧

seg.99983266b588.src: Pick through the urad dal for any small stones. Do not wash it; it must stay dry for roasting.
seg.99983266b588.t: ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱫᱷᱤᱨᱤ ᱠᱚ ᱵᱟᱪᱷᱟᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱟᱞᱚᱢ ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟᱭᱟ; ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ᱾
seg.99983266b588.back: Pick out the small stones from the urad dal and remove them. Don't wash; for frying it must be dry.

seg.2f2807ce216b.src: Put the dal in a heavy pan on a low flame.
seg.2f2807ce216b.t: ᱫᱟᱞ ᱦᱟᱭᱟᱹᱠ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.2f2807ce216b.back: Keep the dal in a heavy pan on low fire.

seg.65588a76c883.src: Dry-roast the urad dal on a low flame till golden and nutty, about 10 minutes. Stir all the time so every grain colours evenly; it should smell toasty and snap when you bite a grain.
seg.65588a76c883.t: ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱥᱩᱜᱚᱫ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱜᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 10 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ᱾ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜ; ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱥᱩᱜᱚᱫ ᱦᱤᱡᱩᱜ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱢ ᱥᱟᱰᱮ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ᱾
seg.65588a76c883.back: Dry-fry the urad dal on low fire until gold colour and a nut-like smell, about 10 minutes. Stir all the time so every grain becomes an even colour; a fried smell must come and when a grain is eaten it must crack crisp.

seg.9e8dc23d38fa.src: Tip the dal onto a plate and spread it out. Cool it, then grind to a fine powder. Grind in short bursts so the mixer does not heat up, and sieve out any coarse bits to grind again.
seg.9e8dc23d38fa.t: ᱫᱟᱞ ᱛᱷᱟᱨᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱹᱛᱩᱨ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱯᱟᱥᱱᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱵᱟᱨᱤᱠ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱠᱷᱟᱴᱚ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱛᱮ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱢᱤᱠᱥᱤ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱞᱚᱞᱚᱜ, ᱟᱨ ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱪᱷᱟᱹᱱᱤ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱫᱩᱦᱲᱟᱹ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.9e8dc23d38fa.back: Take the dal out into a plate and spread. Cool, then grind to a fine powder. Grind in short times so the mixie does not heat up, and sieve out big pieces and grind again.

seg.edfa5bb66e59.src: Grate the palm jaggery finely, or pound the pieces in a mortar, breaking up any hard lumps.
seg.edfa5bb66e59.t: ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱵᱟᱨᱤᱠ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱮ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱠᱚ ᱚᱠᱞᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱢᱮ, ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱫᱤᱞᱟ ᱠᱚ ᱨᱟᱹᱯᱩᱫ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ᱾
seg.edfa5bb66e59.back: Grate the palm jaggery fine, or pound the pieces in a mortar, breaking hard lumps.

seg.fcf7bce21bc5.src: Add the jaggery and cardamom powder to the dal powder in the mixer jar. Grind in the jaggery and cardamom till evenly mixed. A few pulses are enough; tip it all into a wide bowl.
seg.fcf7bce21bc5.t: ᱢᱤᱠᱥᱤ ᱡᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱟᱨ ᱮᱞᱟᱭᱪᱤ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱟᱨ ᱮᱞᱟᱭᱪᱤ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ ᱛᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱠᱷᱟᱴᱚ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱜᱮ ᱡᱚᱛᱚᱱ; ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱚᱥᱟᱨ ᱵᱟᱴᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱹᱛᱩᱨ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.fcf7bce21bc5.back: In the mixie jar add the jaggery and cardamom powder with the dal powder. Grind until the jaggery and cardamom mix evenly. A few short times are enough; take everything out into a dry bowl.

seg.1cd01dc31b1a.src: Melt the ghee in a small pan until it is hot but not smoking.
seg.1cd01dc31b1a.t: ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱞᱤᱞᱤ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜ ᱢᱮᱱᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱫᱷᱩᱸᱣᱟᱹ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱚᱰᱚᱠᱚᱜ᱾
seg.1cd01dc31b1a.back: Melt the ghee in a small pan until hot but smoke does not come out.

seg.0b0ec921a239.src: Pour in the hot ghee, mix well and press into small balls. Start with most of the ghee, mix with a spoon, then use your hands once it is cool enough to touch.
seg.0b0ec921a239.t: ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱵᱮᱥ ᱛᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱪᱟᱯᱟᱹᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱜᱩᱞᱤ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ ᱟᱭᱢᱟ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱛᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱥᱟᱵ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱡᱚᱛᱚᱱ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜᱚᱜ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱛᱤ ᱛᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.0b0ec921a239.back: Pour the hot ghee, mix well and pressing make small balls. First add most of the ghee, mix with a spoon, then when it is cool enough to hold mix with the hand.

seg.0c005163369c.src: Take a small handful and squeeze it firmly in your fist, then roll it round between your palms. If it crumbles, add a spoon more hot ghee to the bowl and mix.
seg.0c005163369c.t: ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱢᱩᱴᱷᱤ ᱦᱟᱛᱟᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱢᱩᱴᱷᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱛᱮ ᱪᱟᱯᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱛᱤ ᱛᱟᱞᱠᱷᱟ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱩᱲᱩᱭ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱜᱩᱞ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱡᱩᱫᱤ ᱨᱟᱹᱯᱩᱫᱚᱜ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ, ᱵᱟᱴᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.0c005163369c.back: Take a small fistful and press tightly in the fist, then roll round between the palms. If it crumbles, add one more spoon of hot ghee in the bowl and mix.

seg.7ac27bb5fb12.src: Set the laddus on a plate to firm up for 15–20 minutes before storing.
seg.7ac27bb5fb12.t: ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱞᱟᱰᱰᱩ ᱠᱚ ᱛᱷᱟᱨᱤ ᱨᱮ 15–20 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.7ac27bb5fb12.back: Before storing let the laddus become firm on a plate 15–20 minutes.

seg.591b2b7e4ef4.src: Roast the dal on a low flame so it cooks through without burning.
seg.591b2b7e4ef4.t: ᱫᱟᱞ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱡᱟᱹᱞᱤ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱚᱜ᱾
seg.591b2b7e4ef4.back: Fry the dal on low fire so it cooks to the inside without burning.

seg.07daa833e53a.src: Grind the dal only after it has cooled completely; warm dal turns pasty in the mixer.
seg.07daa833e53a.t: ᱫᱟᱞ ᱯᱩᱨᱟᱹ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱜᱮ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ; ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱢᱤᱠᱥᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱯᱮᱥᱴ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.07daa833e53a.back: Grind the dal only after it has fully cooled; hot dal becomes a paste in the mixie.

seg.33701abc66f0.src: Shape the laddus while the mixture is still warm; it binds best with the heat of the ghee.
seg.33701abc66f0.t: ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱟᱭᱢᱟ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱞᱟᱰᱰᱩ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ; ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱛᱮ ᱡᱟᱹᱥᱛᱤ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱡᱚᱲᱟᱣᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.33701abc66f0.back: Make the laddus while the mixture is still a little warm; with the heat of the ghee they bind best.

seg.b6fb58b6b287.src: Palm jaggery pieces vary in hardness, so grate or pound them small before they go into the mixer.
seg.b6fb58b6b287.t: ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱠᱚ ᱮᱴᱟᱜ ᱮᱴᱟᱜ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱱᱟ, ᱚᱱᱟᱛᱮ ᱢᱤᱠᱥᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱢᱮ ᱥᱮ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.b6fb58b6b287.back: The pieces of palm jaggery are different in hardness, so before putting in the mixie grate them or pound them small.

seg.1797acff16a2.src: Cane jaggery: use the same amount of grated cane jaggery for a lighter colour and a caramel-like sweetness.
seg.1797acff16a2.t: ᱟᱸᱠ ᱜᱩᱲ: ᱚᱛᱠᱮ ᱜᱮ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱟᱸᱠ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱞᱠᱟᱹ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱠᱮᱨᱟᱢᱮᱞ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.1797acff16a2.back: Sugarcane jaggery: add the same amount of grated sugarcane jaggery, the colour becomes light and the sweetness caramel-like.

seg.f95b0650add7.src: With skin: use black split urad dal with its skin for darker, grainier sunnundalu, the way some village homes make them.
seg.f95b0650add7.t: ᱪᱷᱚᱞᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ: ᱪᱷᱚᱞᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ ᱦᱟᱹᱴᱤᱧ ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱦᱟᱛᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱥᱩᱱᱱᱩᱱᱰᱟᱞᱩ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ, ᱡᱮᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱛᱤᱱᱟᱹᱜ ᱟᱹᱛᱩ ᱚᱲᱟᱜ ᱠᱚ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣᱟ᱾
seg.f95b0650add7.back: With skin: take black split urad dal with skin, for darker and grainy sunnundalu, as some old houses make.

seg.07498f6166e4.src: With sugar: use ¾ cup powdered sugar in place of the jaggery for pale, crisp-melting laddus.
seg.07498f6166e4.t: ᱪᱤᱱᱤ ᱥᱟᱶ: ᱜᱩᱲ ᱵᱚᱫᱚᱞ ¾ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱪᱤᱱᱤ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱦᱟᱞᱠᱟᱹ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱚᱪᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱤᱞᱤᱭᱚᱜ ᱞᱟᱰᱰᱩ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ᱾
seg.07498f6166e4.back: With sugar: instead of jaggery add ¾ cup powdered sugar, for a light-coloured laddu that melts in the mouth.

seg.8fea3a4a695f.src: Serve as an evening sweet with tea or coffee, or as part of the Sankranti and Diwali sweet plate.
seg.8fea3a4a695f.t: ᱟᱭᱩᱵ ᱪᱟ ᱥᱮ ᱠᱚᱯᱷᱤ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱡᱚᱢᱟᱜ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱮ ᱥᱟᱝᱠᱨᱟᱱᱛᱤ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱤᱣᱟᱞᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱛᱷᱟᱨᱤ ᱨᱮ᱾
seg.8fea3a4a695f.back: Serve as a sweet food with evening tea or coffee, or on the sweet plate of Sankranti and Diwali.

seg.83b4edc5c69d.src: Keep in an airtight steel tin at room temperature and eat within 2 weeks. In warm weather they keep longer in the fridge; let them come to room temperature before eating.
seg.83b4edc5c69d.t: ᱦᱚᱭ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱥᱴᱤᱞ ᱰᱟᱵᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱚᱴᱷᱨᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ 2 ᱦᱟᱯᱛᱟ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱡᱤᱞᱤᱧ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱱᱟ; ᱡᱚᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱠᱚᱴᱷᱨᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱦᱤᱡᱩᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.83b4edc5c69d.back: Keep in an air-tight steel box at room temperature and eat within 2 weeks. In hot weather they stay longer in the fridge; before eating let them come to room temperature.

seg.c0ae9315eb0e.src: Why are my sunnundalu not holding shape?
seg.c0ae9315eb0e.t: ᱤᱧᱟᱜ ᱥᱩᱱᱱᱩᱱᱰᱟᱞᱩ ᱪᱮᱫᱟᱜ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱡᱚᱲᱟᱣᱜ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ?
seg.c0ae9315eb0e.back: Why are my sunnundalu not binding?

seg.03c64235659e.src: The mixture needs more hot ghee, or it has cooled down. Warm a spoon or two of ghee, mix it in and shape the laddus while the mixture is still warm.
seg.03c64235659e.t: ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ, ᱥᱮ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱮᱱᱟ᱾ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱵᱟᱨ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱟᱭᱢᱟ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱞᱟᱰᱰᱩ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.03c64235659e.back: The mixture needs more hot ghee, or it has cooled. Heat one or two more spoons of ghee and mix, and make the laddus while the mixture is still warm.

seg.c125d749f215.src: Can I make sunnundalu with palm jaggery?
seg.c125d749f215.t: ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱛᱮ ᱥᱩᱱᱱᱩᱱᱰᱟᱞᱩ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ ᱥᱮ?
seg.c125d749f215.back: Can sunnundalu be made with palm jaggery?

seg.7b13a91f65e1.src: Yes. Grate or pound the palm jaggery (thati bellam) finely and use the same amount as cane jaggery. The laddus turn darker and taste deeper and slightly smoky.
seg.7b13a91f65e1.t: ᱮᱦᱚᱸ᱾ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ (ᱛᱟᱴᱤ ᱵᱮᱞᱞᱟᱢ) ᱵᱟᱨᱤᱠ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱢᱮ ᱥᱮ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱟᱸᱠ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱚᱛᱠᱮ ᱜᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱞᱟᱰᱰᱩ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱜᱟᱲᱦᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱫᱷᱩᱸᱣᱟᱹ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ᱾
seg.7b13a91f65e1.back: Yes. Grate the palm jaggery (tati bellam) fine or pound it and add the same amount as sugarcane jaggery. The laddus become darker and the taste deep and slightly smoky-like.

seg.946f64207639.back: How many days do sunnundalu stay?

seg.b2aed25ebff6.src: About 2 weeks in an airtight tin at room temperature, and longer in the fridge. Use a dry spoon or dry hands to take them out.
seg.b2aed25ebff6.t: ᱠᱚᱴᱷᱨᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱦᱚᱭ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱰᱟᱵᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 2 ᱦᱟᱯᱛᱟ, ᱟᱨ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱡᱤᱞᱤᱧ᱾ ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱥᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱛᱤ ᱵᱮᱵᱷᱟᱨ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.b2aed25ebff6.back: At room temperature in an air-tight box about 2 weeks, and in the fridge longer. For taking out use a dry spoon or dry hands.

seg.e750875c4912.src: Should I use urad dal with or without skin?
seg.e750875c4912.t: ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱪᱷᱚᱞᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱥᱮ ᱪᱷᱚᱞᱟ ᱵᱤᱱ ᱦᱟᱛᱟᱣ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ?
seg.e750875c4912.back: Must urad dal be taken with skin or without skin?

seg.b12320430e22.src: Both are made in Andhra. White skinless urad dal gives smooth, light brown laddus; black urad dal with skin gives darker, grainier ones.
seg.b12320430e22.t: ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱟᱨᱭᱟ ᱜᱮ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱯᱩᱸᱰ, ᱪᱷᱚᱞᱟ ᱵᱤᱱ ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱛᱮ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ, ᱦᱟᱞᱠᱟᱹ ᱵᱷᱩᱨᱟ ᱞᱟᱰᱰᱩ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ; ᱪᱷᱚᱞᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱛᱮ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ᱾
seg.b12320430e22.back: In Andhra both are made. White, skinless urad dal gives an even, light brown laddu; black urad dal with skin, darker and grainy.

seg.d8e8e5770555.src: సున్నుండలు. Andhra sunnundalu: roasted urad dal ground with Thati Bellam palm jaggery and bound with hot ghee into laddus. Step-by-step method, tips and FAQs.
seg.d8e8e5770555.t: ᱥᱩᱱᱱᱩᱱᱰᱟᱞᱩ᱾ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱥᱩᱱᱱᱩᱱᱰᱟᱞᱩ: ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱛᱟᱴᱤ ᱵᱮᱞᱞᱟᱢ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱛᱮ ᱞᱟᱰᱰᱩ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱡᱚᱲᱟᱣ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ᱾ ᱫᱷᱟᱯ ᱫᱷᱟᱯ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ, ᱠᱟᱹᱢᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱛᱷᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱩᱠᱞᱤ᱾
seg.d8e8e5770555.back: Sunnundalu. Andhra sunnundalu: fried urad dal ground with tati bellam palm jaggery and bound like laddus with hot ghee. Step-by-step recipe, tips and questions.

seg.c61b125404d0.src: Sunnundalu: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.c61b125404d0.t: ᱥᱩᱱᱱᱩᱱᱰᱟᱞᱩ: 1acrefarms ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱠᱟᱨᱰ, ᱡᱤᱱᱤᱥ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ
seg.c61b125404d0.back: Sunnundalu: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and steps

seg.da179ec60cc9.t: ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱪᱟᱴᱱᱤ · 4 ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ

seg.02d0a5789a02.src: Tomato pachadi is the everyday chutney of Andhra kitchens: ripe tomatoes cooked down in oil with roasted dals, then ground coarse with chilli, garlic and a little tamarind. Many homes still grind it in the stone roti for a rough, spoonable texture, though a mixer in short pulses does the job. It goes with hot rice and ghee, dosa, idli and pesarattu.
seg.02d0a5789a02.t: ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ ᱫᱚ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱚᱲᱟᱜ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱪᱟᱴᱱᱤ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ: ᱡᱚᱜ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱤᱞᱤ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ, ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱡᱚᱡᱚ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱟᱭᱢᱟ ᱚᱲᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱭᱢᱟ ᱦᱚᱸ ᱫᱷᱤᱨᱤ ᱨᱚᱴᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣᱚᱜᱼᱟ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱠᱷᱟᱨᱟᱥ, ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱛᱮ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜ, ᱢᱮᱱᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱠᱷᱟᱴᱚ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱛᱮ ᱢᱤᱠᱥᱤ ᱦᱚᱸ ᱪᱟᱞᱟᱣᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ, ᱫᱚᱥᱟ, ᱤᱰᱞᱤ ᱟᱨ ᱯᱮᱥᱟᱨᱟᱴᱴᱩ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱡᱚᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.02d0a5789a02.back: Tomato pachadi is the everyday chutney of Andhra rice-cooking houses: ripe tomatoes are cooked in oil with fried dal until melted, then ground coarse with chilli, garlic and a little tamarind. In many houses even now it is ground on the grinding stone so it becomes rough, like to eat with a spoon, but short times in a mixie also work. This is eaten with hot rice and ghee, dosa, idli and pesarattu.

seg.7735dff0ccd2.src: Our Sannam chilli powder gives it a deep red colour and steady, medium heat, and a little turmeric powder goes in with the tomatoes. This recipe makes about 1½ cups.
seg.7735dff0ccd2.t: ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱟᱲᱦᱟ ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ, ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ, ᱟᱨ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱛᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 1½ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.7735dff0ccd2.back: Our Sannam chilli powder gives this deep red colour and even, medium heat, and with the tomatoes a little turmeric powder goes in. With this recipe about 1½ cups are made.

seg.44c4d82a4524.src: Total includes 5 minutes for the tomatoes to cool before grinding.
seg.44c4d82a4524.t: ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 5 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱥᱮᱞᱮᱫ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.44c4d82a4524.back: In the total time 5 minutes for cooling the tomato before grinding is included.

seg.827e4421a48d.src: Fry dals and methi in oil, cook tomatoes down with turmeric and salt, then grind coarsely with Sannam chilli powder, garlic and tamarind. Finish with a mustard and curry-leaf tempering.
seg.827e4421a48d.t: ᱫᱟᱞ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱮᱛᱷᱤ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱞᱤᱞᱤ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ, ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱚᱡᱚ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱢᱩᱪᱟᱹᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.827e4421a48d.back: Fry dal and fenugreek in oil, cook tomato with turmeric and salt until melted, then grind coarse with Sannam chilli powder, garlic and tamarind. At the end add the tempering of mustard and curry leaves.

seg.4171dd59d18a.t: 2 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ⟦1⟧ᱪᱤᱱᱟ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ ᱥᱮ ᱛᱤᱞ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ⟦/1⟧

seg.826b52ef9f19.src: ¼ tsp methi seeds ⟦1⟧fenugreek seeds; no more, or the pachadi turns bitter⟦/1⟧
seg.826b52ef9f19.t: ¼ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱢᱮᱛᱷᱤ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ⟦1⟧ᱢᱮᱛᱷᱤ; ᱱᱚᱣᱟ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱵᱟᱹᱲᱛᱤ ᱫᱚ ᱵᱟᱝ, ᱵᱟᱝᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ ᱦᱚᱨᱚᱜᱚᱜᱼᱟ⟦/1⟧
seg.826b52ef9f19.back: ¼ small spoon fenugreek seeds ⟦1⟧methi; not more than this, otherwise the pachadi becomes bitter⟦/1⟧

seg.6cd60f9cc4c2.src: 5 medium tomatoes ⟦1⟧about 500 g, ripe and red, chopped⟦/1⟧
seg.6cd60f9cc4c2.t: 5 ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱢᱟᱯ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ⟦1⟧ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 500 g, ᱡᱚᱜ ᱟᱨ ᱟᱨᱟᱜ, ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ⟦/1⟧
seg.6cd60f9cc4c2.back: 5 medium-size tomatoes ⟦1⟧about 500 g, ripe and red, cut⟦/1⟧

seg.29558a247c61.src: 2 tsp Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧up to 1 tbsp for a hotter pachadi⟦/1⟧
seg.29558a247c61.t: 2 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ⟦1⟧ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 1 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ⟦/1⟧
seg.29558a247c61.back: 2 small spoons Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧for a hotter pachadi up to 1 big spoon⟦/1⟧

seg.f7c3bb463ff4.t: ᱜᱩᱞᱤ ᱢᱟᱨᱵᱮᱞ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱡᱚᱡᱚ ⟦1⟧ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 5 g, ᱡᱟᱹᱦᱤᱱ ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ⟦/1⟧
seg.f7c3bb463ff4.back: marble-ball sized tamarind ⟦1⟧about 5 g, seeds removed⟦/1⟧

seg.2f8f5bd3f25f.t: ¼ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱷᱚᱱᱤᱭᱟ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ (ᱢᱚᱱ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ) ⟦1⟧ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ⟦/1⟧
seg.2f8f5bd3f25f.back: ¼ cup coriander leaves (as you wish) ⟦1⟧cut coarse coarse⟦/1⟧

seg.2c1074e3a23e.src: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a kadai on medium-low heat.
seg.2c1074e3a23e.t: ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱦᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ-ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ 2 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.2c1074e3a23e.back: Heat 2 big spoons of oil in a kadai on medium-low fire.

seg.9d0674551be0.src: Fry the urad dal, chana dal and methi in oil till golden; lift them out. This takes 2–3 minutes; stir all the time, as methi burns fast and turns bitter.
seg.9d0674551be0.t: ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ, ᱵᱩᱴ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱮᱛᱷᱤ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ; ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱨᱮ 2–3 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫᱼᱟ; ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ, ᱪᱮᱫᱟᱜ ᱥᱮ ᱢᱮᱛᱷᱤ ᱞᱚᱜᱚᱱ ᱡᱟᱹᱞᱤᱭᱚᱜᱼᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱚᱨᱚᱜᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.9d0674551be0.back: Fry urad dal, chana dal and fenugreek in oil until gold colour; take out. This takes 2–3 minutes; stir all the time, because fenugreek quickly burns and becomes bitter.

seg.4727da6f2a95.src: In the same oil, add the chopped tomatoes and stir for a minute on medium heat.
seg.4727da6f2a95.t: ᱚᱱᱟ ᱜᱮ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.4727da6f2a95.back: In that same oil add the cut tomatoes and stir one minute on medium fire.

seg.8032f2a2778c.src: Cook the tomatoes with turmeric and salt till soft and the juice dries up. Cover for the first 5 minutes, then cook uncovered, stirring now and then, about 12–15 minutes in all, until the tomatoes are pulpy and oil shows at the edges.
seg.8032f2a2778c.t: ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱟᱨ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱥᱩᱠᱟᱹᱣᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ 5 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱵᱤᱱ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ, ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱢᱤᱞᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 12–15 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ, ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱞᱤᱞᱤᱭᱚᱜ ᱟᱨ ᱜᱟᱫᱮᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱧᱮᱞᱚᱜ᱾
seg.8032f2a2778c.back: Cook the tomatoes with turmeric and salt until soft and the juice dries. First cover 5 minutes, then cook without cover, stirring now and then, all together about 12–15 minutes, until the tomato melts and oil is seen at the edges.

seg.d606b6ac13a2.src: Switch off, stir in the tamarind so it softens in the heat, and let everything cool for about 5 minutes.
seg.d606b6ac13a2.t: ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱢᱮ, ᱡᱚᱡᱚ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴᱚᱜ, ᱟᱨ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 5 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.d606b6ac13a2.back: Turn off the fire, mix in the tamarind so it softens in the heat, and cool everything about 5 minutes.

seg.c1820dcae462.src: In the stone roti or a mixer jar, first grind the fried dals and methi to a coarse powder.
seg.c1820dcae462.t: ᱫᱷᱤᱨᱤ ᱨᱚᱴᱤ ᱥᱮ ᱢᱤᱠᱥᱤ ᱡᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱮᱛᱷᱤ ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.c1820dcae462.back: In a grinding stone or mixie jar first grind the fried dal and fenugreek to a coarse powder.

seg.f07d8b97d1db.src: Grind the dals, garlic, tamarind, chilli powder and tomatoes coarsely. In a mixer, add the garlic, chilli powder and cooked tomatoes to the dal powder and pulse 4–5 times without water; stop while it still has texture. Stir in the coriander leaves, if using.
seg.f07d8b97d1db.t: ᱫᱟᱞ, ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ, ᱡᱚᱡᱚ, ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱢᱤᱠᱥᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ, ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱵᱤᱱ 4–5 ᱠᱷᱟᱴᱚ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ; ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱛᱷᱟᱢᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱡᱩᱫᱤ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱱᱟᱢ ᱫᱷᱚᱱᱤᱭᱟ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.f07d8b97d1db.back: Grind dal, garlic, tamarind, chilli powder and tomato coarse. In the mixie add garlic, chilli powder and cooked tomato with the dal powder and without water grind 4–5 short times; stop while it is still grainy. If you are adding it, mix in coriander leaves.

seg.6675d75425f6.src: Taste and adjust: a pinch more salt, or a little more chilli powder pulsed in, if you want it hotter.
seg.6675d75425f6.t: ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱧᱮᱞ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱴᱷᱤᱠ ᱢᱮ: ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱤᱢᱴᱤ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ, ᱥᱮ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱠᱩᱥᱤᱭᱟᱜ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.6675d75425f6.back: Taste and adjust: grind adding one more pinch of salt, or if you like hotter a little more chilli powder.

seg.27426b7ca3c6.src: Spoon the pachadi into a bowl. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a small pan and add the mustard seeds; when they splutter, add the urad dal and fry until golden.
seg.27426b7ca3c6.t: ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ ᱢᱤᱫᱴᱟᱝ ᱵᱟᱴᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱹᱛᱩᱨ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱨᱮ 1 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ; ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱥᱟᱰᱮ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.27426b7ca3c6.back: Take the pachadi out into a bowl. Heat 1 big spoon of oil in a small pan and add mustard seeds; when they crackle add urad dal and fry until gold colour.

seg.77131f9506c3.src: Add the red chillies, asafoetida and curry leaves and stir for a few seconds.
seg.77131f9506c3.t: ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ, ᱦᱤᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱥᱮᱠᱮᱱᱰ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.77131f9506c3.back: Adding red chilli, hing and curry leaves stir a few seconds.

seg.d4a4b9439500.src: Temper with mustard, red chillies and curry leaves; pour over. Mix it in just before serving.
seg.d4a4b9439500.t: ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ, ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ; ᱪᱮᱛᱟᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱮᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱜᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.d4a4b9439500.back: Add the tempering of mustard, red chilli and curry leaves; pour on top. Mix only just before serving.

seg.0f23e6b9231e.src: Cook the tomatoes till the juice dries up so the pachadi keeps longer and does not taste raw.
seg.0f23e6b9231e.t: ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱥᱩᱠᱟᱹᱣᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱡᱤᱞᱤᱧ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱭ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱸᱪᱟ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ᱾
seg.0f23e6b9231e.back: Cook until the tomato juice dries so the pachadi stays more days and does not taste raw.

seg.bad083b47507.src: Ripe, deep-red tomatoes give the best colour; if yours are sour, cut the tamarind to half.
seg.bad083b47507.t: ᱡᱚᱜ, ᱜᱟᱲᱦᱟ ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱛᱮ ᱡᱟᱹᱥᱛᱤ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ; ᱡᱩᱫᱤ ᱟᱢᱟᱜ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱡᱚᱰ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱡᱚᱡᱚ ᱟᱫᱷᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.bad083b47507.back: Ripe, deep red tomatoes give the best colour; if your tomatoes are sour, add half the tamarind.

seg.99bd4830d431.src: Pulse, do not run the mixer: a coarse pachadi is how Andhra homes like it, and a smooth paste loses that texture.
seg.99bd4830d431.t: ᱠᱷᱟᱴᱚ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱢᱤᱠᱥᱤ ᱡᱤᱞᱤᱧ ᱟᱞᱚᱢ ᱪᱟᱞᱟᱣᱟ: ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱚᱲᱟᱜ ᱠᱚ ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ ᱠᱩᱥᱤᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ, ᱟᱨ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ ᱯᱮᱥᱴ ᱨᱮ ᱚᱱᱟ ᱵᱟᱱᱟᱣᱴ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱭᱟ᱾
seg.99bd4830d431.back: Grind in short times, don't run the mixie long: Andhra houses like coarse pachadi, and an even paste does not have that texture.

seg.27f2aaa2d25d.src: Sannam chilli powder gives medium heat. Start at 2 tsp and add more after tasting; the heat settles a little as the pachadi rests.
seg.27f2aaa2d25d.t: ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ 2 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱛᱮ ᱮᱦᱚᱵ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱧᱮᱞ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ; ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱠᱚᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.27f2aaa2d25d.back: Sannam chilli powder gives medium heat. Start with 2 small spoons and add more after tasting; if the pachadi is kept, the heat reduces a little.

seg.5e0bf03c1b36.src: Green chilli: replace the chilli powder with 4–5 green chillies, fried with the dals.
seg.5e0bf03c1b36.t: ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ: ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱵᱚᱫᱚᱞ 4–5 ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱫᱟᱞ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ᱾
seg.5e0bf03c1b36.back: Green chilli: instead of chilli powder add 4–5 green chillies, fried with the dal.

seg.d7301a50c407.src: Onion-tomato: fry 1 sliced onion until soft before the tomatoes go in.
seg.d7301a50c407.t: ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ-ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ: ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ 1 ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.d7301a50c407.back: Onion-tomato: before adding tomato fry 1 cut onion until soft.

seg.bc90e2638112.src: Hotter: use 1 tsp Teja chilli powder in place of 1 tsp of the Sannam; Teja is very hot, so go slowly.
seg.bc90e2638112.t: ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ: ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱵᱚᱫᱚᱞ 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ; ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱜᱮᱭᱟ, ᱚᱱᱟᱛᱮ ᱞᱟᱦᱟᱭ ᱛᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.bc90e2638112.back: More heat: instead of 1 small spoon of Sannam add 1 small spoon of Teja chilli powder; Teja is very hot, so add slowly.

seg.aab608a427a9.src: Without garlic: leave out the garlic and add a pinch more asafoetida to the tempering.
seg.aab608a427a9.t: ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱵᱤᱱ: ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱟᱞᱚᱢ ᱮᱢᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱤᱢᱴᱤ ᱦᱤᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.aab608a427a9.back: Without garlic: don't add garlic and add one more pinch of hing in the tempering.

seg.62d9491c4e58.src: Mix a spoonful into hot rice with a little ghee, or serve alongside dosa, idli, pesarattu or upma.
seg.62d9491c4e58.t: ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱮ ᱫᱚᱥᱟ, ᱤᱰᱞᱤ, ᱯᱮᱥᱟᱨᱟᱴᱴᱩ ᱥᱮ ᱩᱯᱢᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.62d9491c4e58.back: Mix a spoon in hot rice with a little ghee, or serve with dosa, idli, pesarattu or upma.

seg.3f0b892d2728.src: Keep it in a clean, dry glass jar in the fridge and eat within 4 days. Always use a dry spoon.
seg.3f0b892d2728.t: ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ, ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱠᱟᱸᱪ ᱡᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ 4 ᱢᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱡᱟᱣᱜᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱵᱮᱵᱷᱟᱨ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.3f0b892d2728.back: Keep in a clean, dry glass jar in the fridge and eat within 4 days. Always use a dry spoon.

seg.20425f76c6e2.src: How do you make Andhra tomato pachadi?
seg.20425f76c6e2.t: ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ ᱪᱮᱫ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣᱚᱜᱼᱟ?
seg.20425f76c6e2.back: How is Andhra tomato pachadi made?

seg.32ae9ac6b03c.src: Fry urad dal, chana dal and methi in oil, cook chopped tomatoes with turmeric and salt until the juice dries up, then grind everything coarsely with chilli powder, garlic and tamarind. Finish with a mustard, red chilli and curry-leaf tempering.
seg.32ae9ac6b03c.t: ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ, ᱵᱩᱴ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱮᱛᱷᱤ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱥᱩᱠᱟᱹᱣᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ, ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱚᱡᱚ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱢᱩᱪᱟᱹᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ, ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.32ae9ac6b03c.back: Fry urad dal, chana dal and fenugreek in oil, cook the cut tomatoes with turmeric and salt until the juice dries, then grind everything coarse with chilli powder, garlic and tamarind. At the end add the tempering of mustard, red chilli and curry leaves.

seg.2e87824684cb.src: Why is my tomato pachadi bitter?
seg.2e87824684cb.t: ᱤᱧᱟᱜ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ ᱪᱮᱫᱟᱜ ᱦᱚᱨᱚᱜ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ?
seg.2e87824684cb.back: Why is my tomato pachadi bitter?

seg.b367557bedfc.src: Usually the methi seeds burnt or there were too many. Use only ¼ tsp for 500 g tomatoes and fry them on medium-low heat, lifting them out as soon as they turn golden.
seg.b367557bedfc.t: ᱥᱟᱫᱷᱟᱨᱚᱱ ᱛᱮ ᱢᱮᱛᱷᱤ ᱡᱟᱹᱞᱤ ᱮᱱᱟ ᱥᱮ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱵᱟᱹᱲᱛᱤ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱠᱟᱱᱟ᱾ 500 g ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱥᱩᱢᱩᱝ ¼ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ-ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.b367557bedfc.back: Usually the fenugreek burnt or there was very much. For 500 g tomatoes add only ¼ small spoon and fry on medium-low fire, and take out as soon as it becomes gold colour.

seg.acdf33e5cc6d.src: Can I make tomato pachadi without tamarind?
seg.acdf33e5cc6d.t: ᱡᱚᱡᱚ ᱵᱤᱱ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ ᱥᱮ?
seg.acdf33e5cc6d.back: Can tomato pachadi be made without tamarind?

seg.53fbd8949e0b.src: Yes, if your tomatoes are sour enough. Taste after cooking; ripe, sweet tomatoes need the small piece of tamarind for balance.
seg.53fbd8949e0b.t: ᱮᱦᱚᱸ, ᱡᱩᱫᱤ ᱟᱢᱟᱜ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱡᱚᱛᱚᱱ ᱡᱚᱰ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ᱾ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱧᱮᱞ ᱢᱮ; ᱡᱚᱜ, ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱡᱚᱡᱚ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ᱾
seg.53fbd8949e0b.back: Yes, if your tomatoes are sour enough. Taste after cooking; ripe, sweet tomatoes need a small piece of tamarind for balance.

seg.2938c7a0249e.src: How long does tomato pachadi last?
seg.2938c7a0249e.back: How many days does tomato pachadi stay?

seg.a35105e3a4af.src: About 4 days in the fridge in a clean, dry jar, as long as the tomatoes were cooked down well and you use a dry spoon.
seg.a35105e3a4af.t: ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ, ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱡᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 4 ᱢᱟᱦᱟᱸ, ᱡᱩᱫᱤ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱛᱮ ᱞᱤᱞᱤ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱟᱨ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱵᱮᱵᱷᱟᱨ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ᱾
seg.a35105e3a4af.back: In the fridge in a clean, dry jar about 4 days, if the tomato was cooked well until melted and if a dry spoon is used.

seg.4dbd4103e7fb.t: ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ · ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ | 1acrefarms

seg.de4e2a65c3ae.src: టమాటా పచ్చడి. Andhra tomato pachadi: tomatoes cooked down with turmeric powder, ground coarse with Sannam chilli powder, garlic and tamarind, then tempered.
seg.de4e2a65c3ae.t: ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ᱾ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ: ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱞᱤᱞᱤ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ, ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ, ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱚᱡᱚ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱮᱢ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ᱾
seg.de4e2a65c3ae.back: Tomato Pachadi. Andhra tomato pachadi: tomatoes cooked with turmeric powder until melted, ground coarse with Sannam chilli powder, garlic and tamarind, then tempered.

seg.03de1ac75259.src: Tomato Pachadi: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.03de1ac75259.t: ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱪᱪᱟᱲᱤ: 1acrefarms ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱠᱟᱨᱰ, ᱡᱤᱱᱤᱥ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ
seg.03de1ac75259.back: Tomato Pachadi: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and steps

seg.6357099a14e8.back: ¼ cup coriander leaves (as you wish)

seg.8dfb472228af.t: ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱫᱟᱞ · 4 ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ

seg.3d323a4b41cc.src: Tomato pappu is the everyday dal of Andhra homes: toor dal (kandi pappu) cooked soft with tomatoes and green chillies, mashed smooth and finished with a garlic tempering. It is cooked most days of the week and eaten with hot rice, a spoon of ghee and an appadam or a pickle on the side.
seg.3d323a4b41cc.t: ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱫᱚ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱚᱲᱟᱜ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ: ᱨᱟᱦᱟᱲ ᱫᱟᱞ (ᱠᱟᱱᱰᱤ ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ) ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ, ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ ᱛᱮ ᱜᱷᱟᱸᱴᱩᱣᱟᱹ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱢᱩᱪᱟᱹᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱦᱟᱯᱛᱟ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱟᱭᱢᱟ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱚᱜᱼᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ, ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱛᱮ ᱟᱯᱯᱟᱰᱚᱢ ᱥᱮ ᱟᱪᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱡᱚᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.3d323a4b41cc.back: Tomato pappu is the everyday dal of Andhra houses: arhar dal (kandi pappu) is cooked until soft with tomato and green chilli, mashed smooth, and at the end a garlic tempering is added. On many days of the week this is cooked and eaten with hot rice, a spoon of ghee and alongside appadam or pickle.

seg.734276af9399.src: Our turmeric powder goes into the cooker with the dal and gives it a deep yellow colour. Sannam chilli powder adds a red tinge and a steady, medium heat that sits behind the sour tomato. This recipe serves 4.
seg.734276af9399.t: ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱠᱩᱠᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱟᱲᱦᱟ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ, ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱡᱚᱰ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱱᱟ᱾ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ 4 ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ᱾
seg.734276af9399.back: Our turmeric powder goes in the cooker with the dal and gives this a deep yellow colour. Sannam chilli powder gives a little red colour and even, medium heat which stays behind the sour tomato. This recipe is for 4 people.

seg.8c5a5da215b1.src: Total includes letting the cooker release its steam.
seg.8c5a5da215b1.t: ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱩᱠᱟᱨ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱥᱤᱡᱩ ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱥᱮᱞᱮᱫ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.8c5a5da215b1.back: In the total time the time for the steam to come out of the cooker is included.

seg.2c1a760b1cf8.src: Pressure-cook toor dal with tomatoes, green chillies and turmeric powder, mash it with Sannam chilli powder and salt, and finish with a garlic and mustard tempering.
seg.2c1a760b1cf8.t: ᱨᱟᱦᱟᱲ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ, ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱯᱨᱮᱥᱟᱨ ᱠᱩᱠᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱜᱷᱟᱸᱴᱩᱣᱟᱹ ᱢᱮ, ᱟᱨ ᱢᱩᱪᱟᱹᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.2c1a760b1cf8.back: Cook arhar dal in a pressure cooker with tomato, green chilli and turmeric powder, mash with Sannam chilli powder and salt, and at the end add a tempering of garlic and mustard.

seg.d102a6fa5887.src: ¾ cup toor dal ⟦1⟧kandi pappu, about 150 g⟦/1⟧
seg.d102a6fa5887.t: ¾ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱨᱟᱦᱟᱲ ᱫᱟᱞ ⟦1⟧ᱠᱟᱱᱰᱤ ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ, ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 150 g⟦/1⟧
seg.d102a6fa5887.back: ¾ cup arhar dal ⟦1⟧kandi pappu, about 150 g⟦/1⟧

seg.258b0303a820.src: ½ tsp turmeric powder ⟦1⟧goes in the cooker⟦/1⟧
seg.258b0303a820.t: ½ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ⟦1⟧ᱠᱩᱠᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ⟦/1⟧
seg.258b0303a820.back: ½ small spoon turmeric powder ⟦1⟧goes in the cooker⟦/1⟧

seg.25c2493b65be.src: 1 tsp Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧goes in after mashing; up to 2 tsp for more heat⟦/1⟧
seg.25c2493b65be.t: 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ⟦1⟧ᱜᱷᱟᱸᱴᱩᱣᱟᱹ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ; ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 2 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ⟦/1⟧
seg.25c2493b65be.back: 1 small spoon Sannam chilli powder ⟦1⟧goes in after mashing; for more heat up to 2 small spoons⟦/1⟧

seg.f4f5c6c6e2d3.src: 2½ cups water ⟦1⟧plus ½ cup to adjust⟦/1⟧
seg.f4f5c6c6e2d3.t: 2½ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ⟦1⟧ᱟᱨ ᱴᱷᱤᱠ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ½ ᱠᱟᱯ⟦/1⟧
seg.f4f5c6c6e2d3.back: 2½ cups water ⟦1⟧and ½ cup for adjusting⟦/1⟧

seg.5f7d589d9776.src: 1 tbsp tamarind water (optional) ⟦1⟧if the tomatoes are not very sour⟦/1⟧
seg.5f7d589d9776.t: 1 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱡᱚᱡᱚ ᱫᱟᱜ (ᱢᱚᱱ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ) ⟦1⟧ᱡᱩᱫᱤ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱡᱚᱰ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ⟦/1⟧
seg.5f7d589d9776.back: 1 big spoon tamarind water (as you wish) ⟦1⟧if the tomatoes are not very sour⟦/1⟧

seg.4efa92e0ce99.src: Wash the toor dal in 2–3 changes of water and drain it.
seg.4efa92e0ce99.t: ᱨᱟᱦᱟᱲ ᱫᱟᱞ 2–3 ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱵᱚᱫᱚᱞ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱧᱩᱨ ᱦᱤᱡᱩᱜ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.4efa92e0ce99.back: Wash the arhar dal changing water 2–3 times and drain the water.

seg.3f536116a096.src: Put the dal in a pressure cooker with the tomatoes, green chillies, onion and 2½ cups of water.
seg.3f536116a096.t: ᱫᱟᱞ ᱯᱨᱮᱥᱟᱨ ᱠᱩᱠᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ, ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ, ᱯᱤᱭᱟᱡ ᱟᱨ 2½ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.3f536116a096.back: Put the dal in the pressure cooker with tomato, green chilli, onion and 2½ cups of water.

seg.7d012f63f2a2.src: Pressure-cook the dal with the tomatoes, green chillies and turmeric powder for 4 whistles. Stir the turmeric powder into the water before closing the lid, then cook on medium heat.
seg.7d012f63f2a2.t: ᱫᱟᱞ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ, ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ 4 ᱥᱤᱴᱤ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱯᱨᱮᱥᱟᱨ ᱠᱩᱠᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.7d012f63f2a2.back: Cook the dal in the pressure cooker with tomato, green chilli and turmeric powder up to 4 whistles. Before closing the lid mix the turmeric powder in the water, then cook on medium fire.

seg.5dccba018dbc.src: Let the pressure drop on its own, about 10 minutes. The dal is done when a grain mashes completely between two fingers.
seg.5dccba018dbc.t: ᱯᱨᱮᱥᱟᱨ ᱟᱡ ᱛᱮ ᱜᱮ ᱠᱚᱢ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 10 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ᱾ ᱵᱟᱨ ᱛᱤ ᱛᱟᱨᱟᱵ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱯᱩᱨᱟᱹ ᱜᱷᱟᱸᱴᱩᱣᱟᱹᱜ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱛᱮᱭᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ᱾
seg.5dccba018dbc.back: Let the pressure reduce by itself, about 10 minutes. If between two fingertips the grains fully mash, the dal is ready.

seg.da76f4c700ad.src: Mash well; add the chilli powder and salt. Use a wooden masher (pappu gutti) or the back of a ladle and mash while the dal is still hot, until the tomatoes and dal turn into one smooth mix.
seg.da76f4c700ad.t: ᱵᱮᱥ ᱛᱮ ᱜᱷᱟᱸᱴᱩᱣᱟᱹ ᱢᱮ; ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱠᱟᱴ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱜᱷᱟᱸᱴᱩ (ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱜᱩᱛᱛᱤ) ᱥᱮ ᱰᱟᱹᱵᱩ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱥᱮᱫ ᱵᱮᱵᱷᱟᱨ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱜᱷᱟᱸᱴᱩᱣᱟᱹ ᱢᱮ, ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜ᱾
seg.da76f4c700ad.back: Mash well; add chilli powder and salt. Use a wooden masher (pappu gutti) or the back of a ladle and mash while the dal is hot, until tomato and dal mix evenly.

seg.c1cb2443fbeb.src: Simmer 5 minutes with a splash of water. Add up to ½ cup water for a pouring consistency, and the tamarind water if using, and keep the heat on low so it does not catch.
seg.c1cb2443fbeb.t: ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ 5 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱯᱚᱛᱞᱟ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ½ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱫᱟᱜ, ᱟᱨ ᱡᱩᱫᱤ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱱᱟᱢ ᱡᱚᱡᱚ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱟᱨ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱞᱟᱛᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣᱜ᱾
seg.c1cb2443fbeb.back: Adding a little water cook 5 minutes on low fire. For pourable-thin up to ½ cup of water, and if you are adding it add the tamarind water, and keep the fire low so it does not stick at the bottom.

seg.b24472a45a67.src: Taste for salt and sourness, then stir in the coriander leaves and switch off.
seg.b24472a45a67.t: ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱚᱰ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱧᱮᱞ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱫᱷᱚᱱᱤᱭᱟ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.b24472a45a67.back: Taste the salt and sourness, then mixing in the coriander leaves turn off the fire.

seg.6f90b7e4f66a.src: Heat the ghee in a small pan on medium heat and add the mustard seeds; let them splutter.
seg.6f90b7e4f66a.t: ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ; ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱥᱟᱰᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.6f90b7e4f66a.back: Heat ghee in a small pan on medium fire and add mustard seeds; let crackle.

seg.0d1dd3c84a64.src: Fry mustard, cumin, garlic and curry leaves in the ghee; pour over. Add the cumin, garlic and dry red chillies after the mustard and fry until the garlic turns golden, then add the curry leaves and hing, and pour the sizzling tempering over the dal.
seg.0d1dd3c84a64.t: ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ, ᱡᱤᱨᱟ, ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ; ᱪᱮᱛᱟᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱥᱚᱨᱥᱚ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱡᱤᱨᱟ, ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱟᱨ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱤᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱟᱨ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱪᱤᱴᱤᱨ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱪᱮᱛᱟᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.0d1dd3c84a64.back: Fry mustard, cumin, garlic and curry leaves in ghee; pour on top. After the mustard add cumin, garlic and dry red chilli and fry the garlic until gold colour, then add curry leaves and hing, and pour the crackling tempering over the top.

seg.81a1668adc10.src: Cover for 2 minutes so the tempering flavours the dal, then stir and serve hot.
seg.81a1668adc10.t: 2 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱥᱩᱜᱚᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱮᱞᱮᱫᱚᱜ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.81a1668adc10.back: Cover 2 minutes so the smell of the tempering settles into the dal, then stir and serve hot.

seg.f904a5f14a1b.src: Mash the dal while it is hot for a smooth pappu. Once it cools, the grains set and stay lumpy.
seg.f904a5f14a1b.t: ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱜᱷᱟᱸᱴᱩᱣᱟᱹ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱛᱷᱤᱨᱚᱜᱼᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱤᱞᱟ ᱫᱤᱞᱟ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱱᱟ᱾
seg.f904a5f14a1b.back: For smooth pappu mash the dal while it is hot. After cooling the grains settle and stay lumpy.

seg.1a8211877e00.src: Sannam chilli powder is medium-hot. Start with 1 tsp; go up to 2 tsp for a spicier pappu.
seg.1a8211877e00.t: ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱜᱮᱭᱟ᱾ 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱛᱮ ᱮᱦᱚᱵ ᱢᱮ; ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 2 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ᱾
seg.1a8211877e00.back: Sannam chilli powder is medium hot. Start with 1 small spoon; for a hotter pappu up to 2 small spoons.

seg.d85da2ea2cf7.src: Ripe, sour country tomatoes (natu tomatoes) give the best flavour; with mild hybrid tomatoes add the tamarind water.
seg.d85da2ea2cf7.t: ᱡᱚᱜ, ᱡᱚᱰ ᱫᱤᱥᱚᱢ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ (ᱱᱟᱴᱩ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ) ᱛᱮ ᱡᱟᱹᱥᱛᱤ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ; ᱦᱟᱞᱠᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱭᱵᱽᱨᱤᱰ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱡᱚᱡᱚ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.d85da2ea2cf7.back: Ripe, sour country tomatoes (natu tomato) give the best taste; with light hybrid tomatoes add tamarind water.

seg.37f3ad1bf7b9.src: Let the garlic turn golden in the tempering before the curry leaves go in; pale garlic tastes raw.
seg.37f3ad1bf7b9.t: ᱠᱟᱨᱤ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱮᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱨᱮ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ; ᱯᱩᱸᱰ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱠᱟᱸᱪᱟ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫᱼᱟ᱾
seg.37f3ad1bf7b9.back: Before adding curry leaves make the garlic in the tempering gold colour; white garlic tastes raw.

seg.dfd3706fe457.src: Teja chilli powder: for a hotter pappu, use ½ tsp Teja chilli powder in place of the Sannam. Teja is very hot, so do not go over 1 tsp.
seg.dfd3706fe457.t: ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ: ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱵᱚᱫᱚᱞ ½ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱜᱮᱭᱟ, ᱚᱱᱟᱛᱮ 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱵᱟᱹᱲᱛᱤ ᱟᱞᱚᱢ ᱮᱢᱟ᱾
seg.dfd3706fe457.back: Teja chilli powder: for a hotter pappu add ½ small spoon of Teja chilli powder instead of Sannam. Teja is very hot, so don't add more than 1 small spoon.

seg.434f1a510bbb.src: Palakura tomato pappu: add 2 cups chopped spinach to the dal after mashing and simmer 5 minutes.
seg.434f1a510bbb.t: ᱯᱟᱞᱟᱠᱩᱨᱟ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ: ᱜᱷᱟᱸᱴᱩᱣᱟᱹ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱨᱮ 2 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱯᱟᱞᱚᱝ ᱥᱟᱠᱟᱢ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ 5 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.434f1a510bbb.back: Palakura tomato pappu: after mashing add 2 cups cut spinach leaves to the dal and cook 5 minutes on low fire.

seg.8d7a932afdbe.src: Pesarapappu: make it with yellow moong dal and cook for 2 whistles only.
seg.8d7a932afdbe.t: ᱯᱮᱥᱟᱨᱟᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ: ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱢᱩᱝ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱛᱮ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱩᱢᱩᱝ 2 ᱥᱤᱴᱤ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.8d7a932afdbe.back: Pesarapappu: make it with yellow moong dal and cook only up to 2 whistles.

seg.94f44314ecbb.src: Serve hot with steamed rice, a spoon of ghee and an appadam or avakaya on the side. It also goes well with chapati.
seg.94f44314ecbb.t: ᱥᱤᱡᱩ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ, ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱛᱮ ᱟᱯᱯᱟᱰᱚᱢ ᱥᱮ ᱟᱣᱟᱠᱟᱭᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱪᱟᱯᱟᱛᱤ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱦᱚᱸ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫᱼᱟ᱾
seg.94f44314ecbb.back: Serve hot with boiled rice, a spoon of ghee and alongside appadam or avakaya. It is also good with chapati.

seg.29a23e2fa864.src: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. The dal thickens when chilled; add a little hot water and heat through before serving.
seg.29a23e2fa864.t: ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ 2 ᱢᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡᱚᱜᱼᱟ; ᱮᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱯᱩᱨᱟᱹ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.29a23e2fa864.back: Keep the leftover covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. When cooled the dal thickens; before serving add a little hot water and heat fully.

seg.8e56f1d7c871.src: How many whistles for toor dal in a pressure cooker?
seg.8e56f1d7c871.t: ᱯᱨᱮᱥᱟᱨ ᱠᱩᱠᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱨᱟᱦᱟᱲ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱛᱤᱱᱟᱹᱜ ᱥᱤᱴᱤ?
seg.8e56f1d7c871.back: How many whistles for arhar dal in a pressure cooker?

seg.562abdd39933.src: About 4 whistles on medium heat, then let the pressure drop on its own. Older dal or dal that was not washed well may need 5.
seg.562abdd39933.t: ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 4 ᱥᱤᱴᱤ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱯᱨᱮᱥᱟᱨ ᱟᱡ ᱛᱮ ᱜᱮ ᱠᱚᱢ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱢᱟᱨᱮ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱥᱮ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱛᱮ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱛᱮ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 5 ᱥᱤᱴᱤ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.562abdd39933.back: On medium heat about 4 whistles, then let the pressure come down by itself. Old dal or dal not cleaned well with water may need 5 whistles.

seg.6a800f643cf1.src: What is the difference between tomato pappu and sambar?
seg.6a800f643cf1.t: ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱢᱵᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱪᱮᱫ ᱯᱷᱟᱨᱟᱠ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ?
seg.6a800f643cf1.back: What difference is there between tomato pappu and sambar?

seg.05135ac52968.src: Tomato pappu is a thick, mashed dal with a simple tempering and no sambar powder or vegetables. Sambar is thinner, uses tamarind, vegetables and a roasted spice powder.
seg.05135ac52968.t: ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱫᱚ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ, ᱜᱷᱟᱸᱴᱩᱣᱟᱹ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ, ᱥᱟᱫᱷᱟᱨᱚᱱ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱢᱵᱟᱨ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱥᱮ ᱩᱛᱩ ᱵᱤᱱ᱾ ᱥᱟᱢᱵᱟᱨ ᱫᱚ ᱯᱚᱛᱞᱟ, ᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱚᱡᱚ, ᱩᱛᱩ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱚᱥᱞᱟ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.05135ac52968.back: Tomato pappu is a thick, mashed dal, with ordinary tempering and without sambar powder or vegetables. Sambar is thin, in it tamarind, vegetables and fried masala powder go in.

seg.19117f898a31.src: Can I make tomato pappu without a pressure cooker?
seg.19117f898a31.t: ᱯᱨᱮᱥᱟᱨ ᱠᱩᱠᱟᱨ ᱵᱤᱱ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ ᱥᱮ?
seg.19117f898a31.back: Can tomato pappu be made without a pressure cooker?

seg.631df239c7a7.src: Yes. Soak the dal for 30 minutes and cook it in a covered pot with 3½ cups of water for about 40–45 minutes, stirring now and then, until it mashes easily.
seg.631df239c7a7.t: ᱮᱦᱚᱸ᱾ ᱫᱟᱞ 30 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱞᱟᱛ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱦᱟᱸᱰᱤ ᱨᱮ 3½ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 40–45 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ, ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱟᱞᱜᱟ ᱛᱮ ᱜᱷᱟᱸᱴᱩᱣᱟᱹᱜ᱾
seg.631df239c7a7.back: Yes. Soak the dal 30 minutes and cook in a covered pot with 3½ cups of water about 40–45 minutes, stirring now and then, until it mashes easily.

seg.b1140d6c02b4.src: Why is my tomato pappu too sour?
seg.b1140d6c02b4.t: ᱤᱧᱟᱜ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱡᱚᱰ ᱪᱮᱫᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ?
seg.b1140d6c02b4.back: Why is my tomato pappu very sour?

seg.6fb0505bf751.src: Some tomatoes are very sour. Simmer the dal a few more minutes and stir in a pinch of jaggery or a spoon of extra mashed dal to balance it.
seg.6fb0505bf751.t: ᱛᱤᱱᱟᱹᱜ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱡᱚᱰ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱱᱟ᱾ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱤᱢᱴᱤ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱥᱮ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱜᱷᱟᱸᱴᱩᱣᱟᱹ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.6fb0505bf751.back: Some tomatoes are very sour. Cook the dal a few more minutes on low fire and for balance mix in a pinch of jaggery or one more spoon of mashed dal.

seg.80a51a64344d.src: టమాటో పప్పు · Andhra Tomato Dal Recipe | 1acrefarms
seg.80a51a64344d.t: ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱳ ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ · ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ | 1acrefarms
seg.80a51a64344d.back: Tomato Pappu · Andhra tomato dal recipe | 1acrefarms

seg.7b91fd1a3bc3.src: టమాటో పప్పు. Andhra tomato dal: toor dal cooked soft with tomatoes and green chillies, our turmeric and Sannam chilli powder, and a garlic tempering. Serves 4.
seg.7b91fd1a3bc3.t: ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱳ ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ᱾ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱫᱟᱞ: ᱨᱟᱦᱟᱲ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱨᱭᱟᱹᱲ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ, ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ, ᱟᱨ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱪᱷᱚᱣᱠ᱾ 4 ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ᱾
seg.7b91fd1a3bc3.back: Tomato Pappu. Andhra tomato dal: arhar dal cooked soft with tomato and green chilli, with our turmeric and Sannam chilli powder, and a garlic tempering. For 4 people.

seg.bf96bcd14023.src: Tomato Pappu: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.bf96bcd14023.t: ᱴᱟᱢᱟᱴᱟ ᱯᱟᱯᱯᱩ: 1acrefarms ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱠᱟᱨᱰ, ᱡᱤᱱᱤᱥ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ
seg.bf96bcd14023.back: Tomato Pappu: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and steps

seg.f112ac607ab2.back: 1 big spoon tamarind water (as you wish)

seg.9078b361da10.src: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · Vellulli Kaaram · Lahsun Ki Sookhi Chutney
seg.9078b361da10.t: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · ᱣᱮᱞᱞᱩᱞᱞᱤ ᱠᱟᱨᱟᱢ · ᱞᱟᱦᱥᱩᱱ ᱠᱤ ᱥᱩᱠᱷᱤ ᱪᱟᱴᱱᱤ
seg.9078b361da10.back: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · Velluli Karam · Lahsun ki sukhi chutney

seg.464f01dcf4e8.src: Vellulli kaaram is the garlic chilli podi kept on Andhra dining tables: red chilli powder pounded with plenty of garlic, roasted coriander and cumin, and salt. Mixed into the first handful of hot rice with ghee, or sprinkled over idli and dosa with a little oil, it is a quick meal on busy days and a staple in tiffin boxes.
seg.464f01dcf4e8.t: ᱣᱮᱞᱞᱩᱞᱞᱤ ᱠᱟᱨᱟᱢ ᱫᱚ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱡᱚᱢᱟᱜ ᱴᱮᱵᱩᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱯᱳᱰᱤ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ: ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱭᱢᱟ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ, ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱫᱷᱚᱱᱤᱭᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱤᱨᱟ, ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ᱾ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ ᱢᱩᱴᱷᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ, ᱥᱮ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱤᱰᱞᱤ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱚᱥᱟ ᱪᱮᱛᱟᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱪᱤᱴᱟᱹᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ, ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱵᱮᱵᱚᱥᱛᱟ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱚᱜᱚᱱ ᱡᱚᱢᱟᱜ ᱟᱨ ᱴᱤᱯᱷᱤᱱ ᱵᱟᱠᱥᱚ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱡᱟᱣᱜᱮ ᱡᱤᱱᱤᱥ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ᱾
seg.464f01dcf4e8.back: Velluli karam is the garlic chilli podi kept on the Andhra meal table: red chilli powder with plenty of garlic, fried coriander and cumin, pounded with salt. Mixed into the first fistful of hot rice with ghee, or sprinkled with a little oil over idli and dosa, this is the go-to thing for quick meals and tiffin boxes on busy days.

seg.a9654adade5e.src: Our Teja chilli powder makes it deep red and very hot, the way Guntur homes like it. For less heat, use half Sannam chilli powder.
seg.a9654adade5e.t: ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱜᱟᱲᱦᱟ ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱟᱨ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱮᱫᱟ, ᱡᱮᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱜᱩᱱᱴᱩᱨ ᱚᱲᱟᱜ ᱠᱚ ᱠᱩᱥᱤᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱠᱚᱢ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱟᱫᱷᱟ ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.a9654adade5e.back: Our Teja chilli powder makes this deep red and very hot, as Guntur houses like. For less heat add half Sannam chilli powder.

seg.b43a6fdf4164.src: Total includes cooling the seeds and garlic before grinding.
seg.b43a6fdf4164.t: ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱥᱮᱞᱮᱫ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.b43a6fdf4164.back: In the total time cooling of the seeds and garlic before grinding is included.

seg.501bcac1011e.src: Roast coriander and cumin, grind them, then pulse with Teja chilli powder, salt and lightly warmed garlic into a coarse podi. Eat it with hot rice and ghee, idli or dosa.
seg.501bcac1011e.t: ᱫᱷᱚᱱᱤᱭᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱤᱨᱟ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ, ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱠᱷᱟᱴᱚ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱯᱳᱰᱤ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ, ᱤᱰᱞᱤ ᱥᱮ ᱫᱚᱥᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.501bcac1011e.back: Fry coriander and cumin, grind, then pounding in short times with Teja chilli powder, salt and slightly warmed garlic make a coarse podi. Eat with hot rice and ghee, idli or dosa.

seg.e9ce857fe180.src: 25 garlic cloves ⟦1⟧about ½ cup, peeled; the thin inner skin can stay⟦/1⟧
seg.e9ce857fe180.t: 25 ᱠᱟᱹᱴᱤ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ⟦1⟧ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ ½ ᱠᱟᱯ, ᱪᱷᱚᱞᱟ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ; ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱯᱚᱛᱞᱟ ᱪᱷᱚᱞᱟ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ⟦/1⟧
seg.e9ce857fe180.back: 25 cloves garlic ⟦1⟧about ½ cup, peeled; the thin inner skin can remain⟦/1⟧

seg.47382aff4c0b.src: ¼ cup Teja chilli powder ⟦1⟧very hot; see the tips to make it milder⟦/1⟧
seg.47382aff4c0b.t: ¼ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ⟦1⟧ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ; ᱠᱚᱢ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱠᱟᱹᱢᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱛᱷᱟ ᱧᱮᱞ ᱢᱮ⟦/1⟧
seg.47382aff4c0b.back: ¼ cup Teja chilli powder ⟦1⟧very hot; for less heat see the tips⟦/1⟧

seg.33ac26ca8201.t: 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱜᱩᱞᱤ ᱢᱟᱨᱵᱮᱞ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱡᱚᱡᱚ (ᱢᱚᱱ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ) ⟦1⟧ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ, ᱡᱟᱹᱦᱤᱱ ᱚᱰᱚᱠ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ⟦/1⟧
seg.33ac26ca8201.back: 1 small marble-ball sized tamarind (as you wish) ⟦1⟧dry, seeds removed⟦/1⟧

seg.7bca54595a6a.src: Ghee or oil ⟦1⟧1 tsp per serving⟦/1⟧
seg.7bca54595a6a.t: ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱥᱮ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ⟦1⟧ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱦᱟᱹᱴᱤᱧ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ⟦/1⟧
seg.7bca54595a6a.back: Ghee or oil ⟦1⟧1 small spoon for every portion⟦/1⟧

seg.074d39a3f8b1.src: Peel the garlic and pat the cloves completely dry with a cloth; any water shortens how long the podi keeps.
seg.074d39a3f8b1.t: ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱪᱷᱚᱞᱟ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱯᱲᱟ ᱛᱮ ᱪᱟᱯᱟᱹᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱯᱩᱨᱟᱹ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱢᱮ; ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱱ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱯᱳᱰᱤ ᱛᱤᱱᱟᱹᱜ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱭᱟ ᱚᱱᱟ ᱠᱚᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.074d39a3f8b1.back: Peel the garlic and dry fully pressing with a cloth; if any water remains it reduces how many days the podi stays.

seg.33bb0e9eea87.src: Dry-roast the coriander and cumin seeds till fragrant; let them cool. Use a small pan on medium-low heat; this takes 1–2 minutes, and the coriander should turn a shade darker, not brown.
seg.33bb0e9eea87.t: ᱫᱷᱚᱱᱤᱭᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱤᱨᱟ ᱥᱩᱜᱚᱫ ᱦᱤᱡᱩᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱜᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ; ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱛᱟᱞᱟ-ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱦᱟᱛᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ; ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱨᱮ 1–2 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫᱼᱟ, ᱟᱨ ᱫᱷᱚᱱᱤᱭᱟ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱫᱷᱟᱯ ᱦᱮᱸᱫᱮ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ, ᱵᱷᱩᱨᱟ ᱫᱚ ᱵᱟᱝ᱾
seg.33bb0e9eea87.back: Dry-fry coriander and cumin until smell comes; cool. Keep a small pan on medium-low fire; this takes 1–2 minutes, and the coriander must become one step dark, not brown.

seg.a2f7a86fc993.src: Warm the garlic in 1 tsp oil for 2 minutes. Keep the heat low and stir; the cloves should soften slightly at the edges without browning. Let it cool.
seg.a2f7a86fc993.t: ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ 2 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ; ᱠᱟᱹᱴᱤ ᱠᱚ ᱜᱟᱫᱮᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴᱚᱜ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ ᱢᱮᱱᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱵᱷᱩᱨᱟ ᱫᱚ ᱵᱟᱝ᱾ ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.a2f7a86fc993.back: Warm the garlic in 1 small spoon of oil for 2 minutes. Keep the fire low and stir; the cloves must become a little soft at the edges but not brown. Cool.

seg.a4d0f7c87bd5.src: Grind the seeds to a powder, then pulse with the chilli powder and salt. Add the tamarind with the seeds, if using, so it breaks down evenly.
seg.a4d0f7c87bd5.t: ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱠᱷᱟᱴᱚ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱡᱩᱫᱤ ᱡᱚᱡᱚ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱱᱟᱢ, ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱜᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱥᱚᱢᱟᱱ ᱛᱮ ᱨᱟᱹᱯᱩᱫᱚᱜ᱾
seg.a4d0f7c87bd5.back: Grind the seeds to powder, then grind in short times with chilli powder and salt. If you are adding tamarind, add it with the seeds so it breaks evenly.

seg.c12763cab28c.src: Add the garlic and pulse in short bursts to a coarse, moist powder. Stop and scrape down the jar after every 2–3 pulses, as garlic sticks to the sides.
seg.c12763cab28c.t: ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱷᱟᱴᱚ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟ, ᱫᱟᱜ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ 2–3 ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱛᱷᱟᱢᱟᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱡᱟᱨ ᱜᱟᱫᱮᱨ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱞᱟᱛᱟᱨ ᱛᱮ ᱟᱹᱛᱩᱨ ᱢᱮ, ᱪᱮᱫᱟᱜ ᱥᱮ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱜᱟᱫᱮᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱟᱴᱟᱣᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.c12763cab28c.back: Add the garlic and grinding in short times make a coarse, damp powder. After every 2–3 times stop and push down from the edge of the jar, because garlic sticks to the edge.

seg.31358182425b.src: In a stone mortar, pound the seeds first, then the garlic with the salt, and work in the chilli powder last.
seg.31358182425b.t: ᱫᱷᱤᱨᱤ ᱚᱠᱞᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ, ᱟᱨ ᱢᱩᱪᱟᱹᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.31358182425b.back: In a stone mortar first pound the seeds, then the garlic with salt, and at the end mix in the chilli powder.

seg.29ac6dd20660.src: Taste a pinch with a little rice and ghee, and add salt if needed.
seg.29ac6dd20660.t: ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱤᱢᱴᱤ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱧᱮᱞ ᱢᱮ, ᱟᱨ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.29ac6dd20660.back: Taste a pinch with a little rice and ghee, and if needed add salt.

seg.b4ccc3b591dd.src: Spread the podi on a plate for 10 minutes so the steam escapes, then pack it into a clean, dry jar.
seg.b4ccc3b591dd.t: ᱯᱳᱰᱤ ᱛᱷᱟᱨᱤ ᱨᱮ 10 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱯᱟᱥᱱᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱥᱤᱡᱩ ᱚᱰᱚᱠᱚᱜ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ, ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱡᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.b4ccc3b591dd.back: Spread the podi on a plate 10 minutes so the steam goes out, then fill it in a clean, dry jar.

seg.23d348ffe051.src: Teja is very hot; use half Sannam for a milder podi, or cut the chilli powder to 3 tbsp for the same garlic.
seg.23d348ffe051.t: ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱟᱹᱰᱤ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱜᱮᱭᱟ; ᱠᱚᱢ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱯᱳᱰᱤ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱟᱫᱷᱟ ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱮ ᱚᱛᱠᱮ ᱜᱮ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ 3 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱠᱚᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.23d348ffe051.back: Teja is very hot; for a less-hot podi add half Sannam, or with the same garlic reduce the chilli powder down to 3 big spoons.

seg.948075d5f572.src: Dry the garlic well and warm it in oil; damp garlic makes the podi go off quickly.
seg.948075d5f572.t: ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱛᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ; ᱫᱟᱜ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱛᱮ ᱯᱳᱰᱤ ᱞᱚᱜᱚᱱ ᱵᱤᱜᱟᱲᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.948075d5f572.back: Dry the garlic well and warm it in oil; with damp garlic the podi quickly spoils.

seg.1a71c64c8c74.src: Pulse, do not run the mixer: run it long and the garlic turns into a paste.
seg.1a71c64c8c74.t: ᱠᱷᱟᱴᱚ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱢᱤᱠᱥᱤ ᱡᱤᱞᱤᱧ ᱟᱞᱚᱢ ᱪᱟᱞᱟᱣᱟ: ᱡᱤᱞᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱞᱟᱣ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱯᱮᱥᱴ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.1a71c64c8c74.back: Grind in short times, don't run the mixie long: if run long the garlic becomes a paste.

seg.d1432fb9a627.src: Mix 1 tsp podi with 1 tsp ghee into a cup of hot rice; adjust to taste.
seg.d1432fb9a627.t: ᱢᱤᱫ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱨᱮ 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱯᱳᱰᱤ ᱟᱨ 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ; ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱠᱚᱢ ᱵᱟᱹᱲᱛᱤ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.d1432fb9a627.back: In a cup of hot rice mix 1 small spoon of podi and 1 small spoon of ghee; reduce or increase according to taste.

seg.bdc5e9728b98.src: With dals: dry-roast 1 tbsp chana dal and 1 tbsp urad dal with the seeds for a nuttier, slightly milder podi.
seg.bdc5e9728b98.t: ᱫᱟᱞ ᱥᱟᱶ: ᱫᱟᱱᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ 1 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱵᱩᱴ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱟᱨ 1 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱩᱨᱤᱫ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱜᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ, ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱠᱚᱢ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱯᱳᱰᱤ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ᱾
seg.bdc5e9728b98.back: With dal: with the seeds dry-fry 1 big spoon chana dal and 1 big spoon urad dal, for a nut-like, slightly less-hot podi.

seg.4d03eacf7428.src: Raw garlic: skip warming the garlic for a sharper taste, and eat it within a week.
seg.4d03eacf7428.t: ᱠᱟᱸᱪᱟ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ: ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱟᱞᱚᱢ ᱞᱚᱞᱚᱭᱟ, ᱟᱨ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱦᱟᱯᱛᱟ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.4d03eacf7428.back: Raw garlic: for a sharp taste don't heat the garlic, and eat within one week.

seg.21139bdcd961.src: Medium heat: use 2 tbsp Teja and 2 tbsp Sannam chilli powder.
seg.21139bdcd961.t: ᱛᱟᱞᱟ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ: 2 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱟᱨ 2 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.21139bdcd961.back: Medium heat: add 2 big spoons Teja and 2 big spoons Sannam chilli powder.

seg.bceea7c8cb4f.src: Mix with the first handful of hot rice and ghee, or sprinkle over idli, dosa or pesarattu with a little oil or ghee.
seg.bceea7c8cb4f.t: ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ ᱢᱩᱴᱷᱤ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱮ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱥᱮ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱤᱰᱞᱤ, ᱫᱚᱥᱟ ᱥᱮ ᱯᱮᱥᱟᱨᱟᱴᱴᱩ ᱪᱮᱛᱟᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱪᱤᱴᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.bceea7c8cb4f.back: Mix with the first fistful of hot rice and ghee, or sprinkle over idli, dosa or pesarattu with a little oil or ghee.

seg.5fd9cf1554fd.src: Keep in a clean, dry, airtight jar for about 2 weeks at room temperature, or a month in the fridge. Always use a dry spoon.
seg.5fd9cf1554fd.t: ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ, ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ, ᱦᱚᱭ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱡᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱚᱴᱷᱨᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 2 ᱦᱟᱯᱛᱟ, ᱥᱮ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱟᱸᱫᱚ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱡᱟᱣᱜᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱵᱮᱵᱷᱟᱨ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.5fd9cf1554fd.back: In a clean, dry, air-tight jar at room temperature about 2 weeks, or keep one month in the fridge. Always use a dry spoon.

seg.c58bc6538b2f.src: How do you make vellulli kaaram?

seg.0ecd3203de93.src: Roast coriander and cumin seeds, grind them, add chilli powder and salt, then pulse in peeled garlic cloves to a coarse, moist powder. Andhra homes often pound it in a stone mortar.
seg.0ecd3203de93.t: ᱫᱷᱚᱱᱤᱭᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱤᱨᱟ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱪᱷᱚᱞᱟ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱠᱟᱹᱴᱤ ᱠᱷᱟᱴᱚ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟ, ᱫᱟᱜ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱚᱲᱟᱜ ᱠᱚ ᱟᱭᱢᱟ ᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱫᱷᱤᱨᱤ ᱚᱠᱞᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱟᱞᱟ᱾
seg.0ecd3203de93.back: Fry coriander and cumin, grind, add chilli powder and salt, then grinding peeled garlic cloves in short times make a coarse, damp powder. Andhra houses many times pound this in a stone mortar.

seg.727d415cb888.src: How do I make garlic podi less spicy?
seg.727d415cb888.t: ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱯᱳᱰᱤ ᱪᱮᱫ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱠᱚᱢ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ?
seg.727d415cb888.back: How can garlic podi be made less hot?

seg.e4231ea5cf7a.src: Use half Sannam chilli powder in place of half the Teja, or use 3 tbsp chilli powder in all. Eating it with plenty of ghee also takes the edge off.
seg.e4231ea5cf7a.t: ᱟᱫᱷᱟ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱵᱚᱫᱚᱞ ᱟᱫᱷᱟ ᱥᱟᱱᱱᱟᱢ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱥᱮ ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱢᱤᱞᱟᱹᱣ 3 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱟᱭᱢᱟ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱦᱚᱸ ᱡᱷᱟᱞ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.e4231ea5cf7a.back: Add half Sannam chilli powder instead of half Teja, or add 3 big spoons of chilli powder in all. Eating with plenty of ghee also softens the heat.

seg.982e854e4417.src: How long does vellulli kaaram last?
seg.982e854e4417.back: How many days does velluli karam stay?

seg.a620f29950c0.src: About 2 weeks at room temperature in a dry, airtight jar, or a month in the fridge. Dry the garlic well and warm it in oil first so it lasts longer.
seg.a620f29950c0.t: ᱠᱚᱴᱷᱨᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ, ᱦᱚᱭ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱡᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 2 ᱦᱟᱯᱛᱟ, ᱥᱮ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱪᱟᱸᱫᱚ᱾ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱛᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱡᱤᱞᱤᱧ ᱫᱤᱱ ᱛᱟᱦᱮᱸᱭ᱾
seg.a620f29950c0.back: At room temperature in a dry, air-tight jar about 2 weeks, or in the fridge one month. Dry the garlic well and first warm it in oil so it stays more days.

seg.4c626acd1bdd.src: Can I use whole dried red chillies instead of chilli powder?
seg.4c626acd1bdd.t: ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱵᱚᱫᱚᱞ ᱥᱟᱵᱩᱛ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱵᱮᱵᱷᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ ᱥᱮ?
seg.4c626acd1bdd.back: Can whole dry red chillies be used instead of chilli powder?

seg.c796942589c3.src: Yes. Dry-roast about 20 dried red chillies with a few drops of oil until crisp, cool and grind them before adding the garlic.
seg.c796942589c3.t: ᱮᱦᱚᱸ᱾ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 20 ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱴᱚᱯᱟ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱢ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱮᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.c796942589c3.back: Yes. Fry about 20 dry red chillies with a few drops of oil until crisp, cool and grind before adding the garlic.

seg.a2202c094baa.t: ᱣᱮᱞᱞᱩᱞᱞᱤ ᱠᱟᱨᱟᱢ · ᱣᱮᱞᱞᱩᱞᱞᱤ ᱠᱟᱨᱟᱢ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ | 1acrefarms

seg.c5afa85ab56d.src: వెల్లుల్లి కారం. Andhra garlic chilli podi: roasted coriander and cumin pounded with garlic, salt and Teja chilli powder. Mix with hot rice and ghee, or idli and dosa.
seg.c5afa85ab56d.t: ᱣᱮᱞᱞᱩᱞᱞᱤ ᱠᱟᱨᱟᱢ᱾ ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱯᱳᱰᱤ: ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱫᱷᱚᱱᱤᱭᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱤᱨᱟ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ, ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱫᱟᱞ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ᱾ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ, ᱥᱮ ᱤᱰᱞᱤ ᱟᱨ ᱫᱚᱥᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.c5afa85ab56d.back: Velluli Karam. Andhra garlic chilli podi: fried coriander and cumin pounded with garlic, salt and Teja chilli powder. Mix with hot rice and ghee, or with idli and dosa.

seg.eff09f5a48ed.src: Vellulli Kaaram: the recipe card from 1acrefarms, with ingredients and method
seg.eff09f5a48ed.t: ᱣᱮᱞᱞᱩᱞᱞᱤ ᱠᱟᱨᱟᱢ: 1acrefarms ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱠᱟᱨᱰ, ᱡᱤᱱᱤᱥ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱥᱟᱶ
seg.eff09f5a48ed.back: Velluli Karam: 1acrefarms recipe card, with ingredients and steps

seg.2b0c8026598d.t: 1 ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱜᱩᱞᱤ ᱢᱟᱨᱵᱮᱞ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱡᱚᱡᱚ (ᱢᱚᱱ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ)
seg.2b0c8026598d.back: 1 small marble-ball sized tamarind (as you wish)

seg.3b01a30ec3ce.src: Rub the chicken with curd, Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt. Rest 30 minutes. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge while it rests.
seg.3b01a30ec3ce.t: ᱥᱤᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱤ, ᱛᱮᱡᱟ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ, ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱵᱩᱞᱩᱝ ᱢᱟᱠᱷᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ 30 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱚᱱᱟ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱵᱟᱴᱤ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.3b01a30ec3ce.back: Rub curd, Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt onto the chicken. Leave for 30 minutes. During that time cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge.

seg.6cceb77cd01b.src: 500 g fish pieces ⟦1⟧firm fish cut into thick steaks: rohu, catla (bochcha), korameenu (murrel) or seer fish (vanjaram)⟦/1⟧
seg.6cceb77cd01b.t: 500 g ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ⟦1⟧ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱛᱮ ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ: ᱨᱚᱦᱩ, ᱠᱟᱛᱞᱟ (ᱵᱚᱪᱟ), ᱠᱳᱨᱟᱢᱤᱱᱩ (ᱢᱟᱨᱚᱞ) ᱥᱮ ᱥᱤᱭᱟᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ (ᱣᱟᱧᱡᱟᱨᱟᱢ)⟦/1⟧
seg.6cceb77cd01b.back: 500 g fish pieces ⟦1⟧firm-fleshed fish cut into thick pieces: rohu, katla (bocha), koramenu (murrel) or seer fish (vanjaram)⟦/1⟧

seg.3248f0a2bb4b.src: 40 g tamarind ⟦1⟧about two lemon-sized balls, soaked in 2 cups warm water for 15 minutes⟦/1⟧
seg.3248f0a2bb4b.t: 40 g ᱡᱚᱡᱚ ⟦1⟧ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱵᱟᱨ ᱜᱩᱞᱤ, 2 ᱠᱟᱯ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ 15 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱞᱟᱛ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ⟦/1⟧
seg.3248f0a2bb4b.back: 40 g tamarind ⟦1⟧about two lemon-sized balls, soaked 15 minutes in 2 cups of warm water⟦/1⟧

seg.6efbfa504170.src: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Reheat gently in the pan without stirring, until steaming hot all the way through.
seg.6efbfa504170.t: ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ 2 ᱢᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱞᱟᱦᱟᱭ ᱛᱮ ᱫᱩᱦᱲᱟᱹ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ, ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱯᱩᱨᱟᱹ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱯ ᱟᱲᱟᱜᱚᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ᱾
seg.6efbfa504170.back: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Reheat gently in a pan without stirring, until it is fully hot inside and steam comes out.

seg.379b410c6994.src: Firm river or sea fish cut into thick steaks: rohu, catla (bochcha), murrel (korameenu) or seer fish. Bony small fish also work but need gentle handling.
seg.379b410c6994.t: ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱛᱮ ᱜᱮᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱜᱟᱰᱟ ᱥᱮ ᱥᱟᱢᱩᱫᱽᱨᱚ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ: ᱨᱚᱦᱩ, ᱠᱟᱛᱞᱟ (ᱵᱚᱪᱟ), ᱢᱟᱨᱚᱞ (ᱠᱳᱨᱟᱢᱤᱱᱩ) ᱥᱮ ᱥᱤᱭᱟᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ᱾ ᱡᱟᱝ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱦᱚᱸ ᱪᱟᱞᱟᱣᱜᱼᱟ ᱢᱮᱱᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱞᱟᱦᱟᱭ ᱛᱮ ᱥᱟᱢᱵᱽᱲᱟᱣ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ᱾
seg.379b410c6994.back: Firm-fleshed river or sea fish cut into thick pieces: rohu, katla (bocha), murrel (koramenu) or seer fish. Small fish with bones also work but must be handled gently.

seg.3af5b68fc2e1.src: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Warm the pulusu in a pan with a splash of water until steaming hot all the way through.
seg.3af5b68fc2e1.t: ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ 2 ᱢᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱯᱩᱞᱩᱥᱩ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ, ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱯᱩᱨᱟᱹ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱯ ᱟᱲᱟᱜᱚᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ᱾
seg.3af5b68fc2e1.back: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Heat the pulusu in a pan with a little water, until it is fully hot inside and steam comes out.

seg.b4d28033bb05.src: Mutton vepudu: pressure-cook 500 g boneless mutton with the marinade and ½ cup water for 5–6 whistles, until tender, then fry it the same way.
seg.b4d28033bb05.t: ᱢᱚᱴᱚᱱ ᱣᱮᱯᱩᱰᱩ: 500 g ᱡᱟᱝ ᱵᱤᱱ ᱢᱮᱨᱚᱢ ᱡᱤᱞ ᱢᱟᱠᱷᱟᱣ ᱟᱨ ½ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱶ 5–6 ᱥᱤᱴᱤ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ, ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱯᱨᱮᱥᱟᱨ ᱠᱩᱠᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱚᱱᱟ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.b4d28033bb05.back: Mutton vepudu: pressure-cook 500 g boneless goat meat with the marinade and ½ cup water for 5–6 whistles, until soft, then fry the same way.

seg.04112853a660.src: Both work. Boneless cooks faster and crisps more; small bone-in pieces have more flavour but need 6–8 minutes longer in their juices.
seg.04112853a660.t: ᱵᱟᱨᱭᱟ ᱜᱮ ᱪᱟᱞᱟᱣᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱡᱟᱝ ᱵᱤᱱ ᱞᱚᱜᱚᱱ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱚᱜᱼᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ; ᱡᱟᱝ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ ᱢᱮᱱᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱟᱡᱟᱜ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱨᱮ 6–8 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱟᱨᱦᱚᱸ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ᱾
seg.04112853a660.back: Both work. Boneless cooks quickly and becomes crisper; small bone-in pieces have more flavour but need 6–8 minutes more in their own juices.

seg.d20a641bec03.src: Pack it for a lunch box or a short journey and eat it within about 4 hours. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat them within a day.
seg.d20a641bec03.t: ᱴᱤᱯᱷᱤᱱ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱥᱮ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱟᱦᱮᱫ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱵᱟᱸᱫᱷᱟᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱤᱫᱤ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 4 ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱤᱫ ᱢᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.d20a641bec03.back: If you pack it for tiffin or a short trip, eat within about 4 hours. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within one day.

seg.bc9078e02646.src: Either the lemon juice was cooked or the turmeric burnt in the oil. Add the turmeric last, switch off the stove right after and stir for only 5–10 seconds; add the lemon juice to the rice, off the heat.
seg.bc9078e02646.t: ᱥᱮ ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱮᱱᱟ ᱥᱮ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱟᱹᱞᱤ ᱮᱱᱟ᱾ ᱥᱟᱥᱟᱝ ᱢᱩᱪᱟᱹᱫ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱚᱱᱟ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱜᱮ ᱪᱩᱞᱦᱟᱹ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱮᱠᱮᱱ 5–10 ᱥᱮᱠᱮᱱᱰ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ; ᱞᱮᱵᱩ ᱨᱚᱥ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱟᱲᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱫᱟᱠᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.bc9078e02646.back: Either the lemon juice got cooked or the turmeric burnt in the oil. Add the turmeric at the end, then switch off the stove and stir only 5–10 seconds; take the lemon juice away from the fire and add it to the rice.

seg.c288f67fcabb.src: Pour the other cup of water into a heavy-bottomed pan; a thin pan lets the ragi catch.
seg.c288f67fcabb.t: ᱮᱴᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱦᱟᱭᱟᱹᱠ ᱞᱟᱛᱟᱨ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱢᱮ; ᱯᱟᱛᱞᱟ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱞᱟᱛᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱟᱴᱠᱟᱣᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.c288f67fcabb.back: Pour the other cup of water into a heavy-bottomed pan; in a thin pan the ragi sticks to the bottom.

seg.e87c26125f87.src: Can I use cane jaggery in ragi java?
seg.e87c26125f87.t: ᱨᱟᱜᱤ ᱡᱟᱣᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱸᱠ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱵᱮᱵᱷᱟᱨ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ ᱥᱮ?
seg.e87c26125f87.back: Can sugarcane jaggery be used in ragi java?

seg.a9a06390a945.src: Yes. Use the same amount of grated cane jaggery (cheruku bellam) and stir it in after switching off the stove, so the milk does not split. It gives a lighter colour and a milder, caramel-like sweetness.
seg.a9a06390a945.t: ᱮᱦᱚᱸ᱾ ᱚᱛᱠᱮ ᱜᱮ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱟᱸᱠ ᱜᱩᱲ (ᱪᱮᱨᱩᱠᱩ ᱵᱮᱞᱞᱟᱢ) ᱦᱟᱛᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱪᱩᱞᱦᱟᱹ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱢᱤᱥᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ, ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱛᱚᱣᱟ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱯᱷᱟᱴᱟᱜ᱾ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱦᱟᱞᱠᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱟᱞᱠᱟ, ᱠᱮᱨᱟᱢᱮᱞ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.a9a06390a945.back: Yes. Take the same amount of grated sugarcane jaggery (cheruku bellam) and mix it in after switching off the stove, so the milk does not split. This gives a light colour and a light, caramel-like sweetness.

seg.e7cb15cc47e2.src: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 1 day. Reheat in a pan only until steaming hot all the way through; longer reheating makes the prawns tough.
seg.e7cb15cc47e2.t: ᱵᱟᱧᱪᱟᱣ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱡᱷᱟᱯ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ 1 ᱢᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱠᱮᱱ ᱚᱛᱠᱮ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱡᱮᱢᱚᱱ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱯᱩᱨᱟᱹ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱦᱩᱭ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱵᱷᱟᱯ ᱟᱲᱟᱜᱚᱜ; ᱚᱱᱟ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱡᱤᱞᱤᱧ ᱚᱠᱛᱚ ᱫᱩᱦᱲᱟᱹ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱞᱮᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱤᱪᱟᱹ ᱦᱟᱹᱠᱩ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.e7cb15cc47e2.back: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 1 day. Heat in a pan only enough that it is fully hot inside and steam comes out; reheating longer than that makes the prawns hard.

seg.ea5408ec0853.src: Can I make sunnundalu with cane jaggery?
seg.ea5408ec0853.t: ᱟᱸᱠ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱛᱮ ᱥᱩᱱᱱᱩᱱᱰᱟᱞᱩ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱫᱟᱲᱮᱭᱟᱜᱼᱟ ᱥᱮ?
seg.ea5408ec0853.back: Can sunnundalu be made with sugarcane jaggery?

seg.ec48010dffbe.src: Yes. Grate the cane jaggery (cheruku bellam) finely and use the same amount as palm jaggery. The laddus turn lighter in colour, with a milder, caramel-like sweetness.
seg.ec48010dffbe.t: ᱮᱦᱚᱸ᱾ ᱟᱸᱠ ᱜᱩᱲ (ᱪᱮᱨᱩᱠᱩ ᱵᱮᱞᱞᱟᱢ) ᱵᱟᱨᱤᱠ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱞᱮᱠᱟ ᱚᱛᱠᱮ ᱜᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱞᱟᱰᱰᱩ ᱦᱟᱞᱠᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ, ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱦᱟᱞᱠᱟ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱮᱨᱟᱢᱮᱞ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ᱾
seg.ec48010dffbe.back: Yes. Grate the sugarcane jaggery (cheruku bellam) finely and add the same amount as palm jaggery. The laddus become light in colour, the sweetness light and caramel-like.

seg.767f9e16fa95.src: Raw garlic: skip warming the garlic for a sharper taste; keep it in the fridge and eat it within 3 days.
seg.767f9e16fa95.t: ᱠᱟᱸᱪᱟ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ: ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱥᱣᱟᱫ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱟᱞᱚᱢ ᱞᱚᱞᱚᱭᱟ; ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ 3 ᱢᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.767f9e16fa95.back: Raw garlic: for a sharp flavour do not heat the garlic; keep in the fridge and eat within 3 days.

seg.8665687f81ce.src: Keep in a clean, dry, airtight jar in the fridge and use it within 2 weeks. Always use a dry spoon.
seg.8665687f81ce.t: ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ, ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ, ᱦᱚᱭ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱡᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ 2 ᱦᱟᱯᱛᱟ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱵᱮᱵᱷᱟᱨ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱡᱟᱣᱜᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱵᱮᱵᱷᱟᱨ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.8665687f81ce.back: Keep in a clean, dry, airtight jar in the fridge and use within 2 weeks. Always use a dry spoon.

seg.367798df40e3.src: Up to 2 weeks in a dry, airtight jar in the fridge. Dry the garlic well and warm it in oil first, and always use a dry spoon.
seg.367798df40e3.t: ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ, ᱦᱚᱭ ᱵᱚᱸᱫ ᱡᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱯᱷᱨᱤᱡᱽ ᱨᱮ 2 ᱦᱟᱯᱛᱟ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ᱾ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱵᱮᱥ ᱛᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱢᱟᱲᱟᱝ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱢᱮ, ᱟᱨ ᱡᱟᱣᱜᱮ ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱵᱮᱵᱷᱟᱨ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.367798df40e3.back: In a dry, airtight jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks. Dry the garlic well and heat it in oil first, and always use a dry spoon.

seg.1d41be2d17f9.src: Yes. Roast about 20 dried red chillies in a few drops of oil until crisp, cool and grind them before adding the garlic.
seg.1d41be2d17f9.t: ᱮᱦᱚᱸ᱾ ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 20 ᱨᱚᱦᱚᱲ ᱟᱨᱟᱜ ᱢᱟᱨᱤᱪ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱴᱚᱯᱟ ᱥᱩᱱᱩᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱟᱲᱟᱢ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱞᱟᱞᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱨᱟᱥᱩᱱ ᱮᱢ ᱞᱟᱦᱟ ᱯᱤᱥᱟᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.1d41be2d17f9.back: Yes. Fry about 20 dried red chillies in a few drops of oil until crisp, cool, and grind before adding the garlic.

seg.6a0d4200f978.t: ᱵᱮᱞᱞᱟᱢ ᱟᱴᱩᱠᱩᱞᱩ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱠᱟᱨᱰ

seg.5e2064c58b7d.t: ᱠᱚᱵᱵᱟᱨᱤ ᱩᱱᱫᱟᱞᱩ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ ᱠᱟᱨᱰ

seg.c473a3556357.t: ᱟᱱᱫᱷᱨᱚ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱡᱚᱢᱟᱜ · 2 ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ · 10 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ
seg.c473a3556357.back: Sweet food of Andhra · for 2 people · 10 minutes

seg.7099f7c35107.src: Bellam Atukulu ⟦1⟧(Sweet Poha with Palm Jaggery)⟦/1⟧
seg.7099f7c35107.t: ᱵᱮᱞᱞᱟᱢ ᱟᱴᱩᱠᱩᱞᱩ ⟦1⟧(ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱪᱩᱲᱟ)⟦/1⟧
seg.7099f7c35107.back: Bellam Atukulu ⟦1⟧(sweet chura with palm jaggery)⟦/1⟧

seg.b6b19d4f12bb.back: ⟦#1⟧ · ⟦#2⟧ · Bellam Atukulu · gur wale pohe (Hindi words in Ol Chiki)

seg.c9c11f5b43da.src: Bellam atukulu is the 10-minute sweet of Telugu homes. It is the poha offered to Krishna on Krishnashtami, recalling Kuchela's gift, and it is also a quick sweet for children after school. The poha is only rinsed, never cooked in water, and then tossed in warm jaggery syrup.
seg.c9c11f5b43da.t: ᱵᱮᱞᱞᱟᱢ ᱟᱴᱩᱠᱩᱞᱩ ᱫᱚ ᱛᱮᱞᱩᱜᱩ ᱚᱲᱟᱜ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ 10 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱡᱚᱢᱟᱜ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ᱾ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱫᱚ ᱠᱨᱤᱥᱱᱟᱥᱴᱚᱢᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱨᱤᱥᱱᱚ ᱴᱷᱮᱱ ᱮᱢ ᱪᱩᱲᱟ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ, ᱚᱱᱟ ᱫᱚ ᱠᱩᱪᱮᱞᱟ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱡᱤᱱᱤᱥ ᱩᱭᱦᱟᱹᱨ ᱦᱚᱪᱚᱭᱟ, ᱟᱨ ᱤᱥᱠᱩᱞ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱦᱤᱡᱩᱜ ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱜᱤᱫᱽᱨᱟᱹ ᱠᱚ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱞᱚᱜᱚᱱ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱡᱚᱢᱟᱜ ᱦᱚᱸ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ᱾ ᱪᱩᱲᱟ ᱫᱚ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱛᱮ ᱟᱹᱨᱩ ᱜᱮ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ, ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚ ᱪᱮᱫ ᱵᱮᱞᱟ ᱦᱚᱸ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱤᱥᱤᱱᱚᱜᱼᱟ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱨᱟᱥᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.c9c11f5b43da.back: Bellam atukulu is a 10-minute sweet food of Telugu homes. This is the chura given to Krishna on Krishnashtami, it brings to memory Kuchela's gift item, and it is also a quickly-made sweet food for children after coming from school. The chura is only washed with water, in water it is not cooked at any time, then it is stirred into warm jaggery syrup.

seg.8594fedb25dc.src: Our Thati Bellam palm jaggery gives it a deep brown colour and a rich, slightly smoky sweetness. This recipe serves 2.
seg.8594fedb25dc.t: ᱟᱞᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱛᱟᱴᱤ ᱵᱮᱞᱞᱟᱢ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱛᱮ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱜᱟᱲᱦᱟ ᱵᱟᱫᱟᱢᱤ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱟᱨ ᱜᱟᱲᱦᱟ, ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱫᱷᱩᱸᱣᱟᱹ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱱ ᱦᱮᱲᱮᱢ ᱮᱢᱚᱜᱼᱟ᱾ ᱱᱚᱶᱟ ᱵᱮᱱᱟᱣ ᱦᱚᱨᱟ 2 ᱦᱚᱲ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱠᱟᱱᱟ᱾
seg.8594fedb25dc.back: Our thati bellam palm jaggery gives this a deep brown colour and a deep, slight smoke-like sweetness. This making-method is for 2 people.

seg.25e28614accb.src: Prep includes 5 minutes for the rinsed poha to soften.
seg.25e28614accb.t: ᱛᱮᱭᱟᱨ ᱨᱮ ᱟᱹᱨᱩ ᱪᱩᱲᱟ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 5 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱥᱮᱞᱮᱫ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.25e28614accb.back: Preparation includes 5 minutes for softening the washed chura.

seg.b9dedcd705aa.src: Soften thick poha, toss it in warm palm jaggery syrup with coconut and cardamom, and finish with ghee.
seg.b9dedcd705aa.t: ᱢᱚᱴᱟ ᱪᱩᱲᱟ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱢᱮ, ᱱᱟᱨᱤᱭᱟᱞ ᱟᱨ ᱮᱞᱟᱭᱪᱤ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱨᱟᱥᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ, ᱟᱨ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱛᱮ ᱯᱩᱨᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.b9dedcd705aa.back: Soften the thick chura, stir it into warm palm-jaggery syrup with coconut and cardamom, and finish with ghee.

seg.e13864ccb71f.src: ½ cup grated palm jaggery ⟦1⟧about 90 g⟦/1⟧
seg.e13864ccb71f.t: ½ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ⟦1⟧ᱢᱚᱴᱟᱢᱩᱴᱤ 90 g⟦/1⟧
seg.e13864ccb71f.back: ½ cup grated palm jaggery ⟦1⟧about 90 g⟦/1⟧

seg.b78c520dca8d.src: ½ cup grated coconut ⟦1⟧white part only⟦/1⟧
seg.b78c520dca8d.t: ½ ᱠᱟᱯ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ ᱱᱟᱨᱤᱭᱟᱞ ⟦1⟧ᱯᱩᱸᱰ ᱦᱟᱹᱴᱤᱧ ᱜᱮ⟦/1⟧
seg.b78c520dca8d.back: ½ cup grated coconut ⟦1⟧white part only⟦/1⟧

seg.2d6d2ff14f71.src: ¼ tsp cardamom powder ⟦1⟧or the crushed seeds of 2–3 pods⟦/1⟧
seg.2d6d2ff14f71.t: ¼ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱮᱞᱟᱭᱪᱤ ᱦᱚᱞᱚᱝ ⟦1⟧ᱥᱮ 2–3 ᱮᱞᱟᱭᱪᱤ ᱵᱷᱤᱛᱤᱨ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱡᱚ, ᱫᱟᱞ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱨᱟᱹᱯᱩᱫ ᱟᱠᱟᱱ⟦/1⟧
seg.2d6d2ff14f71.back: ¼ small spoon cardamom powder ⟦1⟧or the seeds inside 2–3 cardamoms, pounded and crushed⟦/1⟧

seg.5f1854fd1277.t: 6–8 ᱠᱟᱡᱩ, ᱢᱚᱱ ᱞᱮᱠᱟᱛᱮ ⟦1⟧ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ⟦/1⟧
seg.5f1854fd1277.back: 6–8 cashews, as you like ⟦1⟧fried in ghee until gold colour⟦/1⟧

seg.fbe7b4b8afbc.src: Put the poha in a sieve and pick out any bits of husk.
seg.fbe7b4b8afbc.t: ᱪᱩᱲᱟ ᱪᱷᱟᱸᱠᱱᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱡᱟᱦᱟᱸ ᱦᱚᱸ ᱛᱩᱥ ᱴᱩᱠᱨᱟᱹ ᱢᱮᱱᱟᱜ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱵᱟᱪᱷᱟᱣ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱚᱪᱚᱜ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.fbe7b4b8afbc.back: Keep the chura in a sieve and if there are any husk pieces, pick and remove them.

seg.b0f730c0b062.src: Rinse the poha in a sieve under running water for a few seconds, drain, and leave it for 5 minutes to soften. It should feel soft when pressed, but not wet.
seg.b0f730c0b062.t: ᱪᱷᱟᱸᱠᱱᱤ ᱨᱮ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱥᱮᱱᱚᱜ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱚᱭᱮᱠ ᱥᱮᱠᱮᱱᱰ ᱪᱩᱲᱟ ᱟᱹᱨᱩ ᱢᱮ, ᱫᱟᱜ ᱴᱟᱯᱟᱜ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ, ᱟᱨ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ 5 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱫᱚᱦᱚ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱪᱟᱯᱟᱹᱣ ᱞᱮᱱᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱞᱚᱢᱚᱴ ᱵᱩᱡᱷᱟᱹᱣ ᱞᱟᱹᱠᱛᱤᱭᱟ, ᱢᱮᱱᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱞᱟᱞᱟ ᱫᱚ ᱵᱟᱝ᱾
seg.b0f730c0b062.back: Keeping it in the sieve, wash the chura for a few seconds in flowing water, let the water drip, and keep it 5 minutes to soften. When pressed it should feel soft, but not watery.

seg.0a3e2261d7bc.src: Grate the palm jaggery finely, breaking up any hard lumps.
seg.0a3e2261d7bc.t: ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ ᱵᱟᱨᱤᱠ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱜᱽᱨᱮᱴ ᱢᱮ, ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱫᱤᱞᱟ ᱠᱚ ᱨᱟᱹᱯᱩᱫ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ᱾
seg.0a3e2261d7bc.back: Grate the palm jaggery finely, breaking the hard lumps.

seg.d2b892bf70af.src: Melt the palm jaggery with 2 tbsp water on a low flame, then strain it. Wipe the pan and pour the syrup back in.
seg.d2b892bf70af.t: ᱛᱟᱞᱮ ᱜᱩᱲ 2 ᱢᱟᱨᱟᱝ ᱪᱟᱢᱚᱪ ᱫᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ ᱞᱤᱞᱤ ᱢᱮ, ᱛᱟᱭᱚᱢ ᱪᱷᱟᱸᱠ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱡᱩᱥ ᱠᱟᱛᱮ ᱥᱟᱯᱷᱟ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱨᱟᱥᱟ ᱫᱩᱦᱲᱟᱹ ᱚᱱᱰᱮ ᱞᱩᱴᱩᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.d2b892bf70af.back: Melt the palm jaggery with 2 big spoons of water on a small fire, then strain. Wipe the pan clean and pour the syrup back there.

seg.d073ead78aef.src: If you are using cashews, fry them in a little ghee till golden.
seg.d073ead78aef.t: ᱡᱩᱫᱤ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱮᱢ ᱠᱷᱟᱱ, ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱨᱮ ᱥᱚᱱᱟ ᱨᱚᱝ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ ᱵᱷᱟᱹᱡᱤ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.d073ead78aef.back: If adding cashews, fry them in a little ghee until gold colour.

seg.62c17a0f01a5.src: Add the poha, coconut and cardamom to the warm syrup and toss gently on a low flame for 1–2 minutes, until every flake is coated. Use a light hand so the flakes do not break.
seg.62c17a0f01a5.t: ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱨᱟᱥᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱪᱩᱲᱟ, ᱱᱟᱨᱤᱭᱟᱞ ᱟᱨ ᱮᱞᱟᱭᱪᱤ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ ᱟᱨ ᱦᱩᱰᱤᱧ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱨᱮ 1–2 ᱢᱤᱱᱤᱴ ᱞᱟᱦᱟᱣ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ, ᱡᱚᱛᱚ ᱪᱩᱲᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱨᱟᱥᱟ ᱞᱟᱜᱟᱣ ᱦᱟᱹᱵᱤᱡ᱾ ᱪᱩᱲᱟ ᱵᱟᱝ ᱨᱟᱹᱯᱩᱫ ᱞᱟᱹᱜᱤᱫ ᱦᱟᱞᱠᱟᱹ ᱛᱤ ᱛᱮ ᱜᱷᱟᱱᱴᱟ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.62c17a0f01a5.back: Add chura, coconut and cardamom to the warm syrup and stir slowly on a small fire for 1–2 minutes, until syrup coats all the chura. Stir with a light hand so the chura does not break.

seg.d1abe3d7557d.src: Take the pan off the heat as soon as the flakes are coated; longer cooking makes them chewy.
seg.d1abe3d7557d.t: ᱪᱩᱲᱟ ᱨᱮ ᱨᱟᱥᱟ ᱞᱟᱜᱟᱣ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱥᱟᱶ ᱯᱮᱱ ᱥᱮᱸᱜᱮᱞ ᱠᱷᱚᱱ ᱟᱲᱟᱜ ᱢᱮ; ᱡᱟᱹᱥᱛᱤ ᱤᱥᱤᱱ ᱞᱮᱱᱠᱷᱟᱱ ᱡᱚᱢ ᱨᱮ ᱠᱮᱴᱮᱡ ᱦᱩᱭᱩᱜᱼᱟ᱾
seg.d1abe3d7557d.back: As soon as syrup coats the chura, remove the pan from the fire; if cooked too long it becomes hard to eat.

seg.c91ffab6359d.src: Finish with the ghee and cashews. Serve warm or at room temperature.
seg.c91ffab6359d.t: ᱜᱷᱤᱣ ᱟᱨ ᱠᱟᱡᱩ ᱛᱮ ᱯᱩᱨᱟᱹᱣ ᱢᱮ᱾ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱥᱮ ᱠᱚᱴᱷᱨᱤ ᱨᱮᱭᱟᱜ ᱥᱟᱫᱷᱟᱨᱚᱱ ᱞᱚᱞᱚ ᱨᱮ ᱮᱢ ᱢᱮ᱾
seg.c91ffab6359d.back: Finish with ghee and cashews. Give warm or at the normal warmth of the room.

seg.544ea222a497.src: Use thick poha. Thin poha turns mushy in the syrup.
